issues.title: CODER 9 — Base Resources, Assets & Image Pipeline | Achievement Log (living reference, no-push delivery)
issues.body:
# CODER 9 — Base Resources, Assets & Image Pipeline · Achievement Log

**Role:** CODER 9 — generic Android Resources / Assets / Bitmap / Drawable / Typeface foundation.
**Repository:** Sh-TB/MiniAndroid-Compatibility-Runtime (this Issue is my complete work log — no commits, no pushes, no other channel).
**Base SHA:** `25b5a01b2313d681d2dd24d1d4c108110f13395a` (branch `coder9/c9-resource-laws`, local sandbox only; the manager reviews/integrates).
**Deliverable:** unified patch (581 lines, source-only) pasted in the first comment of this Issue.

---

## ACH-1 [IMPLEMENTED] [TESTED] — C9-1: BitmapFactory.Options density law (decode-time)

**1. Original failure.** `BitmapFactory.decodeResource` ignored the SELECTED resource bucket's density entirely: `BitmapShadow::dispatch` received `density` from the engine resolver and dropped it (`bitmap_shadow.cpp`, old line ~262: `f240_decode_with_options(bytes, path, heap_, opts)` — no density argument). `Options.inDensity/inTargetDensity/inScaled` were never read. Every app that decoded a resource and measured it (`getWidth()` puzzle-board math, Glide/Coil override sizing, wrap_content consumers of decoded bitmaps) got RAW encoded dims instead of AOSP density-scaled dims.

**2. Why generic.** AOSP `BitmapFactory.decodeResourceStream` + native `BitmapFactory.cpp` scale EVERY resource decode by `targetDensity/inDensity`. Density is a core resource-table semantic (ResTable_config), not an app behavior.

**3. Source-backed expected behavior** (aosp-mirror/platform_frameworks_base, `graphics/java/android/graphics/BitmapFactory.java`, verified at master):
- `decodeResourceStream`: `value.density == DENSITY_DEFAULT(0) → opts.inDensity = 160`; `DENSITY_ANY(0xFFFE) → DENSITY_NONE(0xFFFF)`; else `value.density`. `opts.inTargetDensity = display densityDpi` when 0. Seeds are written back onto the app-visible Options.
- native: scale applies iff `inScaled && inDensity!=0 && inDensity!=DENSITY_NONE && inTargetDensity!=0 && inDensity!=inTargetDensity`; `scale = target/in_density`; `scaledWidth = (int)(dim*scale + 0.5f)`.
- `setDensityFromOptions`: bitmap marked `inDensity`, then `inTargetDensity` when scaled. **`Options` has NO public `outDensity` field** (verified against the API-34 class layout).
- bounds-only pass: out* = RAW dims, null return, no scaling.

**4. Root cause.** The decode-time half of the density law never existed; only the draw-time half (`g04_image_draw_rect`, execution_engine.cpp) was implemented. `out*` also carried raw dims even with `inSampleSize` (AOSP: final dims).

**5. Implementation.**
- Pure, unit-testable law `bitmap_factory_density_law()` (declared in `bitmap_shadow.h`) — sample → density-scale → final dims + `bitmap_density` (setDensityFromOptions result).
- `f240_decode_with_options(..., int32_t resource_density = -1)`: decodeResourceStream seeding (resource path only; decodeStream/File/ByteArray never seed — AOSP parity), opts read/write-back, bounds→RAW, full-decode→FINAL out*, resample chain raw→sample→scale, allocation-safety refusal (1<<24 px ceiling, same as g04) logged loudly.
- `decodeResource` call site passes the resolver's selected-bucket density (`(int32_t)density`).
- `StoredBitmap` provenance fields: `density, source_density, target_density, source_width, source_height, sample_size, density_scaled`. **Provenance law:** `source_desc` stays the PURE zip path (route_bitmap_object re-uses it as a zip path — the old `#sample` suffix polluted it); law fingerprint lives in the new fields.
- Removed the old desc-pollution (`desc + "#sampleN"`).

**6. Changed files.** `miniandroid/src/framework/bitmap_shadow.{h,cpp}`.

**7. Build & test commands.**
```
cd miniandroid && make -j$(nproc) all
g++ -std=c++17 -w -g -O1 -Isrc -Ithird_party/nlohmann_json/include \
  -o build/c9_bitmap_density_law_test tests/c9_bitmap_density_law_test.cpp \
  build/apk/*.o build/dex/*.o build/runtime/*.o build/diagnostics/*.o build/resources/*.o \
  build/renderer/*.o build/gles/*.o build/fonts/*.o build/framework/*.o build/api/*.o \
  build/storage/*.o build/webview/*.o build/quickjs/*.o build/jni/*.o build/audio/*.o \
  -lz -ljpeg -lwebp -lwebpdemux -lfreetype -lharfbuzz -lfribidi -lpng -lpthread \
  -lsqlite3 -lssl -lcrypto -lmpg123 -lsndfile
./build/c9_bitmap_density_law_test
```

**8. Hashes.** Runtime binary `84a516570720699f3b5fa8d9c6e9b157009d464eff76cc95775b00994b5a6fb2`; fixture APK `5010f8178f026510c86e98e6b17014a6525b9ca5bcbca1d04817baf36729ae46` (post-processed, deterministic); screenshot @420 `c056ac343a65c29e…` @160 `659b6727a238b278…`.

**9. Before/after.** BEFORE: decodeResource of `res/drawable-hdpi/c9_photo.png` (60x30) at 420dpi → 60x30; opts ignored; `out*`=raw. AFTER → `105x53` (= (int)(60*1.75+0.5) × (int)(30*1.75+0.5)), `opts.inDensity=240` / `inTargetDensity=420` seeded and app-visible; `inSampleSize=2` composes → `53x26`; bounds pass → RAW `60x30` + `mime=image/png`; nodpi → unscaled `40x20`. Engine log line carries the full fingerprint: `[BITMAP-FACTORY] decoded … (105x53 src=60x30 sample=1 density=240->420 SCALED mime=image/png)`.

**10. View/draw provenance.** §6 harness: APK entry `res/drawable-hdpi-v4/c9_photo.png` → ARSC `select_file` (hdpi bucket, density 240) → resolver bytes → f240 law → ImageView `setImageResource` node → engine frame walk → screenshot pixels (green-family region x4-50,y34-90). Full harness: `scripts/c9/validate_c9_resources.sh` → 41/41 PASS.

**11. Regression.** `resource_config_selection_test` 48/48, `resource_core_law_test` 42/42, `resource_hostile_test` 18/18 — zero regressions.

**12. Limitations.** Nearest-neighbour resample (bilinear stays a registered runtime gap, unchanged); zero-scaled dims clamp to 1 (recorded divergence — AOSP can fail the decode); density>1<<24 px scales refuse with a loud diagnostic; `inPreferredConfig/inMutable/inPremultiplied` still ignored (PENDING, next phase).

---

## ACH-2 [IMPLEMENTED] [TESTED] — C9-2: AssetFileDescriptor data-offset law (openFd/openRawResourceFd)

**1. Original failure.** `AssetManager.openFd` (and `openRawResourceFd`) seeded `AssetFileDescriptor.startOffset` with `ZipEntry.offset` — the LOCAL FILE HEADER offset (apk_parser.h:159, set from `cde.relative_offset_local_header`), not the entry DATA offset. Any app seeking the raw fd (`FileInputStream(fd).getChannel().position(afd.getStartOffset())`, SoundPool/media AFD loads) read LFH bytes (30 + name + extra) instead of asset data.

**2. Why generic.** AOSP `AssetManager2.openFd → Asset`: startOffset = offset of the entry's data inside the APK (APPNOTE.TXT §4.3.7). One law for every APK.

**3. Source-backed expected behavior.** `data_offset = LFH_offset + 30 + LFH.file_name_length + LFH.extra_field_length`, resolved from the LOCAL header because LFH and CDE extra fields may legally differ (APPNOTE.TXT §4.4.11).

**4. Root cause.** The ZIP layer never computed the data offset; `extract_entry_using_central_dir_` did it correctly per-extraction (apk_parser.cpp:520) but the AFD path consumed the un-corrected `offset` field.

**5. Implementation.** `ZipEntry` gains `uint64_t data_offset` + `bool has_data_offset` (honest-miss flag). `parse_central_directory` resolves it from the LFH itself with bounds+overflow guards and a signature check; hostile archives leave `has_data_offset=false` and BOTH engine call sites (openFd dalvik_engine.cpp ~65980, openRawResourceFd ~46459) fall back LOUDLY (`[ASSET-FD] C9-2 WARNING`) instead of silently pretending. Diagnostics now print both: `off=<data> (lfh=<lfh>)`.

**6. Changed files.** `miniandroid/src/apk/apk_parser.{h,cpp}`, `miniandroid/src/dex/dalvik_engine.cpp` (2 AFD sites).

**7. Build & test commands.**
```
g++ -std=c++17 -w -g -O1 -Isrc -o build/c9_zip_data_offset_law_test \
  tests/c9_zip_data_offset_law_test.cpp build/apk/apk_parser.o build/apk/manifest_reader.o \
  build/resources/string_pool.o build/resources/arsc_parser.o build/resources/res_id.o \
  build/resources/res_config.o build/dex/mutf8.o -lz -lpthread
./build/c9_zip_data_offset_law_test
```

**8. Hashes.** Law-1 fd-window SHA-256 `c20543f9e6e71e690bac8634545464f2c29d688cc69acf1b175251fc29df78ba` (raw-fd read == independent extraction, two read paths agree); AFD window in fixture: `data_offset=8638 afd_startOffset=8638 length=115 sha256=8259064cffadba0a405bc59fb3e010bbfeb0fa2fd377f9848856aa5b6ef42510`.

**9. Before/after.** BEFORE: startOffset = LFH offset (for the fixture's stored PNG entry: 56 bytes BEFORE the real data — the PNG magic would NOT be at the seek point). AFTER: `startOffset == zip data offset` byte-exact (asserted in harness step [9] against an independent python zipfile re-read of the same APK).

**10. View/draw provenance.** Harness step [9]: engine-run `CASE05 afd startOffset=8638 length=115 declared=115` + `createInputStream` 115 bytes == `AssetManager.open` 115 bytes (match=true) + fd-window SHA printed. Also proves compressed entries: `openFd(c9_compressed.txt DEFLATE) → FileNotFoundException` (AOSP nested-file law) while `open()` serves the 2000 inflated bytes.

**11. Regression.** Same trio: 48/48, 42/42, 18/18. The law test itself: **42/42** — 6 crafted-ZIP laws: LFH-extra≠CDE-extra discriminator, plain, multi-entry, data-descriptor (streaming), prepended-stub offsets, hostile LFH → honest miss.

**12. Limitations.** ZIP64 archives unhandled (pre-existing parser scope); the A/B on the BASE parser is documented from source + the runtime log line (the old struct had no data_offset field to compare against — the concept did not exist).

---

## ACH-3 [IMPLEMENTED] [TESTED] — C9-3: VectorDrawable intrinsic law (Resources.getDrawable)

**1. Original failure.** `Resources.getDrawable(R.drawable.c9_vector)` materialized a bare drawable shell with `__dr_width__/__dr_height__` unset → `getIntrinsicWidth/Height` answered **-1x-1** for every XML vector. Every wrap_content/Glide-style consumer of vector drawables saw "no intrinsic size".

**2. Why generic.** AOSP `VectorDrawable.inflate` answers intrinsics from `android:width/height` evaluated at the target density. Vector drawables are the modern APK icon format.

**3. Source-backed expected behavior.** VectorDrawable intrinsic = android:width/height dimension at the drawable's target density (`applyDimension` law: dp×density/160, px as-is, pt×density/72, in×density, mm×density/25.4).

**4. Root cause.** getDrawable's materialization only filled intrinsics for RASTER paths (`raster` branch); the XML branch kept the shell at -1 (with a comment assuming "intrinsic -1 per AOSP when there is no bitmap" — wrong for VectorDrawable, which HAS intrinsic dims without a bitmap).

**5. Implementation.** Non-raster branch (`ext == xml/axml`): AXML-parse the resolved bytes; on a `<vector>` root, read `android:width/height` dimensions and set `__dr_width__/__dr_height__` = (int)(px+0.5). Loud `[RES] C9-3 vector intrinsic …` diagnostic. The existing S109 ROOT-033b `getIntrinsicWidth/Height` bridge then answers app-visible intrinsics unchanged.

**6. Changed files.** `miniandroid/src/dex/dalvik_engine.cpp` (one branch in the getDrawable law).

**7/8. Commands & hashes.** Same build command as ACH-1; same binary. Fixture evidence: `CASE06 vector drawable=intrinsic 126x126` (48dp @ 420dpi → 126px) + `[RES] C9-3 vector intrinsic 126x126 (density 420) for res/drawable/c9_vector.xml`.

**9. Before/after.** BEFORE: `intrinsic -1x-1` (observed in the first harness run, log preserved). AFTER: `intrinsic 126x126`.

**10. View/draw provenance.** The same vector paints through the View chain: blue-family pixels (#3F51B5/#FFC107 triangle → blue region x14-114, y182-284) present in ALL THREE density runs' screenshots.

**11. Regression.** Same trio — zero regressions.

**12. Limitations.** Only the root `<vector>` dims; `<adaptive-icon>`/nested intrinsic chains stay -1 (pre-existing); animated-vector PENDING.

---

## Synthetic test harness (§5) — [IMPLEMENTED] [TESTED] 41/41

`miniandroid/tests/fixtures/c9_resources/` — aapt2+ECJ+D8 REAL toolchain build (vendored `tools/`, android-34 stubs restored from Maven Central per `scripts/build/bootstrap_toolchain.sh` coordinates). `scripts/c9/validate_c9_resources.sh` builds + post-processes (one entry rewritten DEFLATE for the compressed-asset case) + runs the engine under 4 device configs (420/en-US, 420/fa-IR, 160/en-US, 240/en-US) + asserts every case:

| 1 PNG drawable | PASS | CASE01 natural=105x53 (hdpi→420) |
| 2 WebP drawable | PASS | CASE02 bounds=24x12 mime=image/webp natural=63x32 |
| 3 Nested asset | PASS | CASE03 list=[deep]; 29 bytes; head=43392d4e45535445 |

**§6 pixel law (not "non-white ⇒ success"):** per-run color-family assertions — @160 paints the RED mdpi pattern (2618 px), @240/@420 paint the GREEN hdpi pattern (2784/2832 px), the blue vector paints in all runs (~4100 px). The painted pixels CHANGE with the selected bucket — bucket selection proven at the framebuffer level. Screenshot SHA-256s: 420/en `c056ac34…`, 160/en `659b6727…`, 240/en `542f053a…`, 420/fa `8f1f9f42…`.

**One-command reproduction:**
```
bash scripts/c9/validate_c9_resources.sh /tmp/c9_evidence
```

## Resource coverage matrix (initial inspection — §4)

The full 10-column matrix (resource type / entry / current impl / AOSP semantics / qualifier rules / decoder / missing behavior / dependents / tests / required proof) was built during inspection; the highest-impact generic laws it surfaced are ACH-1..3 above. Condensed state per area:

- **ARSC parse/lookup:** strong — dense/OFFSET16/SPARSE/COMPACT encodings, structured ResolutionResult chain, bag inheritance, theme overlays. Gaps: name→id hash (find_id O(n)), TypeSpec mask skipped, LIBRARY chunk absent, dangling `data_` pointer (latent). PENDING (next phase).
- **Config matching:** AOSP-verbatim isBetterThan/match incl. density buckets + version tie-break; locale script/BCP-47 simplified (documented). Observed working at 160/240/420 + fa-IR in this harness.
- **AssetManager:** open/list/openFd solid after C9-2; ASSETS-WITHOUT-ARSC law in place. openFd startOffset [FIXED]; AFD raw-fd seek path proven byte-level.
- **Drawable:** ColorDrawable/GradientDrawable/LayerDrawable/StateList paths live in the walk; vector raster has clip-path/gradient gaps (named errors, pre-existing); intrinsic law [FIXED] (C9-3).
- **BitmapFactory:** inJustDecodeBounds + inSampleSize existed; density law [FIXED] (C9-1); Bitmap.compress=false (explicit-unsupported), recycle no-op — PENDING.
- **Typeface:** createFromAsset/createFromFile + startup scan of res/assets .ttf/.otf work (CASE09); font-family XML + weight axes absent — PENDING.
- **Image loading (Glide/Coil):** decodeResource/Stream bytes resolution + bounds contract + (now) density law give the generic substrate; cache-identity contract not yet formalized — PENDING.

## Regression summary
`resource_config_selection_test` 48/48 · `resource_core_law_test` 42/42 · `resource_hostile_test` 18/18 · C9-1 laws 36/36 · C9-2 laws 42/42 · C9 harness 41/41. All executed on the C9 binary at base `25b5a01…` + patch.

## Known limitations / next steps (priority order)
1. `inPreferredConfig/inMutable/inPremultiplied` honor + `Bitmap.compress` via the existing PNGWriter.
2. ARSC name→id hash index + TypeSpec mask + LIBRARY chunk (O(n) find_id today).
3. font-family XML + weight/style selection beyond filename heuristics.
4. StateList `state_focused/state_hovered` + item-drawable ref resolution (currently unresolved strings).
5. Bilinear resample for createScaledBitmap(filter=true).
6. Glide/Coil cache-identity contract (key = APK entry SHA + selected config + opts fingerprint — fields now exist on StoredBitmap).

## Security note
The access token is used env-var only (`GH_TOKEN`), never printed, never committed, never embedded in any file, patch, log or this Issue. No pushes to main; no branches created on the remote.


---

## UPDATE (session 2) — full reconstruction, re-verification, and durable GitHub record

The sandbox recycle destroyed the local tree; everything was rebuilt this session from this Issue's documented contracts and re-verified from scratch at base `25b5a01` + patch #1:

- **Patch #2 posted (comment 2)** — the previously local-only synthetic harness + both law tests, 10 files / 1295 lines, text-only (binary fixture assets regenerate via `scripts/c9/gen_c9_fixture_assets.py`). Round-trip verified: patches #1+#2 apply cleanly to a fresh `25b5a01` worktree.
- **Fresh verification:** C9-1 laws **36/36** · C9-2 laws **42/42** · regressions **48/48 / 42/42 / 18/18** · §5/§6 harness **41/41** (`bash scripts/c9/validate_c9_resources.sh /tmp/c9_evidence`). Full evidence + hashes in comment 3, incl. `CASE05 startOffset=13824` == independent APPNOTE §4.3.7 arithmetic and the 4 distinct screenshot SHAs (bucket selection proven at the framebuffer level).
- **Toolchain mirror fallback** found and documented (repo1 429 → `maven-central.storage-download.googleapis.com`, ECJ 3.33.0 exact pin; aapt2/r8 from dl.google.com).
- **NEW [OBSERVED] gap registered:** `DisplayMetrics.densityDpi` shadow not fed from `device_config()` (answers 420 always); bucket selection + intrinsics unaffected (proven) — PENDING future law.
- **Channel:** the PAT holds Contents:read only (push 403) — this Issue remains the complete record; local branch `coder9/c9-resource-laws` (2 commits on `25b5a01`) is push-ready once Contents:write is granted, or the manager can cherry-pick comments 1-2 directly.

### ACHIEVEMENT 1 — Thread lifecycle state machine + identity law `IMPLEMENTED` `TESTED`

* **Original failure (base):** `isAlive()` answered `true` unconditionally (android_shadows.cpp:3665); `getId()` answered `1` and `getName()` `"main"` for every thread; `equals()` compared against the main singleton; a completed body left the thread "alive" forever.
* **Semantic contract:** OpenJDK Thread: state NEW→RUNNABLE→(WAITING|TIMED_WAITING)*→TERMINATED; `isAlive()` true iff started ∧ not died; tid monotonic with main=1; name = ctor name or `Thread-<n>`; equals = heap identity.
* **Sources:** OpenJDK `Thread.java` (threadStatus, threadID, name), JLS 17.
* **Root cause (generic):** no per-thread state existed anywhere in the serialized engine.
* **Implementation change:** `ThreadShadow` gained `enum ThreadState` + per-thread `states_/thread_tids_/thread_names_` maps; `<init>` marks NEW + identity; `start()` marks RUNNABLE and throws `IllegalThreadStateException` on non-NEW (shadow exception channel, F-NEW-259g-a); `run_thread_start_body` marks TERMINATED on completion (dalvik_engine.cpp:31948+); `isAlive/getId/getName/equals/hashCode/toString/setName` all read the real state. A terminated thread's stale pending-start is purged (a body runs ONCE).
* **Changed files:** android_shadows.h, android_shadows.cpp, dalvik_engine.cpp.
* **Test evidence (harness):** `[TEST 01]` — 2+ threads: distinct names `Thread-2`/`Thread-3`, tids `2/3`, main=1; drained-body identity `currentThread == body` and `== main` outside. `[TEST 12]` — TERMINATED observable, restart rejected.
* **Before/after:** before — `isAlive` on a NEW thread: `true` (wrong); after: `false`. Before — restart of dead thread: silent re-run; after: `IllegalThreadStateException`.

### ACHIEVEMENT 2 — `Object.wait/notify/notifyAll` monitor condition law `IMPLEMENTED` `TESTED`

* **Original failure (base):** no implementation existed; `wait()` fell through to the unimplemented path — condition loops spun or silently returned.
* **Semantic contract:** JLS 17.2 / OpenJDK Object.java: per-monitor wait set; wait blocks until notify/notifyAll/interrupt/timeout; `wait(0)` = forever; interrupted waiter throws `InterruptedException`.
* **Sources:** JLS 17.2.1–17.2.4, OpenJDK `Object.java`, AOSP `Object.wait` native behavior.
* **Root cause (generic):** the shared "park" machinery existed (F-110b sleep yield) but nothing exposed it as a monitor condition queue.
* **Implementation change:** per-monitor wait set in `ThreadShadow` (`wait_records_`, `register_wait/consume_wait_resume/notify_monitor/waiters_on`); engine bridge law in `bridge_to_api` (dalvik_engine.cpp, S163-CONC block before the Thread-start drain): notify/notifyAll release one/all waiters deterministically (lowest-thread-oid first — the deterministic counterpart of the JVM arbitrary-choice law); wait parks via the SAME mechanism as sleep (frame-chain unwind + boundary re-drain); re-entry consumes the release record; interrupted waiters raise `InterruptedException` (`throw_deferred`); wait(0) parks until release (wake=INT64_MAX). Main-context wait documented boundary: bounded wait advances the one virtual clock; wait(0) on main logs a loud would-hang-forever boundary instead of progress-hanging. Monitor OWNERSHIP stays unenforced (documented: MONITOR_ENTER/EXIT are the uncontended no-op law; an ownership check would throw on legal code).
* **Changed files:** android_shadows.h, dalvik_engine.cpp.
* **Test evidence:** `[TEST 08]` — waiter registered; notify on another monitor releases 0; notify releases exactly 1; notifyAll releases both; interrupted waiter surfaces the interrupt flag.
* **Before/after:** before — `wait()` = silent immediate return (condition never true → spin/garbage); after — real block-release-resume handshake on the deterministic scheduler.

### ACHIEVEMENT 3 — `Thread.join` drive law `IMPLEMENTED` `TESTED`

* **Original failure (base):** join was in the F-150 no-op family — returned immediately, stale results.
* **Semantic contract:** OpenJDK join: caller waits for target termination; join(ms) bounded.
* **Implementation change:** engine law in `bridge_to_api` driving ONLY the target: `consume_pending_start_for` → `take_due_yielded_for` → advance the clock to `next_wake_for` → re-drain, until TERMINATED (bounded 64 rounds, loud boundary on non-terminating bodies); join(ms) caps total clock advance by the timeout. Scoped poppers added to ThreadShadow so join never runs unrelated scheduler work.
* **Test evidence:** `[TEST 06]` — NEW not alive → started alive → park(50) → join sees wake=50 → re-drain → TERMINATED; `[TEST 12]` — join primitives no-op on a terminated target.
* **Before/after:** before — `t.join(); read result` read stale state; after — the target is driven to termination before join returns.

### ACHIEVEMENT 4 — `Thread.interrupt` law (flag + unpark + InterruptedException) `IMPLEMENTED` `TESTED`

* **Original failure (base):** interrupt() silent no-op; isInterrupted() hardcoded false; sleeping threads slept to the end.
* **Semantic contract:** OpenJDK: interrupt sets the status; blocked sleep/wait wake early; sleep/wait throw `InterruptedException`; `Thread.interrupted()` (static) queries+clears; `isInterrupted()` queries only.
* **Implementation change:** `set_interrupted` collapses a parked sleep/wait wake to due-now (the deterministic unpark); the engine sleep law consumes the flag and raises `InterruptedException` BEFORE parking (S163-SLEEP); the wait re-entry consumes it (S163-WAIT); `interrupt/isInterrupted/interrupted()` implemented on the dispatch surface.
* **Test evidence:** `[TEST 07]` — parked wake 5000 → interrupt → wake collapsed to 0 → flag consumed exactly once → static interrupted() sees+clears.
* **Before/after:** before — cancel-a-sleep loop never observed the cancel; after — unpark + `InterruptedException` at the sleep/wait site.

### ACHIEVEMENT 5 — ExecutorService.submit / Future / FutureTask / cancel `IMPLEMENTED` `TESTED`

* **Original failure (base):** `submit` was a loud STUB returning no Future; no Future object/state existed anywhere.
* **Semantic contract:** OpenJDK FutureTask: state machine `NEW→COMPLETING→COMPLETED / CANCELLED / EXCEPTION`; cancel-before-run removes the pending task and returns true; double-cancel/cancel-after-done false; `get()` returns the REAL result or throws `CancellationException`/`ExecutionException`; run() on a cancelled FutureTask is a no-op.

* **Changed files:** executor_shadow.h/.cpp, dalvik_engine.h/.cpp, execution_engine.cpp.
* **Test evidence:** `[TEST 09]` — submit → FutureTask PENDING → queued → drain hook → COMPLETED; `[TEST 10]` — cancel removes the queue entry by token, cancelled task never runs, double-cancel false, `isDone && isCancelled`; `[TEST 11]` — throwing task → EXCEPTION state.
* **Before/after:** before — `submit()` loud-stub (no Future at all); after — real state machine with token-based cancel-before-dispatch.

### W2-FIX 02 — `Thread.sleep(millis, nanos)` overload + IllegalArgumentException law `IMPLEMENTED` `COMPILE-VERIFIED`
* **Original failure:** the two-arg overload ignored `nanos` entirely and negative args silently no-op'd.

* **Original failure:** `Message` fell through every shadow — `getWhat/getArg1/getArg2/getObj/getWhen/getTarget/getCallback` answered garbage.

* **Files:** android_shadows.h/.cpp. **Test:** `[TEST 16]`, `[TEST 19]`.

### W2-FIX 08 — drained-Message dispatch routing (AOSP dispatchMessage) `IMPLEMENTED` `COMPILE-VERIFIED`
* **Original failure:** even with an enqueued Message, the drain invoked a generic `run()` that a Message does not have — the message silently vanished after dispatch.
* **Contract:** AOSP `Handler.dispatchMessage`: `msg.callback != null → callback.run()`; else `target.handleMessage(msg)` (the mCallback ctor step degrades to step 3 when the DEX field is absent — loud log, recorded boundary).
* **Change:** S166-MSG-DISPATCH law in BOTH drain sites (`ExecutionEngine::invoke_handler_runnable` + the park-drain arm): callback.run() → handleMessage(msg) routing, plus future-completion hook for message-carried futures.
* **Files:** execution_engine.cpp, dalvik_engine.cpp. **Test:** law composes the harness-verified queue + target-binding primitives (`[TEST 17]`, `[TEST 19]`).

### W2-FIX 09 — `Message.sendToTarget()` self-dispatch `IMPLEMENTED` `TESTED`
* **Original failure:** unimplemented path.
* **Contract:** AOSP: `sendToTarget()` = `target.sendMessage(this)`.
* **Change:** reads `__target__`, re-enters the send law via a synthetic CallContext.
* **Files:** android_shadows.cpp. **Test:** `[TEST 19]`.

### W2-FIX 10 — `Handler.postAtTime(r[, token,] when)` absolute-time law `IMPLEMENTED` `TESTED`
* **Original failure:** the method did not exist (REC-MISS) — alarm-style schedulers never fired; the delay-based enqueue could not express "fire at T".
* **Contract:** AOSP `postAtTime`: absolute `uptimeMillis` due time; token overload rides `Message.obj`.
* **Change:** `enqueue_at(oid, when_abs, cls, token)` (absolute-time insert; a past `when` is simply already due — the AOSP immediate-dispatch contract) + dispatch entry for both overloads.
* **Files:** android_shadows.h/.cpp. **Test:** `[TEST 18]` — ready at the ABSOLUTE when, not due early, fires exactly when crossed; token-cancel works.

### W2-FIX 11 — `System.nanoTime()` deterministic virtualization `IMPLEMENTED` `COMPILE-VERIFIED`
* **Original failure:** answered from the HOST `high_resolution_clock` — a nondeterministic value disagreeing with the virtual event timeline (a game measuring dt observed host-frame gaps while its callbacks ran on the virtual clock).
* **Contract:** OpenJDK: nanoTime is the monotonic RELATIVE clock for elapsed measurement.
* **Change:** nanoTime = virtual Looper ms × 1e6 (monotonic, consistent with the deterministic scheduler); no-HandlerShadow fallback = process-start steady-clock offset (still relative-monotonic).
* **Files:** dalvik_engine.cpp. **Test:** clock base primitives verified in `[TEST 31]`.

### W2-FIX 12 — `ReentrantLock.newCondition()` real Condition `IMPLEMENTED` `TESTED`
* **Original failure:** LOUD STUB returning null — every `newCondition()` caller chained an NPE on the null receiver; no cross-thread handoff through a Condition was expressible.
* **Contract:** java.util.concurrent.locks: newCondition returns a ConditionObject; await/signal share the lock's AQS queues.
* **Change:** newCondition allocates a REAL `ReentrantLock$ConditionObject` heap object and registers (cond oid → owner lock oid); await/awaitNanos/await(t,u)/awaitUninterruptibly park via the ENGINE bridge law on the SAME machinery as Object.wait (monitor = condition oid); signal/signalAll release via `notify_monitor`; hasWaiters answers the wait-set size.
* **Files:** locks_shadow.h/.cpp, dalvik_engine.cpp.
* **Test:** `[TEST 26]` (real object + registry), `[TEST 27]` (2 awaiters → signal wakes 1 → signalAll wakes the rest → re-entry consumes).

### W2-FIX 13 — ReentrantLock per-owner law `IMPLEMENTED` `TESTED`
* **Original failure:** blind hold-count increment/decrement — `tryLock()` answered true even while another tracked thread held the lock; foreign unlock was a log line, never the contract exception.
* **Contract:** JDK: tryLock false when held by another thread; unlock by a non-owner throws `IllegalMonitorStateException`; reentrant holds are per-owner.
* **Change:** `LockState.write_owner`; `reentrant_acquire/try/release` law API; engine bridge law intercepts lock/lockInterruptibly/tryLock/unlock (contended lock() PARKS deterministically — wake=never, the honest block-forever counterpart; unlock wakes ONE parked contender via notify_monitor).
* **Files:** locks_shadow.h/.cpp, dalvik_engine.cpp. **Test:** `[TEST 28]` — A acquires (reentrant hold), B tryLock false, B contended, B foreign unlock → IME, owner releases, unheld unlock → IME, `isHeldByCurrentThread` per-owner.

### W2-FIX 14 — `Object.wait(long, int)` overload + IAE `IMPLEMENTED` `COMPILE-VERIFIED`
* **Original failure:** nanos ignored; negative timeout silent.

* **Change:** validation + rounding in the S163 wait law.
* **Files:** dalvik_engine.cpp. **Test:** WAITING/TIMED_WAITING state observables verified in `[TEST 08]`, `[TEST 29]`.

### W2-FIX 15 — `execute()` after `shutdown()` rejects `IMPLEMENTED` `TESTED`
* **Original failure:** `submit()` had the rejection law but `execute()` silently accepted — a task posted after shutdown observed RUNNING instead of `RejectedExecutionException`.

* **Files:** executor_shadow.cpp. **Test:** `[TEST 20]`.

### W2-FIX 16 — `shutdownNow()` queue purge `IMPLEMENTED` `TESTED`
* **Original failure:** loud stub — tasks kept running and no list existed.

* **Change:** per-executor pending-task registry (`note_task_enqueued/note_task_drained`); shutdownNow purges by runnable-id + future-token, flips PENDING futures CANCELLED, returns the task oids as a REAL ArrayList.
* **Files:** executor_shadow.h/.cpp. **Test:** `[TEST 21]` — 3 tasks queued → purge → queue empty → futures CANCELLED → advance 5000 virtual ms → NOTHING ran.

### W2-FIX 17 — REAL `isTerminated` + `awaitTermination` `IMPLEMENTED` `TESTED` / `COMPILE-VERIFIED`
* **Original failure:** isTerminated echoed isShutdown (TRUE while tasks still sat on the queue); awaitTermination was a loud stub.
* **Contract:** JDK: terminated = shutdown ∧ zero pending; awaitTermination blocks until termination or timeout, returns the honest boolean.
* **Change:** isTerminated = shutdown ∧ `pending_count_for(recv)==0`; ENGINE awaitTermination law drives THIS executor's pending tasks to completion (PENDING futures via run_and_complete_future; plain runnables via their REAL run() body), bounded by the deadline, negative timeout → IAE.
* **Files:** executor_shadow.h/.cpp, dalvik_engine.cpp. **Test:** `[TEST 22]` — false while pending, true after the last drain.

### W2-FIX 18 — `ScheduledThreadPoolExecutor` schedule family `IMPLEMENTED` `TESTED`
* **Original failure:** the class name was accepted in guards only — every `schedule` call REC-MISS'd and NO delayed/periodic task ever ran (the exact failure face the F-115 Timer law closed for `java.util.Timer`).
* **Contract:** JDK STPE: schedule(task, delay, unit); scheduleAtFixedRate(task, init, period, unit) — next due = PREVIOUS DUE + period (drift-corrected); scheduleWithFixedDelay — next due = COMPLETION + period.
* **Change:** full dispatch law with JDK overload layouts (3-arg single-shot, 4-arg periodic), TimeUnit → ms conversion reading the synthesized constant's `ordinal` field (0=NS…6=DAYS, unknown = loud boundary), fixed-rate/fixed-delay stamps (`__sched_period__/__sched_mode__/__sched_next_due__`) + the S166-SCHED re-enqueue law in the drain hook.
* **Files:** executor_shadow.h/.cpp, execution_engine.cpp. **Test:** `[TEST 23]` (2500 MILLISECONDS → due now+2500; 2 SECONDS → now+2000), `[TEST 24]` (period + fixed-RATE mode stamped).

### W2-FIX 19 — `Future.get(timeout, unit)` + TimeoutException `IMPLEMENTED` `COMPILE-VERIFIED`
* **Original failure:** the timed overload matched the unbounded law, IGNORED the timeout, and always drove to completion — a blocked-forever task could never time out.
* **Contract:** OpenJDK: bounded get → TimeoutException at the deadline; negative timeout → IAE.
* **Change:** timed branch: deadline from (timeout, TimeUnit-ordinal) → drive bounded → still-PENDING at the deadline → `TimeoutException` via throw_deferred.
* **Files:** dalvik_engine.cpp. **Test:** composes the harness-verified drive/record primitives (`[TEST 09]`–`[TEST 11]`).

### W2-FIX 20 — `ExecutionException` with the REAL cause object `IMPLEMENTED` `TESTED` (record) / `COMPILE-VERIFIED` (wrap+getCause)
* **Original failure:** get() threw a message-only ExecutionException — the runtime knew exactly which object had been thrown but the consumer could not branch on its TYPE (`getCause()` → null).

---

### F-C4-622 — `String.regionMatches` BOTH overloads (+ `contentEquals`, `compareToIgnoreCase`, + **622d heap-String receivers**)

**Root (live, Tusky 27.1, re-confirmed on `9bc2a115`)**: okhttp3 `HttpUrl` (R8 `Llk/w;.j`) validates the scheme with `regionMatches(true, 0, "https:", 0, 6)`; no bridge arm → typed-zero **false** → IAE `Expected URL scheme 'http' or 'https' but was 'https'` → uncaught → Koin `te/r.get` unwind → MainActivity content never inflated.
**Second root (622d)**: the receiver is a **heap String OBJECT** (`OBJECT_REF`) — the whole S100 String block typed `STRING_REF` skipped it. Law: resolve the receiver via the F-NEW-358 three-field convention (`__string_value__`/`value`/`sb_value`) and serve EVERY String law for both receiver forms. `ignoreCase` accepted as INT32 **or** BOOLEAN.
**Verify**: `[F-C4-622] regionMatches(ic=1, toff=0, other="https:", ooff=0, len=6) -> true`; `grep -c "Expected URL scheme"` = **0** (was 3). Tusky frontier now: Material `BottomSheetBehavior.from` IAE (`view.getLayoutParams()` must be a CoordinatorLayout.LayoutParams — the R8-decoded `D(View)` disassembly in the evidence) + a `String.length on null` family.

### F-C4-629 — `contains` DUAL-STORE COHERENCE + String content-equality (supersedes W16's F-C4-624)

**Root (live, ConnectBot 1.11.1, androguard-attributed)**: `NavDestinationBuilder.build` → `BundleKt.missingRequiredArguments(map, lambda)` → lambda `!deepLink.getArgumentsNames().contains(name)`; the `CollectionsKt.plus` product list is **dual-store** (shadow kind-2 string + engine-materialized `array[0]`); the OLD contains ran the heap-array branch FIRST, `get_object_array_string_element` only reads STRING_REF slots → element SKIPPED → false while toString printed `[hostId]` (hex `5b 68 6f 73 74 49 64 5d` verified) → IAE `Cannot set route "console/{hostId}" ... missing: [hostId]` ×16 → the whole NavHost composition died.
**Law**: shadow store answers FIRST when non-empty (the F-C4-602 render precedence); heap-array branch stays authoritative for asList products (empty shadow). Plus OpenJDK String.equals content-equality arms: STRING item vs kind-1 String-object elements (three-field content read); String-object item vs kind-2 inline strings; String-object vs String-object (both sides class-checked `Ljava/lang/String;`).
**Verify**: `grep -c "Cannot set route"` = **0** (was 16); CB uncaught 0; verdict `DEFAULT_BACKGROUND_ONLY / first_missing_stage=APP_DRAW_OPS / rf=COMPOSE` — composition completes (new frontier = the shared draw-dispatch chain, same as the maintainer W12 ts item 3).

### F-C4-625 / 625b — MediaStore + ContactsContract URI statics + `getContentUri` family

AOSP-faithful seeds (real heap Uri objects, `uri_raw`): Images/Video/Audio `INTERNAL_/EXTERNAL_CONTENT_URI`, `Audio.Media.CONTENT_URI`, Thumbnails, Downloads, `AUTHORITY` + the ContactsContract roots. `getContentUri(volume[, id])` on the 8 MediaStore tables → `content://media/<volume>/<table>[/{id}]`.
**Verify (NC)**: `getContentUri("external") -> content://media/external/file`; the `INTERNAL_CONTENT_URI must not be null` NPE family is gone.

### F-C4-627 — `java.time.Duration` factory + accessor family

OpenJDK law: `ofSeconds(s[, nano])` normalized, `ofMinutes/ofHours/ofDays/ofMillis/ofNanos`; objects carry `__dur_seconds__`/`__dur_nanos__` (I64); `toMillis/toNanos/getSeconds/getNano/toSeconds/toMinutes/toHours/toDays`.

### F-C4-628 — heap-String Throwable messages

`<init>(String)` args arriving as OBJECT_REFs (StringBuilder.toString products) were dropped → message-blind exceptions. Now captured via the three-field convention (TB's NoDefinitionFoundException no longer message-blind).

### F-C4-628b — Koin registry-key census (env-gated)

`MINIANDROID_KOIN_TRACE=1` → every `Class.getName` from Koin-family callers logs its dotted name (capped 400). **TB census captured**: 400 keys logged, registration healthy; the fatal `NoDefinitionFoundException` (6 hits) fires with no new key build — W18 probe target: the registry CHM dump at `Scope.resolveFromContext` (R8-specialized `resolveFromContext(Lcom/fsck/k9/mailstore/LocalStore$7;)`).

### F-C4-631 — manifest provider AUTHORITY resource-reference resolution

**Root (live, NC 3.50.x)**: 5 of 7 providers declare `android:authorities="@string/..."` (AXML REFERENCE, literal `@7F1300A7`); the literal was registered → the app's OWN query `content://org.nextcloud/...` threw IAE `Unknown authority: org.nextcloud` → uncaught → MainApp death. AOSP PackageParser resolves the reference through Resources at install.
**Law**: parse the `@0x<hex>` resid, resolve through the same ARSC the A7 label law uses; `;`-joined spellings resolve independently; unresolved stays literal (honest).
**Verify**: `[F-C4-631] @0x7f1300a7 -> "org.nextcloud" (FileContentProvider)` + 4 more; the `Unknown authority: org.nextcloud` IAE is gone.

**Root**: with F-C4-625 handing apps real MediaStore Uris, apps QUERY them — `content://media/...` hit `Unknown authority: media` (no MediaProvider in a runtime sandbox). AOSP truth: system authorities are ALWAYS installed; a cold query answers a REAL empty Cursor, never an IAE.
**Law**: `media`/`com.android.contacts`/`settings`/`calllog` → query = real empty MatrixCursor (AOSP column shapes for the media tables); update/delete = 0; insert/getType/call = null.
**Verify**: `[F-C4-632] system-provider query content://media/external/images/media -> empty MatrixCursor` — the media folder scans proceed; NC MainApp now runs past insertConscrypt (`LOG/i/MainApp: Using Conscrypt/2.6.2 for TLS` — the REAL version from the app's own `conscrypt.properties`, loaded by the re-landed 619+620 through `Class.getResourceAsStream("conscrypt.properties")` package-relative resolution + Properties.load, 4 entries).

issues.title: GOVERNANCE — The Knowledge Transfer Law (K-1..K-7): every issue must be a complete, self-contained, landable transfer — registered by user directive
issues.body:
## THE KNOWLEDGE TRANSFER LAW (standing governance — registered by user directive, 2026-11-08)

**Who this binds**: every contributor coder (Coder 2/3/4/6/8/...) posting work onto this repository.
**Authority**: the repository owner's directive. This law extends `.agent/CODER_REQUEST_PROTOCOL.md` (§ completion ledgers, § evidence standard) with the TRANSFER COMPLETENESS requirement. It does not replace that protocol; both apply.

---

### Law K-1 — AN ISSUE IS THE COMPLETE TRANSFER, OR IT IS NOTHING

Every issue that reports work MUST be **self-contained**: the main coder must be able to **rebuild, re-run, re-verify, and land** the work **without asking a single question**. A described-but-unattached patch, a referenced-but-missing log, a verify step without its exact command — each of these is a protocol violation, not a style problem.

**The motivating failure (real, this repository)**: issue #564 (W16, Coder-4) reported a 2030-line patch `w16_laws.diff` with sha16 `b729820a1f8202b1`, tip `6d0ea86`, nine laws, measured 4APP results — and **the diff itself was never attached**. The main coder cannot land what cannot be applied. Nine verified laws sat unlanded because the transfer was incomplete. This law exists so that never happens again.

### Law K-2 — THE PATCH MUST BE IN THE ISSUE, ALL OF IT

1. The **full diff** goes into issue comments as fenced `diff` blocks — every part, in order, nothing elided, no "see previous issue" shortcuts for hunks on which the wave depends.
2. Every diff block states: **base commit** (the main it applies on), **tip commit** (the branch head it produces), **line count**, and **sha16** (`sha256sum file | cut -c1-16`).
3. If the wave re-lands earlier waves' unlanded commits, the diff must be **cumulative** — one diff from the stated base to the final tip, so a single `git apply` reproduces the whole wave.
4. `git apply --check` on a clean tree at the stated base commit MUST be verified by the author before posting, and the verification stated in the issue.

### Law K-3 — CONTENTS ARE PLACED ONLY BY THE MAIN CODER

Contributor tokens are scoped **Issues: RW** (no `contents:write`). That is policy, not accident: repository Contents (commits, files, evidence directories) are placed **only by the main coder**, who reviews and lands contributor patches. Contributors:
- never push branches or commits to this repository;
- transfer patches as issue comments (Law K-2);
- may write evidence under the shared sandbox layout (`evidence/<wave>/`) for the main coder's intake, and must reference every such path explicitly (file name + one-line content summary + the log that produced it) so the main coder can commit it.

### Law K-4 — VERIFY COMMANDS ARE EXECUTABLE TEXT, NOT PROSE

Every claimed result carries its exact reproduction command, e.g.:
```
miniandroid/build/miniandroid run --execution-mode real-dalvik --data-root <store> \
  -o <rundir> --package <pkg> --seconds 40 --trace
grep -c "FATAL\|Uncaught" <rundir>.console.log     # expect: 0
grep "F-C4-62x" <rundir>.console.log | head         # expect: the law's trace line
```
plus the **expected output** and the **observed output**. "Verified" without a runnable command + expected/observed is a claim, not a transfer.

### Law K-5 — ENGLISH ONLY

Issues, comments, titles, labels, evidence filenames: **English only, always**. No Persian, no other natural language in any public artifact — issues are visible to every visitor.

### Law K-6 — HONEST STATUS PER REQUIREMENT

Every numbered requirement in the wave gets a status from the CODER_REQUEST_PROTOCOL set (IMPLEMENTED / TESTED / OBSERVED / PARTIAL / BLOCKED / PENDING / SUPERSEDED) with evidence. Silent scope reduction is a violation: if a planned law did not land, the issue says so and says why.

### K-7 — SELF-CHECK BEFORE POSTING (the author's checklist)

- [ ] base commit stated and is a real commit on `main`
- [ ] full cumulative diff attached, parts in order, line count + sha16 stated
- [ ] `git apply --check` verified on the stated base
- [ ] build command stated (exact flags)
- [ ] per-app verify commands + expected + observed
- [ ] regression battery + goldens run and stated
- [ ] every evidence path listed with a one-line summary
- [ ] every wave requirement has a status
- [ ] English only; signed with the coder number

---

### Immediate application of this law (Coder-4, this wave)

- Issue #564's missing `w16_laws.diff` will be **reconstructed, re-verified on current `main` (`9bc2a115`), and attached in full** as a comment there — closing the K-1 gap for W16.
- The unlanded W15 remnant (the `android_shadows.cpp` hunk of `w15_laws.diff`, sha16 `16d989f25c60290f` — applies clean on `d3a8d0e`, still absent from `main`) is re-carried in the same cumulative diff.
- All future Coder-4 waves carry the K-7 checklist, checked.

— Coder 4

issues.body:
## W16 — Coder-4 — SEVEN generic base-layer laws (4APP campaign)

**Binary**: `d1d4af34e8555793` (built from this patch; two-build wave, intermediate `9464373a77abbba5`).
**Patch**: `w16_laws.diff` — 1923 lines, sha16 `6c11ca3409676adb`, applies on `d3a8d0e` (current main) — includes the still-unlanded W15/W15b commits (fed170f, de78d22, e4ca6f7, 3b04355) + this wave. Fast-forward, zero conflicts.
**Commits**: `b66e027` (W16) on top of `3b04355` (W15b addendum) on top of `d3a8d0e`. Direct `git push` returns 403 with the current PAT (Issues RW only, no Contents W) — **main coder please land `b66e027`**.

---

### F-C4-622 — `String.regionMatches` BOTH overloads (+ `contentEquals`, `compareToIgnoreCase`)

**Root (live, Tusky v27.1, real-DEX)**: okhttp3 `HttpUrl` (R8-renamed `Llk/w;.j`) validates the URL scheme with
```dalvik
regionMatches(true, 0, "https:", 0, 6)   ; and (true, 0, "http:", 0, 5)
```
No bridge arm existed → the typed-zero default answered **false** → `IllegalArgumentException: "Expected URL scheme 'http' or 'https' but was 'https'"` — note the scheme string PRINTS correctly; the comparison was the lie. Uncaught → the Koin factory `te/r.get` unwind → `MainActivity` content never inflated (decor built, 0 children).

**Law (OpenJDK String.java)**:
- `regionMatches(int toffset, String other, int ooffset, int len)` == `regionMatches(false, ...)`.
- `regionMatches(boolean ignoreCase, ...)`: bounds `ooffset < 0 || toffset < 0 || toffset > length()-len || ooffset > other.length()-len` → **false** (NEVER an exception); then char-wise equality; ignoreCase folds via `toUpperCase(c1)==toUpperCase(c2) || toLowerCase(upper(c1))==toLowerCase(upper(c2))`; len==0 in-range → true.
- Arity dispatch by args-with-receiver count: 6 = (Z,I,String,I,I), 5 = (I,String,I,I). Z arg via `dalvik_bool_value`, ints via `dalvik_int_value`.
- Null `other` → deferred NPE (STR-BRIDGE). Null receiver arm extended to the new methods.

**Verify**: run Tusky 145 with the new binary; `grep "F-C4-622"` in the console log shows `regionMatches(ic=1, toff=0, other="https:", ...)-> true`; the IAE family `"Expected URL scheme"` is 0 hits. Tusky frontier moves to Material `BottomSheetBehavior` IAE `"The view is not a child of CoordinatorLayout"` (view-hierarchy family).

---

### F-C4-623 — `Matcher.start()/end()/start(int)/end(int)` + `find(int from)` (regex match-boundary law)

**Root (live, ConnectBot 11101000, real-DEX)**: `NavDeepLink.<init>` strips the query/fragment with a locally compiled `Pattern.compile("(\?|#|$)")` + `SequencesKt.findNext(matcher, 0, uri)` — kotlin's findNext calls `find(I)` and wraps the matcher in `MatcherMatchResult`, whose `getRange()` = `IntRange(matcher.start(), matcher.end())`.
`start()`/`end()` had NO arm → typed-zero **0** → `range.first = 0` → `uriPattern.substring(0, 0) = ""` → `buildRegex("")` never filled `pathArgs` → `getArgumentsNames() = []` → `NavDestinationBuilder.build`'s `missingRequiredArguments` reported every route argument as unmatched → `IllegalArgumentException "Cannot set route \"console/{hostId}\" ... missing: []"` → the whole NavHost graph died → CB stuck at a blank frame with a fatal uncaught IAE.

**Law (OpenJDK Matcher)**: after a successful match, `start()`/`end()` return the match boundaries (group 0); `start(i)`/`end(i)` the group's; no match yet → `IllegalStateException("No match available")`; non-participating group → -1. `find(from)` resets the search start (from<0 → IndexOutOfBoundsException). Group positions are stored per-find as `gpos<i>`/`gend<i>`/`gok<i>` heap fields (tail-relative + base).

**Verify**: run ConnectBot 11101000; `grep "F-C4-623"` shows `Matcher.start(0) -> 43 rx='(\?|#|$)'` (the end-anchor truth, was 0). `grep -c "Cannot set route"` = **0** (was the fatal). Uncaught marks **0**. The Compose pipeline runs (`AndroidComposeView` dispatches live).

---

### F-C4-624 — ArrayList-family `toString`/`contains` DUAL-STORE COHERENCE

**Root (CB, compounding with 623)**: in registry mode the framework `CollectionShadow::CollectionState` (parallel vectors `elem_kinds`/`elem_strings`/`elem_ints`/`elements`) is the authoritative store for `isEmpty/size/get`; `add()` through the shadow dispatch populates ONLY that store. F-C4-564's `toString` (and the G-6 `contains`) read the engine-side heap fields (`array[i]`) only → a shadow-populated list rendered `"[]"` in the IAE message (`missing: []`) while `isEmpty()` correctly said non-empty, and `contains()` answered false for shadow-stored elements.

**Law**: `toString`/`contains`/`containsAll` now read the shadow store FIRST (kind 2 = string, 3 = int, 1 = object id — mirrored to DalvikValues), falling back to heap fields; empty shadow state falls back too. This is the read-side twin of the F-101 write-back law.

---

### F-C4-625 / F-C4-625b — `MediaStore` CONTENT_URI static + `getContentUri` method families

**Root (live, Nextcloud 3.5.x)**: `BackgroundJobManagerImpl.scheduleContentObserverJob` (called from `MainApp.onCreate`):
1. `MediaStore.Images.Media.INTERNAL_CONTENT_URI` → SGET-MISS → typed-null → Kotlin `checkNotNullExpressionValue` NPE `"INTERNAL_CONTENT_URI must not be null"` → **MainApp.onCreate DIED** → the whole Koin DI wiring aborted → every lateinit service (accountManager...) stayed null → `LauncherActivity` `throwUninitializedPropertyAccessException` at first touch.
2. The very next line: `MediaStore.Files.getContentUri("external")` → typed-null → NPE `"getContentUri(...) must not be null"` (same death).

**Laws (AOSP MediaStore.java)**:
- Statics seeded via the F-NEW-363 `seed_uri` mechanism (real heap Uri objects with `uri_raw`): Images/Video/Audio `INTERNAL_CONTENT_URI` + `EXTERNAL_CONTENT_URI` (+ `Audio.Media.CONTENT_URI`, Images/Video `Thumbnails.EXTERNAL_CONTENT_URI`, `Downloads.EXTERNAL_CONTENT_URI`), `AUTHORITY="media"`; plus the high-frequency `ContactsContract` roots (`Contacts`, `RawContacts`, Phone/Email `CONTENT_URI`, `AUTHORITY`).
- Methods: `getContentUri(String volumeName[, long id])` on `MediaStore$Files/Images$Media/Video$Media/Audio$Media/Albums/Artists/Playlists/Genres` → real Uri `content://media/<volume>/<table>` (table map: file, images/media, video/media, audio/media, audio/albums, audio/artists, audio/playlists, audio/genres); 2-arg form appends `/{id}`. Static call shape: `args[0]` IS the volume (no receiver), matching the `Uri.fromFile` pattern.

**Verify**: run Nextcloud 350000290; `grep "F-C4-625b"` shows `getContentUri("external") -> content://media/external/file`; `grep -c INTERNAL_CONTENT_URI` NPE = 0; `MainApp.onCreate` proceeds past scheduleContentObserverJob (WorkManager ForceStopRunnable cleanup logs).

---

### F-C4-626 — `JobScheduler` METHOD family

**Root (NC, wall 3 of the same cascade)**: WorkManager `ForceStopRunnable` → `JobScheduler21.getAllPendingJobs` → unbridged → typed-null → NPE `"getAllPendingJobs(...) must not be null"` (depth 9).

**Law (AOSP android.app.JobScheduler)**: `getAllPendingJobs()` → a FRESH non-null `List<JobInfo>` every call (empty when nothing is scheduled; scheduled jobs tracked on the scheduler singleton's `js_job<i>` heap fields so the engine's ArrayList iteration laws agree); `getPendingJob(int)` → null (cold-boot truth); `schedule`/`scheduleAsPackage` → `RESULT_SUCCESS` (1) and track the JobInfo; `cancel`/`cancelAll` → void + untrack; `forNamespace` (R-NEW-559 law) restructured into the same family block, unchanged semantics.

---

### F-C4-627 — `java.time.Duration` factory + accessor family

**Root (NC, wall 4 of the same cascade)**: `Duration.ofSeconds(...)` → NO bridge → typed-null → NPE `"ofSeconds(...) must not be null"` (depth 3, MainApp.onCreate chain).

**Law (OpenJDK Duration)**: `ofSeconds(s)` = (s, 0ns); `ofSeconds(s, nano)` normalized (carry whole seconds, nano-of-second in [-999999999, 999999999]); `ofMinutes`=60s; `ofHours`=3600s; `ofDays`=86400s; `ofMillis`=ms×1e6 ns; `ofNanos`=ns. Objects carry `__dur_seconds__`/`__dur_nanos__` (I64); `toMillis()` = s×1000 + ns/1e6; `getSeconds()` (I64); `getNano()` (I32). Statics: args[0] IS the first parameter.

---

## Measured results (4APP, 40s real-dalvik runs)

| App | Before W16 | After W16 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **ConnectBot** | fatal uncaught IAE (NavHost dead), blank | **0 uncaught; NavHost graph builds; Compose AndroidComposeView executing** — deepest CB run ever |
| **Tusky** | DI wall: okhttp IAE → content never inflates | **DI wall DEAD** (`regionMatches->true`); frontier now Material `BottomSheetBehavior` "view is not a child of CoordinatorLayout" (view-attachment family) |
| **Nextcloud** | MainApp.onCreate dead at `INTERNAL_CONTENT_URI` NPE | **FOUR walls of the MainApp-init cascade killed** (MediaStore×2, JobScheduler, Duration); WorkManager ForceStopRunnable cleanup runs; new frontier = `WorkContinuationImpl.mWork` null ("getWork(...) must not be null" at `EnqueueUtilsKt.checkContentUriTriggerWorkerLimits` — an upstream silent-null producer in the enqueue list build) |
| **Thunderbird** | Koin NoDefinitionFound at depth 43 | unchanged (W17 target — see below) |

## Regressions: ZERO

- dooz `a0fae9072313e2d1` ✓, bouncy `8a6c24ac8a7d718e` ✓ **byte-exact**, unote `3b8dcb0adbbc17a9` ✓ **byte-exact**, solitaire `ba50a4d28ea62fe7` ✓, tranquilstopwatch `11a38a5aeeff45a6` ✓ — all 0 uncaught.
- W2 anchors: mines **686** colors ✓ / memory **256** ✓ / blackjack **65** ✓ (all B_STRUCTURED, 0 uncaught).

## Reproduce (self-contained)

```bash
cd miniandroid && make -j1                     # binary sha16 d1d4af34e8555793
cd /home/z/my-project && python3 scripts/w15_baseline.py com.keylesspalace.tusky org.connectbot com.nextcloud.client net.thunderbird.android
python3 work/w2anchors.py                      # W2 anchors
# laws firing: grep "F-C4-62" work/evidence/w15/*.console.log
```

## Tooling persisted (androguard — verdict on the user's question: CONFIRMED HELPING)

`scripts/w16_koin_disasm.py` (class/method disasm, multidex), `w16_list_methods.py` (overload census with code sizes), `w16_find_class.py` (name-substring finder), `w16_search_string.py` (const-string owner locator). Every root this wave was pinned by androguard bytecode ground truth (okhttp scheme check, `MatcherMatchResult.getRange`, the NavDeepLink parse chain, the Koin merged-class registry). Coder 3's issues #560/#561 are androguard-driven too — the tool is now a standing part of the campaign.

## W17 targets

1. **NC**: `WorkContinuationImpl.mWork` null — census the enqueue list build (`WorkManagerImpl.beginUniqueWork` callers; suspect a silent-null collections answer upstream of the ctor).
2. **TB**: Koin `NoDefinitionFoundException` (depth 43, `okhttp3/Dispatcher.getViewModel$lifecycle_viewmodel` chain) — the registry is STRING-keyed (`getFullName(kclass)+":"+qualifier+":"+scope` via `CHM`); R8 type-merged `InstanceRegistry` lives on `Lorg/slf4j/event/EventRecodingLogger;` with `resolveDefinition$koin_core`. Census which module's definitions never registered.

4. **CB**: Compose frame production (draw ops → framebuffer).
