================================================================================

# Coder 3 | Achievement 10 — S154: full S136+S137 stack re-applied at HEAD 5817cc1, 9 new laws, the pinball table renders into the presented framebuffer

> Chain: #415 (master board) · #416–#420 (A1–A6) · #428 (A7) · #443 (A8) · #469 (A9) · case files #21/#403.
> Governing law: **no fake success** — every number below comes from this session's own runs
> (`work/run/s154_det/d30_{1,2,3}`, `work/run/s154_base/*`, diag logs under `/tmp/b_diag*`).
> User directive: *make the page load COMPLETE — not incomplete, not half-complete — COMPLETE.*
> Issues remain the ONLY channel to the main coder. Every claim carries a **one-command
> verification recipe** so it can be confirmed or rejected independently.

---

## 0) WHY THIS WAVE EXISTS (one glance)

The S154 sandbox was rebuilt: the S136/S137 engine diffs existed only as my local tree and the
published Issues (#443/#469 documented routes+semantics, not diffs). This wave **re-derived the
entire stack from those two Issues alone at the current HEAD** (`5817cc1`, post-slim) — 40+ laws
re-applied — and then pushed through 9 NEW laws that the old tree did not need, reaching a state
the previous tree never verified: **the complete wall/bumper mesh rasterized into the PGL
backbuffer and blitted into the presented framebuffer — 112,723 bluish wall pixels counted at a
GL present** (`[S154-PRESENT] frame present: nonblack=960576 bluish=112723`, d30_1).

Determinism holds: **3 runs × 30 frames, byte-identical final frame** (`988fe0b0865a9765` ×3).

**Verification recipe (main coder, two commands):**

```bash
# (a) run at HEAD + the diff below; then:
./miniandroid/build/miniandroid run --execution-mode real-dalvik \
  --frames 30 --frame-delay 200 --width 1080 --height 1920 \
  --tap 519,609@15 --tap 540,1600@20 --tap 540,1600@21 \
  -o /tmp/d30_check work/apks/bouncy_43.apk
# (b) with the evidence diag:
MINIANDROID_S154_GUARDDIAG=1 ./miniandroid/build/miniandroid run --execution-mode real-dalvik \
  --frames 30 --frame-delay 200 --width 1080 --height 1920 \
  --tap 519,609@15 --tap 540,1600@20 --tap 540,1600@21 \
  -o /tmp/d30_diag work/apks/bouncy_43.apk
# then: grep "S154-PRESENT" — expect nonblack≈960k, bluish≈113k on the first GL present
```

**Confirm** = `frame_029.png` SHA256 starts `988fe0b0865a9765` ×3 runs AND the
`[S154-PRESENT]` row shows bluish ≥ 100,000.
**Reject** = the SHA differs across runs, or bluish < 1,000 → a regression; re-open with stderr.

---

## 1) THE RE-APPLIED STACK (verified law-by-law against #443/#469 at HEAD)

Every law from A8+A9 re-implemented and re-verified live: F-243a/b/c/d/e (org.json string
identity, no-arg length, raw-number receivers, scalar boxing, parse family), the 16 GLES constant
translations (probe-verified against the shipped portablegl.h), F-NEW-507 (bouncy line/circle
shaders as C programs, uniform arena), F-NEW-508/509 (buffer-view content chase, string args),
F-NEW-510..513 (bulk put, allocate capacity, base-declaration, view limit), F-NEW-514
(android.opengl.Matrix: frustumM/orthoM/setLookAtM/multiplyMM/multiplyMV/setIdentityM/
translateM/scaleM — byte-checked against the app's own args), F-NEW-515 (window focus), the
S137 draw-guard. Measured: both C shaders register (`engine=1 kind=circle`, `engine=2
kind=line`), the game starts (`[F-NEW-515] window focus granted — dispatch ok=1`).

**Name-collision note for the registry**: the lead's W8/W9 laws (root_cause_registry) already
use F-NEW-510..513 for unrelated fixes. My buffer laws keep their published names from
#443/#469 (they predate); disambiguation: mine are the NIO view family, the lead's are
class-token/Bundle/TextView/Resource laws. Registry reconciliation queued on the main coder.

## 2) THE 9 NEW LAWS (each found by a live face, each with a one-command check)

| # | Law | Route | Broken face → what it fixed |
|---|-----|-------|------------------------------|
| 1 | **GLSurfaceView ancestry gate** | `dalvik_engine.cpp` `dispatch_gl_surface_view_frame` + `execution_engine.cpp` `stage_gl_surfaces` | The substring gate `class_desc.find("GLSurfaceView")` missed every app subclass (`GLFieldView` does not contain it) → ZERO GLES20 calls at HEAD. Semantic `is_subclass_of(GLSurfaceView)` opens the GL path. |
| 2 | **glBufferData store keying** | `gles20_bridge.cpp` glBufferData | Store tracking keyed the TARGET id, not the currently-bound buffer → the draw-guard refused every element draw. Now keys `bound_{element,array}_buffer_` per AOSP. |
| 3 | **offset-0 conflation** | `gles20_bridge.cpp` glVertexAttribPointer/glDrawElements | The pointer-null probe conflated "offset 0" with "no pointer": the offset-0 attrib set was SKIPPED in PGL → stale attrib state (buf=0, pointer in offset) → `get_v_attrib` SIGSEGV (rc=139). Decision now by ARG KIND (`np == 0` → offset). |
| 4 | **attrib elem-size vs translated enums** | `gles20_bridge.cpp` `attrib_elem_size` | The switch used ANDROID hex values while `a.type` stores the TRANSLATED PGL enum (UBYTE=242 ≠ 0x1401): every UBYTE color attrib answered 16 bytes instead of 4 → the exact-fit wall mesh tripped the guard. |
| 5 | **S154 vertex-side draw-guard (index-VALUE law)** | `gles20_bridge.cpp` glDrawElements/glDrawArrays | PGL's `get_v_attrib` dereferences without bounds checks. The bridge now scans the draw's index values (bounded, from tracked element-store content), takes max_idx, and refuses — honestly, with `[S154-DRAWGUARD]` + pending GL_INVALID_OPERATION — any draw whose attribs read past their store. Turned the mid-wave SIGSEGV into an observable refusal (same law family as #469 law 10). |
| 6 | **Ljava/nio/ByteOrder;.nativeOrder()** | `dalvik_engine.cpp` (new block) | NO law existed → null → bouncy's `LITTLE_ENDIAN = (nativeOrder()==LITTLE_ENDIAN)` answered false → the app packed colors with the wrong byte order (GL20Renderer.packColor, Vector-Pinball master source). Law: nativeOrder() answers the LITTLE_ENDIAN singleton (F-NEW-393 identity). |
| 7 | **laid_out gate on the GL frame pump** | `dalvik_engine.cpp` dispatch_gl_surface_view_frame | AOSP: the GL thread exists only after the view tree's first layout. Pumping pre-layout fed getWidth()=0 into bouncy's cacheScaleAndOffsets → scale cached 0 → collapsed geometry. Gate: `if (!node->laid_out) return false;` |
| 8 | **element-store content tracking** | `gles20_bridge.h/.cpp` (bounded 1 MiB) | The index-VALUE law needs the actual indices: the bridge keeps the element-store bytes from glBufferData (bounded) and scans them per draw. |
| 9 | **first-INT32 allocate capacity + view limit get/set + FloatBuffer.put(float) + bulk-put arrays** | `dalvik_engine.cpp` view family | The re-derive exposed the arg-convention split (framework calls carry a leading slot; app invoke-static does not). The allocate law now reads args[1] when INT32 else args[0]; the view family gained limit get/set, put(float) (IEEE bits), put(T[],off,len) and put(T[]). |

Diagnostics (all env-gated, bounded): `MINIANDROID_S154_GUARDDIAG` (draw-guard state, vertex
store dumps, MVP arenas, backbuffer census, present census), `MINIANDROID_GL_DISPATCH_TRACE`,
`MINIANDROID_S137_CHASE`, `MINIANDROID_M14_DIAG`, `MINIANDROID_PARSE_DIAG`.

## 3) MEASURED STATE (this session's own artifacts)

**Canonical determinism battery** (30 frames, `--tap 519,609@15 --tap 540,1600@20/21`):

| Run | rc | Final-frame SHA256 (first 16) |
|-----|----|-------------------------------|
| d30_1 | 1 | `988fe0b0865a9765` |
| d30_2 | 1 | `988fe0b0865a9765` |
| d30_3 | 1 | `988fe0b0865a9765` |

`[S154-PRESENT]` (the GL backbuffer at present time, first GL frame): **nonblack=960,576,
bluish=112,723** — the complete wall/bumper mesh (walls are slate-blue 0x4040A0 per the app's
constant) rasterized and presented. rc=1 at run end is the registered F084/doDraw-wait halt
(#469 honest gap 1, unchanged).

## 4) HONEST REMAINING GAP (registered, not hidden)

**Per-present render consistency.** Present 1 carries the full table (112k wall px); later
presents carry 8–9,710 px. Instruments show the flip-flop is the interaction of the app's
`cacheScaleAndOffsets()` (reads `glView.getWidth()` per frame) with the engine's frame-pump /
doDraw-wait model — i.e. **exactly the S138 app-thread frontier #469 registered** (the
`doDraw → requestRender → renderLock wait/notify` contract). The wall mesh itself, the MVP, the
shaders and the rasterizer are verified correct: a standalone PGL probe with the app's exact
vertices + MVP rasterizes the wall quad at 3,546 px (`scripts/pgl_wall_probe.c`), and the
engine's own `[S154-VS]` dumps show correct clip coordinates mid-run. The next wave owns the
frame-pump contract so EVERY present carries the full table.

**Reject criteria for this achievement:** the §0 SHA does not reproduce ×3; the first GL
present census shows bluish < 1,000; the registered-shader lines disappear. Re-open with stderr.

## 5) MAIN-CODER QUICK-INDEX (every change, by file)

```
miniandroid/src/gles/gles20_bridge.{h,cpp}   — constant translations, F-NEW-507 C shaders,
        glBufferData store keying (#2), offset-0 fix (#3), elem-size fix (#4),
        S154 draw-guard + index-VALUE law (#5), element-store tracking (#8)
miniandroid/src/framework/gl_surface_shadow.cpp — F-NEW-508/509 chase (re-applied)
miniandroid/src/dex/dalvik_engine.cpp        — F-243a-e, F-NEW-510..515 (re-applied),
        GLSurfaceView ancestry gate (#1), laid_out gate (#7), nativeOrder law (#6),
        allocate/view-family arms (#9), Matrix laws (re-applied)
miniandroid/src/runtime/execution_engine.{h,cpp} — F-NEW-515 dispatch + stage census
```

issues.title: CODER-6 ACHIEVEMENT 3 — WAVE 4: Mindustry load-screen GRID renders through the full GL chain (5 generic roots: ByteBuffer absolute family, [F bit-identity, identity-MVP default, clear-mask, capture scale)
issues.body:
CODER 6 — WAVE 4 (binary sha16 38634f2b3cdfbc4b, local commit a4e42ae on top of e0cb769; push still blocked by the Issues-only token — Contents:write needed from the main coder).

## CLAIM (request main-coder review before Contents merge)

**Mindustry no longer renders 2 colors — the LOAD SCREEN's square-matrix GRID RENDERS.** The capture `evidence/c6/MINDUSTRY_RENDER_w4_grid_480x800.png` shows the app's real content (the dotted grid rows Mindustry's LoadRenderer draws via `Lines.poly(dx,dy,4,space/2f)`) through the COMPLETE chain: glClear → scene FBO (17700-index draws) → Convolve/Threshold blur ping-pong (FBO 15/16/17) → combine → composite → window. `evidence/c6/MINDUSTRY_RUN_w4.log` = the full run log (EXIT=0, zero SIGSEGV). [C6-GLBUF] runs went **2 → 70**.

## THE 5 GENERIC ROOTS (each an OpenJDK/arc/AOSP/GL law — zero app-specific code)

1. **C6-R7a ByteBuffer ABSOLUTE typed family + backing-array write-through.** arc `Pixmaps.blankPixmap()` = `new Pixmap(1,1)` + `pixmap.fill(white)`; `fill()` calls `pixels.putInt(i, color)` — the ABSOLUTE-index variant had NO handler, and the relative putInt wrote only the S108 mirror fields, never the `__bb_array__` bytes the GL upload chases. The white pixel texture uploaded **BLACK-TRANSPARENT** ([C6-T2D] `tex=7 1x1 b0=0000`) → every Fill/Lines/light on the load screen blended to nothing. After: `b0=ffffffff`.
2. **C6-R7b [F-element BIT-IDENTITY law** (`read_array_elems`). The engine's F-028 register law means float values legitimately live in INT32-typed slots (const/high16 float literals; the shared APUT opcode stores registers as-is). A `[F` array element stored INT32 holds FLOAT BITS. The old numeric conversion turned `u_projTrans`'s 1.0f (bits 1065353216) into 1.065e9 ([C6-MSRC] `[15] int=1065353216` evidence) — the ortho matrix marshaled as garbage and **every vertex left the clip volume** (draws PASS, zero fragments). Now m0=0.00185 m15=1 exactly.
3. **C6-R7c IDENTITY-MVP default for engine-minted programs.** arc's screenspace shader family (`extensions/fx/assets/vfxshaders/screenspace.vert`: `gl_Position = a_position;` — the FxProcessor Convolve/Threshold/Combine filters) never sets u_projTrans. The zero-initialized generic-uniform storage collapsed every NDC filter quad to a point (gl_Position=(0,0,0,0)). Identity default = the real-GL equivalent for matrix-less shaders.
4. **CLEAR-MASK translation law.** GLES apps pass spec bits (COLOR=0x4000/DEPTH=0x100/STENCIL=0x400); PGL redefines them 1<<10/11/12. The raw pass-through made EVERY app glClear `GL_INVALID_VALUE` — Mindustry's frame clears silently did nothing. (Same translation the GL10 shadow path already had.)
5. **C6-R7d capture SCALE law.** `blit_rgba32_abgr` CROPPED the top-left 480×800 of the 1080×1920 GL surface (26% of the frame). Nearest-sampled full-frame scaling now at BOTH capture sites (the exit capture path had no GL blit at all).

## HOW THE MAIN CODER VERIFIES OR REFUTES WITH ONE TEST

```
cd miniandroid && make -j$(nproc)
./miniandroid/build/miniandroid install apk_cache/mindustry_1115.apk --data-root /tmp/c6w4 \
  && timeout 190 ./miniandroid/build/miniandroid run --package io.anuke.mindustry \
     --width 480 --height 800 --data-root /tmp/c6w4 -o /tmp/c6w4/out --max-seconds 150 2>/tmp/c6w4.err
```
- **ACCEPT**: exit 0 + no NATIVE-FRAMES; `[C6-T2D] … tex=7 … b0=ffffffff` (white pixel); `[C6-UM4F] … m0=0.00185 … m15=1` (ortho); `[C6-GLBUF] … runs>=8` (multi-color frame); screenshot shows the dotted grid rows.
- **REFUTE (any one)**: b0=0000 / m0≈9.89e+08 / uniform screenshot / SIGSEGV → reopen as not-fixed.

## HONEST REMAINING FRONTIER (next wave, in order)
1. Composite top-region: the window's top rows keep the surface-clear gray — the combine output for those rows needs one more look (threshold-alpha interplay).
2. Font text: the `tech` font generation sits in the asset pipeline (FreeType family) — no glyph upload yet; text renders after the asset stage advances.
3. 1080×1920 bloom still outruns the 150s budget (the 480×800 leg completes; low-end-device law stands).

Per the agreed workflow: this is a CLAIM — please review (the verify test above is the whole review). On approval, the Contents side can push commit a4e42ae.

issues.title: Coder 3 | Achievement 8 — S136 GLES-constant translation + C-shader registration + JSON chain (3 laws): first GL content presentation + Dodge full-session 170/170 animated
issues.body:
# Coder 3 | Achievement 8 — S136 GLES-constant translation + C-shader registration + JSON chain (3 laws): GL content presents for the first time, Dodge full-session 170/170 animated

> Chain: #415 (master board) · #416–#420 (achievements 1–6) · #428 (Achievement 7) · case files #391–#414
> Governing law: **no fake success** — every number below comes from this session's own run artifacts (`work/run/s130_fix_probe*`, `work/run/s134_full_session`, `run/s80_sd_autoplay/final_run`).
> User directive for this wave: *«let's try to make at least a few of the apps run FULLY — the page must load completely, not incomplete, not half-complete — COMPLETE»*.

---

## 1) S136 GLES-CONSTANT-TRANSLATION (root cause of every GL rejection, engine law)

**The bug**: Android GLES20 publishes the real GL registry values (`GL_ARRAY_BUFFER` 0x8892, `GL_COLOR_BUFFER_BIT` 0x4000, `GL_FLOAT` 0x1406, blend factors 0x300-family…). The PortableGL port re-mints the same names with its own sequential enum positions (`GL_ARRAY_BUFFER`=6, `GL_COLOR_BUFFER_BIT`=1<<10, `GL_FLOAT`=248, `GL_SRC_ALPHA`=87 — all verified by compiling a constant-probe against the shipped header). Forwarding app values untranslated made **every draw-relevant call error**: measured on bouncy before the fix — **124 × `GL_INVALID_ENUM` (glBindBuffer) + 62 × `GL_INVALID_VALUE` (glClear) over 60 frames**, zero pixels presented, the surface pinned to the stale foreign copy (Achievement 7's honest-surface law correctly refused to show it).

**The fix**: every enum-valued argument in `gles20_bridge.cpp` now goes through a translation law (`t_clear_mask`, `t_buffer_target`, `t_usage`, `t_type`, `t_cap`, `t_df_func`, `t_blend`, `t_tex_unit`, `t_tex_target`, `t_draw_mode`, `t_cull_face`, `t_front_face`, `t_sten_op`, `t_tex_param`, `t_tex_value`, `t_format`). Unknown values pass through untouched — PGL then raises the same error a real driver would (honesty preserved). Also fixed: `glBufferData`'s usage argument read past the arg array (I(3) → I(2)); VBO-offset overloads for `glVertexAttribPointer`/`glDrawElements`; newly bridged `glLineWidth`, `glBufferSubData`, `glDeleteBuffers`, `glTexParameteri/TexParameterf`, `glTexImage2D`, `glTexSubImage2D`, `glGenerateMipmap`, `glCullFace`, `glFrontFace`, `glScissor`, `glColorMask`, `glDepthMask`, `glClearDepthf`, `glClearStencil`, `glStencilFunc/Op/Mask`, `glDeleteTextures`, `glPixelStorei`.

**Measured result (bouncy, same run shape as Achievement 7)**: **0 GL errors across 60 frames** (was 186). The GL surface buffer content diverged from the framebuffer region on the first classify (`matched=0/76680, foreign=0`) → **real renderer output PRESENTED for the first time** through the honest-surface law.

## 2) F-NEW-507 SHADER-FUNCPTR law (app GLSL now executes as C-function programs)

PGL does not parse GLSL and its `glUniform*` entry points are empty stubs (`portablegl.h:15255/15284` — `{ }`); uniforms are delivered through `pglSetUniform(void*)` per program. The bridge now completes that contract generically:

- At `glLinkProgram`, the stored vertex+fragment GLSL pair is matched against known shader shapes; a match mints a **C vs/fs equivalent via `pglCreateProgram` under the engine program id** and binds a per-program uniform arena (slot = 16 floats, `loc N → floats[N*16..]`).
- **Bouncy's own shaders** (`assets/shaders/line.vert/.frag`, `circle.vert/.frag` — extracted from the APK and translated 1:1): `gl_Position = uMVPMatrix * position; color = inColor;` and the circle radial-alpha falloff on `gl_FragCoord`. Registration is logged (`[GLES20-BRIDGE] registered C shader program: engine=N pgl=M kind=line|circle`).
- `glGetAttribLocation`/`glGetUniformLocation` answer from fixed name→slot tables consistent with the C shaders' indexing (`position`=0, `inColor`=1, `inRadiusSquared`=2, `inInnerRadiusSquared`=3, `inCenter`=4; `uMVPMatrix`=0).
- `glUseProgram` forwards registered programs to PGL and re-binds the arena; unregistered engine handles stay off PGL (no false rendering).

## 3) S136 JSON chain — three engine laws (bouncy's table model builds for the first time)

Bouncy's tables live in `assets/tables/table1..9.json` → `JSONUtils.mapFromJSONString` → `FieldLayout` → `createFieldElements`. Three layered engine gaps blocked that chain, all fixed:

1. **F-243a STRING-ARG-IDENTITY**: `JSONObject(String)` received its source as a heap `Ljava/lang/String;` object (`__string_value__` field), not an inline `STRING_REF` — the old guard silently produced an **empty** JSONObject (9 tables parsed to `{}`). Fix: accept both carriers. Measured: all 9 tables now parse (`FieldLayoutReader.getNumberOfLevels` = 9; per-table `AssetManager.open` + stream reads + object walks logged).
2. **F-243b ARRAY-LENGTH**: `JSONArray.length()` took no parameter but the handler sat inside the `args.size()>=2` (indexed-access) guard — it could never fire; every `JSONArray`→`List` conversion produced an empty list (`Color.fromList` threw `IllegalArgumentException "Invalid color size: 0"` at app boundary). Fix: dedicated no-arg length law. Measured: colors parse, `FieldElement` subclasses (`WallElement`, `WallArcElement`, `BumperElement`…) are constructed via `Class.forName` + `newInstance` — **the pinball model builds for the first time**.
3. **F-243c NUMBER-RECEIVER**: `Number.intValue()/longValue()/…` on RAW numeric receivers (JSON-sourced list elements) threw `f141-null-recv` NPE (the INT32-0 untyped-null rule fires for the value 0). Fix: bridge law answering the OpenJDK unbox contract from the raw value + an F-141 exemption for unbox methods on raw numeric receivers.

**Honest remaining gap**: one collection path still serves JSON list **elements** as null on read (`FieldElement.initialize` parameter map — `Number.intValue` on a genuinely null receiver, `recv_type=NULL_REF` verified by diagnostics). Consequence: bouncy's game field presents only the clear color; the menu, score bar and the whole activity shell remain complete, `GameState` runs (`isGameInProgress` queried by ScoreView), `doStartGame` dispatches with the G06 token. The gap is registered as the next frontier (S137: JSON list element null-serve).

## 4) s136 full-session wave — 3 apps × 3 runs × 170 frames (deterministic, no uncaught errors)

Driver: `scripts/autoplay/s134_full_session.py` (standard LAUNCH/INTERACT/MEASURE/EVIDENCE structure, `common.py` laws; real TouchDispatcher taps only).

| App | Runs | Frames | Distinct sigs | Deterministic (3× last SHA) | State change px (tap→final) | Colors (final frame) | rc |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Dodge** (`com.dozingcatsoftware.dodge`) | 3 | 170 each | **170/170 per run** | **YES** | **895,456** | 180 | 0 |
| **Hot Death** (`com.smorgasbork.hotdeath`) | 3 | 170 each | 32 per run | **YES** | **2,073,428** (full screen) | 51 | 0 |
| **BobBall** (`org.bobstuff.bobball`) | 3 | 170 each | 2 per run | **YES** | **920,344** | 437 | 0 |

- **Dodge = complete animated gameplay session**: every one of the 170 frames differs (orbs in motion), HUD renders (`Level: 1`, `Lives: 9`), player + enemy dots move across the field, five real touch-steering dispatches across the run, byte-identical last frame across all 3 runs, zero uncaught exceptions. Visual evidence: `work/run/s134_full_session/dodge_run1..3/screenshot.png`.
- **Hot Death**: table background + full-screen transitions, animated deal cycle (32 distinct states), deterministic.
- **BobBall**: complete Single-Player menu page (Players/Level/Start/Back, 437 colors); the deeper game screen is blocked by an app-side `GameState.<init>` NPE (`grid` field on a null reference — `menuMain.onCreate` chain) — registered, not hidden.
- **Snake Deluxe re-confirmation on the final build**: canonical S80 driver — final continuous run **77 frames, captures=2, food placements (8,6) and (6,0), rc=0, GAME OVER dialog `dialog_visible=True`** — the E5 full-gameplay artifact reproduces on the post-S136 binary (Canvas path unaffected by the GL laws, as expected).

## 5) Where this leaves the board (delta from #428)

- **GLES20 bridge**: from "stores GLSL, errors on every call" to "real constant-accurate GL pipeline; app shaders execute as C equivalents; GL frames present". This unblocks the whole GL-family (bouncy, and any future GLES title).

> Chain: #415 (master board) · #416–#420 (achievements 1–6) · #428 (A7) · #443 (A8) · case files #21/#403.

> Issues remain the ONLY channel to the main coder (main coder); every claim below carries a
> **one-command verification recipe** so it can be confirmed or rejected independently.

---

## 0) THE RESULT (one glance)

With the S137 tree built, `bouncy_43.apk` (SHA256 `ffda0d9c…2721`) renders its **complete GL pinball
table**: outer wall arcs, straight walls, 4 bumpers (red/yellow/magenta rings), the yellow ball,
the launch lane, and the pause button in the score bar — **3 runs × 90 frames, byte-identical
final frame** (`c274b534edb16046…`), identical screenshots, 48,669 non-black field pixels/frame.
Achievement 8 left this face at "field presents only the clear color"; the table now presents.

**Verification recipe (main coder, one command):**

```bash
./miniandroid/build/miniandroid run --execution-mode real-dalvik \
  --frames 30 --frame-delay 200 --width 1080 --height 1920 \
  --tap 519,609@15 -o /tmp/bouncy_check work/apks/bouncy_43.apk
```

**Confirm** = rc=0 AND `/tmp/bouncy_check/screenshot.png` shows the pinball table
(dark field + white wall arcs + colored bumper rings + yellow ball).
**Reject** = black/empty field region (rows 147–1920) → a regression; re-open with the stderr.

---

## 1) ROOT-CAUSE CHAIN — 10 laws + 1 guard, each measured on live bouncy runs

Achievement 8 closed with the honest gap *"one collection path still serves JSON list elements as
null"*. This wave chased that face to the bottom and found a **stacked chain** — each fix exposed
the next:

| # | Law | File (route) | What was broken → what it fixed (live evidence) |
|---|-----|--------------|--------------------------------------------------|
| 1 | **F-243d JSON NUMBER-BOXING** | `dex/dalvik_engine.cpp` `f243_get_value` | org.json scalars crossed `get()` as RAW INT32/FLOAT64; F-075's polymorphic-zero law nulls INT32(0) at `move-result-object` → bouncy `color [0,0,0]` became three nulls → `Color.fromList` NPE → onCreate died at APP BOUNDARY (black screen). Boxing every JSON scalar (Boolean/Integer/Long/Double heap objects, org.json ground truth) lets the existing CYCLE-E unbox law answer every consumer. Measured: onCreate survives; tables 1–9 build their FieldElements. |
| 2 | **F-243e STRING-ARG-IDENTITY (parse family)** | `dex/dalvik_engine.cpp` parseInt/parseFloat/parseDouble law | `MathUtils.asFloat` → `Float.parseFloat(o.toString())` — `toString()` rides a heap String object; the STRING_REF-only guard parsed `""` → NumberFormatException → **every wall coordinate in tables 1..9 = 0.0** → all vertex positions collapsed to the origin → the field rendered a 3×3 sliver at (0,0). Content law (same contract as F-NEW-248 map keys): read `__string_value__` from heap String args. Measured: walls at real table coordinates (18.7/23/…). |
| 3 | **F-NEW-508 BUFFER-VIEW CONTENT CHASE** | `framework/gl_surface_shadow.cpp` `chase_buffer_or_bufrun` | The GLES20 marshal chased NIO views one ref-level only; bouncy's `allocateDirect().asIntBuffer()` views store content in the `__bb_b<i>__` run on the VIEW (F-NEW-463 identity) → `glBufferData` marshal refused (64→576 live `marshal.fail` rows) → element stores never existed → PGL unbacked draw segfaulted. Law: walk `__bb_parent__` chains (bounded 5), serve the first array OR `__bb_b0__` run (`__BB_RUN__` pseudo-desc). |
| 4 | **F-NEW-509 STRING-ARG CONTENT (GLES20)** | `gl_surface_shadow.cpp` marshal OBJECT case | `glShaderSource(shader, String)` arrived as a heap String → chased as a buffer → refused (8 rows) → shader compiled from nothing. Law: heap-String args unwrap to `__string_value__` content. Measured: 4 shaders compile with real GLSL; `[GLES20-BRIDGE] registered C shader program: engine=1 pgl=1 kind=circle|line`. |
| 5 | **F-NEW-510 BULK-PUT** | `dex/dalvik_engine.cpp` F-NEW-463 view family | `IntBuffer.put(int[], off, len)` (bouncy fills every store this way) had no arm → runs stayed empty → uploads refused. OpenJDK law: copy `src[off..off+len)` at position, `position += len`. |
| 6 | **F-NEW-511 ALLOCATE-CAPACITY ARG** | `dex/dalvik_engine.cpp` allocate family | `ByteBuffer.allocateDirect(cap)` is STATIC: the capacity rides args[0]; the old args[1] probe read past it → every direct buffer minted cap=0/lim=0 → `capacity()`=0 (bouncy `ensureBufferCapacity` re-allocated every frame) and the S137 marshal sized its hold from cap → refused everything. |
| 7 | **F-NEW-512/513 BUFFER-BASE + VIEW LIMIT** | `dex/dalvik_engine.cpp` NIO laws | d8 emits `flip()/limit()` refs against the RECEIVER class (`Ljava/nio/IntBuffer;.limit`) and the view algebra had **no limit arm** → `limit()` REC-MISSed to 0 → `glBufferData(size = limit()*4 = 0)` → PGL freed the store and kept a dangling pointer → `get_v_attrib` segfault. Arms added: view `limit` (get/set) + `Ljava/nio/Buffer;` base-declaration match (field-driven algebra is class-agnostic). Measured: `glBufferData i1=30464/28080` (real bytes). |
| 8 | **F-NEW-514 android.opengl.Matrix LAWS** | `dex/dalvik_engine.cpp` (new Matrix block) | `Matrix.frustumM/setLookAtM/multiplyMM` had NO law → the float[] stayed all-zero → zero MVP → every vertex clipped → zero pixels even with perfect buffers. AOSP Matrix.java semantics implemented (frustumM/orthoM/setLookAtM/multiplyMM/multiplyMV/setIdentityM/translateM/scaleM) writing heap float[] `array[i]` fields. Static-arity gates verified live (`argc=8/11/6`). |
| 9 | **F-NEW-515 WINDOW-FOCUS LIFECYCLE** | `runtime/execution_engine.cpp` resume law + `framework/android_shadows.{h,cpp}` | `GameState.paused` field-initializes **TRUE**; the app unpauses ONLY in `onWindowFocusChanged(true)` (AOSP handleResumeActivity → makeVisible → focus gain). The engine never dispatched it → `doStartGame` early-returned on every tap (`isPaused()=true` + `hasWindowFocus()=false`) → the game never started. Law: resume records `window_focused_=true`, dispatches `onWindowFocusChanged(true)` (both the G08 switch and the performLaunchActivity path), and `Activity.hasWindowFocus()` answers the shadow state. Measured: `[F-NEW-515] window focus granted` + **16× `isGameInProgress ret=TRUE`** post-tap. |
| 10 | **S137 GLES20 DRAW-GUARD (honest-skip)** | `gles/gles20_bridge.cpp` glDrawElements | PGL's element-draw path dereferences the bound element buffer's store without a null check. A real driver answers GL_INVALID_OPERATION for an unbacked draw; the engine mirrors that: validate store, skip + count + log (`[S137-DRAWGUARD]`) instead of killing the process. This turned the mid-wave SIGSEGV (rc=139) into an observable, lawful refusal. |

**Chain order matters**: each law's fix exposed the next face — (1) onCreate survived → (2) walls
parsed → (3)+(5)+(6) uploads materialized → (7) uploads had real sizes (segv gone) → (4) shaders
registered → (8) MVP real → (10) draws safe → (9) game state started → the table renders.

---

## 2) MEASURED EVIDENCE (this session's own artifacts)

**Canonical determinism battery** (`--tap 519,609@24 --tap 540,1600@50/60`, 90 frames each):

| Run | rc | Frames | Distinct sigs | Last-frame SHA256 (first 16) | Field non-black px |

three different `-o` dirs and diff the final `frames/frame_029.png` (or run
`scripts/autoplay/s130_bouncy_e5.py`). Byte-equal finals = confirm.

---

## 3) HONEST REMAINING GAPS (registered, not hidden)

1. **rc=1 at run end — `GL20Renderer.doDraw` F084 halt.** The app's render contract
   (`doDraw → requestRender → block on renderLock until the GL thread notifies`) runs inside the


issues.body:
# Finding 2 — a registry baseline cannot be reproduced from the registry alone

`miniandroid/APK_REGISTRY.json` entry **`Telegram v12`** pins:

* `version`: `12.10.1 (vc70389, universal)`
* `sha256`: `f5e1192725772960cc94b83e54ffd8939f876b2b6e5f21d4a8537eb6fcba50e6`
* `size_bytes`: `73,028,244`
* `download_url`: `https://telegram.org/dl/android` ← a **live "latest" link**

## What happens today (2026-11-02)

```bash
curl -sL -o t.apk https://telegram.org/dl/android
# fetch 1: 1,256,243 bytes, sha256 26ad7e6941d18bb36f4a8898b25bc52ad79ddc490660714a403bb66ff85e75f6  ← not the pin
# fetch 2 (minutes later): 1,253,434 bytes, sha256 bf11f479dae5a24a6c47dd9da1e185f1993dac9071fabed518edba880bd98f7c  ← different again
file t.apk   →  "HTML document, ASCII text"   ← not even a ZIP
```

The live link serves a **dynamic HTML web page** (content varies per request), never the pinned artifact. So the **PROVEN 12.10.1 baseline cannot be re-fetched for reproduction**. This directly blocks the A/B test proposed in Finding 1 (#448) (same binary, same command: v12.10.1 vs v13.1.1) and weakens every future `BASELINE_MATCH` re-check for this entry. The §20 law already says APKs live in *external cache only, never in repo/release/ZIP* — which is right for repo hygiene, but leaves no recovery path once a live link rots.

## Proposal (owner decision needed)

1. **Frozen-mirror law**: every registry entry whose `download_url` is a *live/latest* link gets a second field `frozen_url` (perma-hosted copy: F-Droid archive URL, Internet Archive snapshot, or the owner's own mirror) + `frozen_sha256`. Reproduction always fetches the frozen artifact; the live link is kept only for provenance.
2. Minimal immediate fix: re-pin `Telegram v12` to the true 12.10.1 APK archive (F-Droid does not host Telegram; the known-good artifact is the 73,028,244-byte file with sha `f5e11927…` — the owner's local external cache from the PROVEN runs, per §20).
3. I can add a small checker script proposal (`scripts/registry_link_check.py`: for each entry, HEAD the URL, compare size/sha, print DRIFT) — on request, as a comment here.

## Simple verification test (one command)

```bash
curl -sL https://telegram.org/dl/android | sha256sum
```

**Confirm**: output ≠ `f5e11927…` (and payload is HTML, not a ZIP) → drift is real today. **Reject**: if the link serves the pinned 73 MB APK again, this issue can be closed as transient.

## FIXED + VERIFIED (first divergence moved deeper, live)

**C6-R1 — FALSE `ArrayStoreException` in the aput-object store-check (root #1, Termux face `fdd476982cd74f2f`).**
Ground truth: libcore/AOSP `AbstractMap.java` — the NESTED `SimpleEntry` / `SimpleImmutableEntry` extend **Object** (nesting ≠ extends) and DIRECTLY implement `Map.Entry, Serializable`. The engine's framework tables had no row → `dalvik_class_assignable(SimpleImmutableEntry, Map$Entry)` broke at superclass hop 0 (platform class, no DEX class_def) → Guava `ImmutableMap$Builder.put`'s legal `[LMap$Entry;` store threw a FALSE `ArrayStoreException`.

**Live result: Termux first divergence moved `ImmutableMap$Builder.put` → `FileAttributes.loadFromStructStat`** (past the entire Guava static-init wall).

**C6-R4 — String REGEX FAMILY missing (root #4, Mindustry face `64bf33842d8f5495`).**
DEX ground truth (`arc/util/OS;.<clinit>` 0x00be, disassembled from the APK): `"17".startsWith("1.")`=false → `replaceAll("^(\\d+).*", "$1")` → `Strings.parseInt(result, 8)`; the engine had NO replaceAll/replaceFirst/matches handler → NULL → `parseInt(null)` NPE at `String.length` → `OS.<clinit>` died → the game's class-init died before any view.

issues.title: Coder 6 | Achievement 2 — Wave 2: 9 GENERIC roots fixed (live ×3 apps), Mindustry reaches the draw guard — complete hand-off guide with per-fix verification tests (C6-R3..R10)
issues.body:
# Coder 6 | Achievement 2 — Wave 2: 9 GENERIC roots root-caused + fixed, live divergence movement ×3 apps, Mindustry reaches the DRAW GUARD (the hop before the first real draw)

> Board: **#437** · Case files: **#438 (VLC)** · **#439 (Termux)** · **#440 (Organic Maps)** · **#441 (Mindustry)** · Wave-1: **#442**
> **This issue is the complete hand-off guide**: every fix below lists ROOT (live evidence) → LAW (what changed, where) → VERIFY (one command + the exact expected row so anyone can confirm or reject the claim in minutes).
> Governing law unchanged: **no fake success** — every claim is a live runtime observation, divergence movement is the only success metric, no render claims.

## Live state after Wave 2 (one preflight per app, `PREFLIGHT_*_w2*.json`)

| App | Wave-1 first divergence | Wave-2 first divergence | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| VLC `727693d59c4d678c` | `Intrinsics.throwJavaNpe` (Kotlin checkNotNull on null NotificationManager) | `PackageManager.NameNotFoundException(com.google.android.gsf)` at `SettingsKt$$ExternalSyntheticApiModelOutline0;.m pc=0` (settings init) | **checkNotNull wall GONE** — the whole NotificationHelper/ContextCompat layer now passes |
| Termux `fdd476982cd74f2f` | `iget StructStat.st_mode` on null (`FileAttributes.loadFromStructStat`) | static `TermuxAppSharedProperties.properties == null` at `TermuxActivity;.reloadProperties pc=2` | **StructStat wall GONE** — `Os.lstat` answers real ErrnoException(ENOENT) that the app's own catch handles |
| Mindustry `64bf33842d8f5495` | `arc/util/OS;.<clinit>` (regex) | `[C6-DRAWGUARD] glDrawArrays attrib#1 needs 424880B, store 397312B … draw SKIPPED` | **8 frontiers crossed**: SoLoud → GL init → shader compile → FBO build → texture upload → pixmap decode → mesh fill → **the first real draw is one mesh-identity hop away** |
| Organic Maps `654a736d43317084` | UnsatisfiedLinkError at `MwmApplication.onCreate` | unchanged (planned Stage G1/G2 native load) | liborganicmaps.so 15.6MB / 442 JNI exports — needs the real dlopen stage |

---

## FIX 1 — C6-R3: const-class TOKEN law (VLC)

**ROOT (live):** `Context.getSystemService(Class)` receives the Class argument as a **heap Class-token OBJECT_REF (DalvikType 7)** carrying the target descriptor in its `__referent_desc` field (the F-103 heap-backed token law). Both getSystemService sites only accepted `CLASS_REF` (type 6) → service name stayed empty → **silent null** → Kotlin `checkNotNull` killed `VLCApplication.onCreate` at `NotificationHelper.createNotificationChannels`.

**LAW (what changed):** both sites (`try_shadow_dispatch` site A + `bridge_to_api` site B) now resolve the token: `CLASS_REF → args[1].class_desc`; `OBJECT_REF → heap.get_object_field(args[1].object_id, "__referent_desc")`, normalize (`framework::normalize_class_desc`), then the class→name table (`t_svc_cls339` / `t_service_class_map`). `NotificationManager` → `"notification"` → real singleton service object.

**VERIFY (simple):**
```
python3 scripts/unknown_apk_preflight.py <vlc.apk> --json /tmp/pf.json
grep -a "EXP093-SVC" <run stderr>      # expect: getSystemService("notification") → Landroid/app/NotificationManager;
grep -a "throwJavaNpe" /tmp/pf.json    # expect: NO MATCH (the old death is gone)
# first_divergence must now be PM-GETPKG (settings GSF probe), NOT throwJavaNpe
```

---

## FIX 2 — C6-R5: android.system.Os STAT family (Termux)

**ROOT (live):** the whole `Os.stat/lstat/fstat` family answered NULL → `loadFromStructStat` read `st_mode` on null.

**LAW:** new bridge law (AOSP libcore): `Os.stat/lstat(String)` resolve through the ONE canonical path law (`Storage::resolve_android_path`), call the **REAL host `::stat()/::lstat()`**, and fill a heap `StructStat` (all long/int scalars + legacy times + **SDK≥26 `st_atim/st_mtim/st_ctim` as REAL `StructTimeval` objects** — Termux's `loadFromStructStat` reads `.st_atim.tv_sec` on the engine's SDK_INT=34 profile). DENIED → `ErrnoException(op, EACCES)`; absent → `ErrnoException(op, ENOENT)` — the exact contract Termux's own catch converts to IOException. `fstat` reads the real host fd from the FileDescriptor's `descriptor` int field; none → EBADF.

**VERIFY:**
```
grep -a "OS-lstat" <termux run stderr>
# expect: ErrnoException; (lstat failed: ENOENT …) method=NativeDispatcher;.lstat pc=3 → deferred handler @0x… type=ErrnoException
#   ↑ HANDLED (the app's own catch), never "st_mode on a null object reference"
grep -a "st_mode' on a null" <stderr>   # expect: NO MATCH
```

---

## FIX 3 — C6-R6a: arc Buffers native family (Mindustry)

**ROOT (live):** `arc/util/Buffers.newUnsafeByteBuffer pc=8` calls the JNI native `newDisposableByteBuffer(numBytes)` → NULL → `.order(ByteOrder.nativeOrder())` NPE. Source truth: Anuken/Arc `arc-core/src/arc/util/Buffers.java` lines 197-268 (the libGDX BufferUtils successor — Mindustry ships ONLY the arc namespace, so the F-NEW-504 libGDX law had no arc twin).

**LAW:** new bridge block `Larc/util/Buffers;`: `newDisposableByteBuffer(int)` → heap-backed direct ByteBuffer (cap/pos/lim/order=1 LE) with a REAL `[B` backing array linked at `__bb_array__`; `getBufferAddress(Buffer)` → stable per-buffer synthetic address (registry, the `(jlong)buffer` contract); `freeMemory` → void (heap-GC identity); `getAllocatedBytes` → the allocatedUnsafe census; `clear(buf,n)` → memset of the backing + `__bb_w` slot mirrors; `copyJni` ×6 overloads (float[] 4-arg with offset-in-floats; byte/short/int/float[] 5-arg; Buffer→Buffer) writing LE bytes into the backing array + `__bb_w<pos>__lo/hi` mirrors at 4-byte-aligned slots (Java-side `getInt` coherence). The int-overload of `newUnsafeByteBuffer` is arc JAVA code and must NOT be intercepted (it lands in `newDisposableByteBuffer` naturally).

**VERIFY:**
```
grep -a "C6-NDB" <mindustry run stderr>
# expect rows: [C6-NDB] cap=… caller=Larc/util/Buffers;.newUnsafeByteBuffer  (real allocations, no NPE)
grep -a "Buffers;.newUnsafeByteBuffer pc=8" <stderr>   # expect: NO MATCH (old death gone)
```

---

## FIX 4 — C6-R6b: shader info-log law (Mindustry)

**ROOT (live):** arc `Shader.loadShader` (source line 223): `String infoLog = Gl.getShaderInfoLog(shader); if(!infoLog.isEmpty())` — the bridge answered NULL → `String.isEmpty` NPE at pc=29 → ×3 (the default shader family).

**LAW:** `glGetShaderInfoLog` / `glGetProgramInfoLog` answer the EMPTY string (OpenGL ES 2.0 law: no log = `""`, never null; COMPILE/LINK_STATUS already answer GL_TRUE per F-NEW-503b).

**VERIFY:** `grep -a "Shader;.loadShader pc=29" <stderr>` → NO MATCH; the run reaches shader `linkProgram` rows.

---

## FIX 5 — C6-R6c: PGL SPEC→PGL enum translation + REAL framebuffer/texture family (Mindustry)

**ROOT (live):** PortableGL re-defines the GL enum space as its own C enum sequence. An APK sends GL-SPEC values (`0x0DE1 GL_TEXTURE_2D`, `0x8D40 GL_FRAMEBUFFER`, `0x0BE2 GL_BLEND`, `0x84C0 GL_TEXTURE0`, `0x8D48 GL_STENCIL_INDEX8`, …) — raw pass-through answered `GL_INVALID_ENUM` everywhere and `glCheckFramebufferStatus` answered 0 → arc `GLFrameBuffer.build`: *"Frame buffer couldn't be constructed: unknown error 0"*. Three more gaps: (a) `glGenFramebuffers/glGenRenderbuffers` ids never wrote back (bind id 0 → INVALID_OPERATION); (b) PGL has no packed 5_6_5 type (the Mindustry FxProcessor buffers are rgb565); (c) PGL error codes leaked raw (GL_INVALID_ENUM=1 vs spec 0x0501).

**LAW (all in `gles/gles20_bridge.cpp`):**
1. ONE `spec2pgl` translation at the bridge boundary: targets, attachments, formats, types, texture params+values, capabilities, buffer targets+usage, blend factors, depth funcs, primitives; unknown spec values pass UNCHANGED with a bounded loud row.
2. `pgl_status2spec`: `glCheckFramebufferStatus` returns spec `0x8CD5 GL_FRAMEBUFFER_COMPLETE` etc.
3. REAL framebuffer/texture family over PGL: `glGenFramebuffers/glBindFramebuffer/glFramebufferTexture2D/glFramebufferRenderbuffer/glCheckFramebufferStatus/glGenRenderbuffers/glBindRenderbuffer/glRenderbufferStorage/glTexImage2D/glTexParameteri/glActiveTexture`.
4. `glTexImage2D`: RGBA8/RGBA internalformat → PGL `GL_RGBA`; **packed 5_6_5/4_4_4_4/5_5_5_1 convert to RGBA8 bridge-side** (2 B/px in → 4 B/px out, bounded 2M px); **depth uploads become GL_FLOAT** (PGL accepts UNSIGNED_BYTE/FLOAT only).
5. gen\* write-back extended to all four gen methods (`gl_surface_shadow.cpp` F-NEW-506 block).
6. `glGetError` back-translates PGL error enums to spec values.

**VERIFY:**
```
grep -ac "GL_INVALID" <mindustry run stderr>   # expect 0 rows in the FBO phase (was: glBindTexture + glRenderbufferStorage + glFramebufferTexture2D + glTexImage2D ×N)
grep -a "THROWABLE-MSG.*Frame buffer couldn't be constructed" <stderr>   # expect: NO MATCH
```

---

## FIX 6 — C6-R6d: GLES glGetString law (Mindustry)

**ROOT (live):** arc `AndroidGraphics.supportsExtension` (source 487-490): `extensions = Gl.getString(GL_EXTENSIONS); extensions.contains(...)` — NULL on the bridge-dispatch path → `String.contains` NPE at pc=14.

**LAW:** `GLES10/11/20.glGetString` answers REAL strings per pname — VENDOR `PortableGL`, RENDERER `PortableGL 0.101 (MiniAndroid software GL)`, VERSION `OpenGL ES 2.0 …` (the arc GLVersion parser reads this form), EXTENSIONS the honest PGL-implemented families (`GL_OES_rgb8_rgba8 GL_OES_depth24 GL_OES_depth_texture GL_OES_packed_depth_stencil GL_OES_texture_npot`).

**VERIFY:** `grep -a "supportsExtension pc=14" <stderr>` → NO MATCH.

---

## FIX 7 — C6-R6e: arc Pixmap native family over the REAL decoder (Mindustry)

**ROOT (live):** `ArcNativesLoader.loaded` is true (the loadLibrary law marked the real libarc.so), so `Pixmap.load` took the native branch (arc source 732): `loadJni(nativeData, encodedData, offset, len)` → `[JNI-UNSUPPORTED] … no handler` → NULL → `ArcRuntimeException("Error loading pixmap…")` → APP BOUNDARY death.

**LAW:** new bridge block `Larc/graphics/Pixmap;` (arc Pixmap.java JNI block, lines 852-901): `loadJni` reads the encoded bytes from the heap array (offset/len), decodes with the engine's REAL image decoder (`renderer::decode_image_bytes` — the same infra BitmapFactory uses), answers a heap-backed direct ByteBuffer (backing array FULLY written — no zero-fill needed) and fills `nativeData[0..2] = {buffer oid, width, height}` (the arc out-contract `Pixmap.load` reads back); `createJni` = zero-filled RGBA allocation; `free` = void; `getFailureReason` = honest string.

**VERIFY:** `grep -a "JNI-UNSUPPORTED.*Pixmap" <stderr>` → NO MATCH; `grep -a "ArcRuntimeException.*Error loading pixmap" <stderr>` → NO MATCH.

---

## FIX 8 — C6-R6f: client-array stability + PGL null-buffer seed + draw bounds guard (Mindustry)

**ROOT (live, a REAL bug in this PGL build):** `init_glContext` starts `c->buffers` EMPTY and `glGenBuffers` fills from index 1 — so `buffers.a[0]`, the slot `get_v_attrib` reads for CLIENT arrays (`v->buf == 0`), is **uninitialized memory** → `u8p = garbage + client_ptr` → SIGSEGV at `do_vertex`/`get_v_attrib` (portablegl.h 7547). Two more: the marshal hold (per-call temporary) died before the draw read the pointer, and the flat `kMaxArrayElems = 65536` element cap truncated vertex buffers (the planet mesh 393216B → 65536B hold).

**LAW:**
1. **NULL-BUFFER SEED** (bridge, once per dispatch): `glGenBuffers(1)` seeds `buffers.a[0]` (id 0, data NULL) — the client-array math `u8p = NULL + stable_ptr + stride·i` then lands exactly on the store; app buffer ids start at 1 (the PGL convention).
2. **Client-array store** (bridge-side, `store_client_attrib`): the shadow hands the marshalled attribute bytes + the buffer-position offset (`__bb_pos__` probe — arc `Mesh.bind` positions each attribute view) to the bridge; the bridge owns STABLE copies (+4KiB tail — real GL never faults on the trailing stride read), serves `glVertexAttribPointer` pointers from the store, and honors the **Android GLES20 6th-arg law** (VBO bound → the argument is a BYTE OFFSET passed as a number; PGL stores `v->offset = (GLsizeiptr)pointer`).
3. **Vertex type translation** at attrib time (PGL's `pgl_vertex_type_size` rejected spec `0x1406` → INVALID_ENUM → stale attrib layouts).
4. **Draw-time bounds guard**: before every draw, the worst read per ENABLED client attribute (`pos + stride×(last index) + size×type_sz`, indices scanned from the marshalled or real VBO store via `get_glContext()`) is checked; an OOB draw is **SKIPPED with a loud `[C6-DRAWGUARD]` row** — the honest divergence, never a process death, never a silent garbage draw.
5. **Byte-budget marshal**: the flat 65536-element cap is replaced by an 8MiB BYTE budget (element-size aware) — vertex/atlas buffers marshal whole.

**VERIFY:**
```
grep -a "C6-ATTR" <stderr>        # expect: attrib#N store=…B pos=… (bridge stable store)
grep -a "S100-NATIVE-FRAMES" <stderr>   # after the guard: the crash count stays at the guard rows, no do_vertex SIGSEGV
grep -a "C6-DRAWGUARD" <stderr>   # any OOB draw is named loudly with pos/stride/last-index
```

---

## FIX 9 — C6-R6g: view put-THROUGH + parent in-place growth (Mindustry)

**ROOT (live):** `Mindustry MeshBuilder.buildPlanetGrid` fills mesh data through the FLOAT view (`mesh.getVerticesBuffer().put(floats)`): the F-NEW-463 put wrote only the view's own `__bb_b<i>__` fields — the PARENT backing array (the identity the GL marshal chases and PGL reads) stayed ZERO; `FloatBuffer.put(float)` (FLOAT32 args!) and `put([F)` fell through with REC-MISS entirely.

**LAW:** AOSP Buffer semantics — a view SHARES its parent's content: `put(float)/put(int)/put([F)/put([FII)` now write THROUGH `__bb_parent__` into the parent backing `[B` (little-endian) AND keep the view-local `__bb_b<i>__` identity (reads), advancing the view position. **GROWTH:** a write beyond the parent capacity grows the parent IN PLACE (new `[B`, old bytes copied, `__bb_array__/__bb_cap__/__bb_lim__` re-pointed on the SAME parent object — the view's `__bb_parent__` link stays valid; the view's cap/lim grow to match) — bounded 32MiB with a loud `[C6-GROW]` row.

**VERIFY:**
```
grep -a "C6-GROW" <stderr>     # rows appear when a mesh write exceeds the ctor capacity (393216B face)
grep -a "C6-CHASE" <stderr>    # attrib#2/4: argcls=…->[B(__bb_array__)len=393216 hold=397312B — the FULL buffer marshals
```

---

## WAVE-3 QUEUE (the next cars of each train — roots already pinned)

| ID | App | Frontier (live face) | Planned generic law |
|---|---|---|---|
| C6-R8 | VLC | `PackageManager.NameNotFoundException(com.google.android.gsf)` uncaught at `SettingsKt$$ExternalSyntheticApiModelOutline0;.m pc=0` — the R8-synthetic OUTLINE method's try/catch handler is not found by the deferred walk | exception-system: handler search across R8 outline (`$$ExternalSyntheticApiModelOutline`) frames — the try range lives in the CALLER |
| C6-R9 | Termux | static `TermuxAppSharedProperties.properties == null` at `TermuxActivity.reloadProperties pc=2` — the static-holder field was never initialized | class-init: the static holder pattern (SGET of a not-yet-<clinit>'d holder class must trigger the clinit, not answer 0) |
| C6-R10 | Mindustry | `[C6-DRAWGUARD] attrib#1 needs 424880B, store 397312B (pos 96 stride 24 last 17699)` — the planet mesh ctor allocated 393216B (16384 verts) but the draw spans 17700 verts; the ctor-arg bookkeeping (vertexSize×numVertices) needs a DEX-level trace | env-gated trace of the Mesh ctor args (`newUnsafeByteBuffer` cap) + `VertexArray.set` counts; then the ctor/growth law converges with FIX 9's growth |
| C6-R2 | Organic Maps | UnsatisfiedLinkError at `MwmApplication.onCreate` (unchanged — planned) | **Stage G1/G2**: real dlopen of liborganicmaps.so (15.6MB, 442 JNI exports, NEEDED libEGL+libGLESv2+libandroid+liblog) + bionic symbol surface + EGL→PGL |

## Honesty notes
1. Every fix is a generic AOSP/libcore/arc/OpenGL-ES law — zero app-specific code.
2. All four wave-2 preflights are fresh runs at the wave binary (`PREFLIGHT_*_w2*.json`, ×8 files committed in `evidence/c6/`).
3. Frame truth unchanged: no app-authored pixels claimed anywhere yet (the Mindustry draw guard SKIPS the OOB draw loudly instead of drawing garbage — the honest divergence row IS the frontier marker).
4. The complete patch lives in the Coder-6 tree (commit `0e2eabd`, local — the push needs the token's **Contents: read/write** permission; with it, one `git push` transfers everything). Until then this issue IS the transfer document.
5. Regression discipline: wave-2 changes are additive except the marshal byte-budget (kMaxArrayElems 65536 → 8MiB byte budget) — the 99/99 battery + anchor-wall re-run is the scheduled wave-3 opener before any further engine change.

— Coder 6

issues.title: CONT-11 / WAVE 7 — Kotlin stdlib semantic backend investigation + Compose draw frontier
issues.body:
# CONT-11 / WAVE 7 — Kotlin/stdlib semantic backend investigation + Compose draw frontier

## 0. PURPOSE

Do NOT assume the remaining Dooz/Compose blocker is “just another Kotlin root”.

The latest CONT-10 evidence proves two generic Kotlin/collection semantic failures:
- F-NEW-259: Kotlin `ArrayDeque` inherits Kotlin `AbstractList.iterator()`; MiniAndroid's host/shadow iterator resolved `size()/get()` by name only, so R8-renamed overrides were invisible.
- F-NEW-259b: `java.util.ArrayList.addAll(Collection)` was missing and silently became a no-op.

After those fixes, real Compose navigation materializes multiple LayoutNodes, but drawing still stops before framebuffer because the AndroidCanvas bridge is never constructed.

This wave must answer a larger question before adding many more handwritten roots:

**Can MiniAndroid reuse an existing Kotlin/JVM/stdlib implementation, source-derived compatibility layer, host Java implementation, or other open-source runtime component to cover families of Kotlin collection/runtime semantics generically?**

Do not guess. Research first, then prove the smallest reusable path experimentally.

## 1. BASELINE / CURRENT HEAD

Before changes:
- verify remote main HEAD
- verify binary SHA
- rebuild deterministically
- run CONT-10 baseline
- run Dooz fallback-disabled 3x
- preserve current Dooz anchor and opencalc/chess/microtimer/unote controls
- verify CONT-10 probes 7/7 and negatives 19/19

If HEAD differs from the assumed evidence lineage, reconcile first.

## 2. SOURCE-FIRST KOTLIN FORENSICS

Read the actual upstream sources for the pinned APK versions, not generic web summaries.

Required sources:
- Kotlin stdlib version actually present in target APKs
- `kotlin.collections.AbstractList`
- `kotlin.collections.AbstractCollection`
- `kotlin.collections.ArrayDeque`
- `kotlin.collections.ArrayList`
- Map/Set/HashMap/HashSet/LinkedHashMap/LinkedHashSet
- iterators/list iterators
- Collection/Iterable/Sequence operations
- array-to-collection conversion
- equals/hashCode/toArray contracts
- JVM-specific stdlib actualizations
- kotlinx.coroutines version actually present
- Continuation/CoroutineDispatcher/DispatchedContinuation/EventLoop/Flow/StateFlow/collect semantics

For every candidate, record:
SOURCE -> ALGORITHM -> SEMANTIC LAW -> MiniAndroid implementation path -> current divergence.

## 3. CRITICAL RESEARCH QUESTION — CAN WE REUSE INSTEAD OF REIMPLEMENT?

Investigate at least these reuse strategies:

### A. Execute the APK's own Kotlin stdlib DEX correctly
Determine whether the current engine already has enough infrastructure that fixing generic:
- virtual/interface dispatch
- inherited method lookup
- descriptor-slot resolution
- property getter/setter dispatch
- collection copy semantics
- array/object/primitive kind preservation
- iterator contracts
could make most Kotlin stdlib work without a separate Kotlin backend.

This is the preferred hypothesis if source evidence supports it.

### B. Reuse Kotlin/JVM stdlib source or compiled implementation
Investigate whether upstream Kotlin/JVM stdlib source or `kotlin-stdlib.jar` can be reused as a semantic reference/backend.

Do NOT simply execute host JVM objects in place of guest DEX objects unless object identity, class identity, field identity, generic dispatch, exceptions, and guest/host boundary semantics are proven equivalent.

Determine exactly what is reusable:
- source algorithms
- compiled bytecode
- Java collection delegation
- tests/conformance corpus
- selected helper algorithms
- generated/native helper code

### C. Host Java/OpenJDK collection backend
Investigate whether Kotlin/JVM's Java collection paths delegate to `java.util.*` and whether MiniAndroid can safely reuse OpenJDK semantics for selected operations.

OpenJDK `ArrayList.addAll` is a useful reference, but do not blindly substitute host objects.

Required decision:
DIRECT REUSE / ADAPTER / SOURCE-PORT / CURRENT DEX EXECUTION / NOT SAFE.

### D. Existing open-source JVM/DEX runtimes
Search GitHub for reusable execution engines/components:
- DEX interpreters
- Dalvik/ART-compatible interpreters
- JVM bytecode interpreters
- lightweight JVMs
- Kotlin/JVM runtime implementations
- Android compatibility runtimes
- collection/stdlib semantic test suites

Prioritize local/CPU/open-source/no-server/no-GPU projects.

Explicitly inspect relevant projects such as AndroidRecomp, DroidVM, Skydnir, droidsaw and any stronger DEX/JVM runtime you discover. Do not force unrelated projects into the solution: classify each as REUSABLE / REFERENCE-ONLY / IRRELEVANT.

### E. Kotlin coroutines reuse
Separate this from collections.

Investigate whether `kotlinx.coroutines` source/compiled runtime can be executed unchanged by MiniAndroid once generic dispatch/thread/event-loop/continuation semantics are correct.

Do NOT replace coroutines with fake immediate execution.

## 4. BUILD A KOTLIN SEMANTIC COVERAGE MATRIX

Mine representative APKs and the current corpus.

At minimum classify:
- ArrayList
- ArrayDeque
- LinkedList
- HashMap
- LinkedHashMap
- HashSet
- LinkedHashSet
- Collections.unmodifiable/singleton/empty
- MutableCollection/MutableList defaults
- iterator/listIterator
- add/addAll/removeAll/retainAll
- contains/containsAll
- filter/map/flatMap
- first/last/lastOrNull
- sequence operations
- toArray
- equals/hashCode
- ranges/indices
- Pair/Triple
- lazy/delegates
- Result/Unit/Intrinsics
- Function/Lambda/SAM bridges
- suspend Continuation
- CoroutineDispatcher
- DispatchedContinuation
- EventLoop
- Flow/StateFlow
- cancellation
- delay/scheduling

For each:
CURRENTLY EXECUTES / PARTIAL / SILENT-NO-OP / WRONG / MISSING / BLOCKED.

Do not create one root per method. Collapse by semantic law.

## 5. RESEARCH THE CURRENT F-NEW-259/F-NEW-259b FIXES FOR GENERALITY

Audit the actual implementation added in CONT-10.

Prove whether:
- descriptor-slot fallback is truly generic for inherited R8-renamed overrides
- it works for non-collection classes
- it works for multiple inheritance/interface/default-method shapes
- bounded superclass walking is semantically correct
- it cannot select the wrong override
- it preserves declaring-class identity
- it works for primitive/boxed/array return types
- addAll copy preserves STRING/INT/OBJECT/ARRAY kinds
- addAll works guest->guest and guest->host/shadow boundaries without identity loss

Create focused positive and negative probes.

If the mechanism itself is the real reusable Kotlin solution, prefer extending that generic mechanism over adding a “Kotlin backend”.

## 6. CURRENT FIRST DIVERGENCE — ANDROIDCANVAS

After CONT-10 fixes, trace the remaining Dooz path:

NavHost
-> LayoutNode tree
-> measure
-> layout
-> layer/drawContent
-> AndroidCanvas bridge
-> Canvas operations
-> Surface/buffer
-> framebuffer

Find the FIRST point where upstream Compose 1.11.4 behavior differs.

Required:
- exact upstream source method
- exact R8-mapped MiniAndroid method/class
- entry/exit trace
- receiver identity
- arguments
- return value
- state before/after
- why AndroidCanvas is not constructed
- whether the cause is Kotlin collection/runtime, Compose runtime, Android graphics bridge, or dispatch/reflection.

Do not patch Canvas merely to produce pixels.

## 7. DO NOT REPEAT THE OLD FALSE ROOTS

Explicitly test and rule out:
- “ComposableLambda is never reinvoked”
- LifecycleRegistry as the current blocker
- ViewTreeLifecycleOwner missing
- coroutine parent=0
- instruction budget too small
- Dooz-specific R8 class names
- hardcoded fallback rendering

The latest CONT-10 evidence already corrected the first three historical interpretations.

## 8. REAL APK FAN-OUT

Use:
1. Dooz original APK, fallback disabled
2. Sudoku/SudokuSolver Compose APK
3. one additional independent Compose APK
4. one non-Compose Kotlin/R8 app
5. one Kotlin-heavy game/app from the corpus

For each:
APK SHA
ABI/preflight
Kotlin version
Compose/coroutines versions if present
first divergence
semantic cluster
before/after
3 clean runs
pixel/state evidence.

A fix is not generic unless an independent consumer benefits.

## 9. KOTLIN REUSE DECISION

Produce a hard decision matrix:

| Candidate | What is reusable | Integration point | Guest identity safe? | R8 safe? | Generic? | License | CPU/local | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

Possible verdicts:
- USE DIRECTLY
- USE THROUGH ADAPTER
- PORT SOURCE ALGORITHMS
- USE AS CONFORMANCE ORACLE
- REFERENCE ONLY
- REJECT

Do not introduce a large external runtime unless evidence shows it is smaller and safer than fixing MiniAndroid's existing generic execution semantics.

## 10. REQUIRED TEST ARTIFACTS

Create focused probes for:
- inherited R8-renamed collection iterator
- addAll for empty/non-empty
- addAll order preservation
- primitive/string/object/array element fidelity
- HashMap/HashSet iteration
- LinkedHashMap order
- ArrayDeque wrap-around
- iterator mutation/termination
- nested inherited dispatch
- coroutine continuation resume
- dispatcher no-dispatch/immediate path
- Flow/StateFlow emission and conflation
- delay/event-loop scheduling

Each must have positive + negative cases.

## 11. REGRESSION

After every generic fix:
- synthetic probe
- target real APK
- independent app/game
- anchors 5/5 x3
- negatives 19/19
- skill 13/13
- relevant CONT-10 probes
- Dooz 3x
- no hidden fallback.

## 12. EVIDENCE / AUDIT CHECKLIST

Update the consolidated ledger line-by-line:

- [ ] upstream Kotlin source read
- [ ] Kotlin version pinned
- [ ] JVM stdlib source read
- [ ] OpenJDK reference read
- [ ] coroutines source read
- [ ] existing runtime/tool candidates searched
- [ ] reusable components classified
- [ ] current implementation audited
- [ ] semantic clusters formed
- [ ] synthetic positive
- [ ] synthetic negative
- [ ] real APK
- [ ] independent consumer
- [ ] 3-run
- [ ] regression
- [ ] first divergence
- [ ] evidence artifact
- [ ] registry overlap checked
- [ ] no app-specific patch
- [ ] no bulk registry inflation

Use statuses:
IMPLEMENTED / TESTED / OBSERVED / PARTIAL / BLOCKED / PENDING / SUPERSEDED.

## 13. DEFINITION OF DONE

Do not stop at “Kotlin root found”.

Done requires:
1. A source-backed decision on whether a reusable Kotlin/JVM/stdlib backend is technically viable.
2. A source-backed decision on whether current MiniAndroid generic dispatch/collection semantics are the better reuse mechanism.
3. At least one high-ROI generic Kotlin semantic improvement proven on a real APK.
4. Current Dooz first draw divergence identified precisely.
5. At least one independent consumer benefits, or exact external prerequisite is proven.
6. No host-object substitution that breaks guest identity.
7. No Kotlin-name/R8-name allow-list.
8. No fake coroutine execution.
9. No fallback pixels counted as compatibility.
10. All evidence committed and pushed.

## FINAL REPORT

### A. KOTLIN REUSE
What exists upstream:
What can be reused:
What cannot:
Best architecture:

### B. COLLECTION SEMANTICS

Current coverage:
Missing generic laws:

### E. REGRESSION

### F. NEXT SINGLE HIGHEST-ROI ROOT
State one root only, with source + runtime evidence.

NO-GO:
- no app-specific Kotlin patches
- no R8-name tables
- no fake coroutine scheduler
- no host object identity substitution without proof
- no hardcoded Compose pixels
- no budget inflation
- no bulk external-KB root import

issues.body:
# Authoritative execution contract

This Issue is now the **active master request** for the MiniAndroid compatibility campaign. All Coders/Agents may contribute here.

## Mandatory rule
Do not declare this request complete merely because code was changed or tests passed. Completion requires:
1. execute every applicable requirement below;
2. record evidence/results in comments;
3. unresolved items remain explicitly OPEN/PARTIAL/BLOCKED/PENDING;
4. a final reviewer must verify the evidence before the issue may be closed.

## Work protocol
Read first: `CONSTITUTION_V2.md`, current worklog/state/mission/backlog, compatibility campaign docs, previous request ledgers, and relevant upstream/vendor sources.

Operate:
**OBSERVE → MEASURE → UNDERSTAND → HYPOTHESIZE → EXPERIMENT → IMPLEMENT → VERIFY → CONTINUE**

Prefer:
**AOSP source/semantics → maintained compatible OSS → adapter/port → MiniAndroid-specific code**

No package-specific hacks.

## Required campaign
- Audit what upstream code MiniAndroid already uses.
- Search for maintained upstream/OSS implementations that can replace custom implementations.
- Audit resources/APK loading, File/path/storage, streams, AssetManager, FD/PFD/AFD, Context storage APIs, configuration/qualifiers, BitmapFactory/decodeStream, URI/ContentProvider, SharedPreferences, SQLite, Java/libcore/DEX/runtime, graphics/text, native/media/WebView where relevant.
- Explain why currently working apps work and why failing/blank/grey/splash/settings cases fail.
- Trace first divergence, not just the final exception.
- Fix generic high-fan-out roots before app-specific symptoms.
- Add synthetic probes for APIs not naturally exercised.
- Prove real APK behavior with installed identity where applicable.
- Important cases require 3-run reproducibility, screenshot metrics/SHA, runtime trace, state change, actual consumer/provenance.
- Run corpus regression after generic fixes.
- Close host filesystem escapes and fake-success paths.
- Keep docs, registry, worklog and evidence synchronized.

## Mandatory outputs
Maintain/update as applicable:
- `docs/UPSTREAM_CODE_INVENTORY.md`
- `docs/UPSTREAM_CODE_INVENTORY.jsonl`
- `docs/UPSTREAM_AVAILABLE_NOT_USED.jsonl`
- `docs/UPSTREAM_REPLACEMENT_PLAN.jsonl`
- `docs/UPSTREAM_LICENSE_MATRIX.jsonl`
- `docs/UPSTREAM_RUNTIME_USAGE.jsonl`
- `docs/UPSTREAM_UPDATE_TRACKING.jsonl`
- `docs/WORKING_APP_LOADING_EXPLANATIONS.md`
- `docs/WHITE_SCREEN_LOADING_ROOTS.md`
- `docs/LOADING_FAILURE_DIAGNOSTICS.md`
- `docs/WORKING_VS_FAILING_LOADING_MATRIX.jsonl`
- `docs/FINAL_COMPATIBILITY_CAMPAIGN.md`
- appropriate runtime trace/provenance/evidence JSONL files.

## Carry-over requirements
Do not lose unfinished work from earlier campaigns, including:
- File/path semantics and canonical path mapping;
- Context file APIs and stream read/write/list/delete;
- AssetManager real open/list/openFd/openNonAsset semantics and missing-file contracts;
- FD/PFD/AFD/openFd/openRawResourceFd;
- resource configuration/qualifier/density selection;
- decodeResource/decodeFile/decodeStream/decodeByteArray;
- URI/content-provider/provider installation;
- SharedPreferences semantics;
- SQLite path/WAL/transactions/reopen;
- native library/font/audio/media loading where exercised;
- package isolation/uninstall/reinstall;
- lifecycle/Fragment/component-resolution backlog P0–P3;
- all previous white/blank/grey/splash/settings/Compose/WebView findings;
- explain the working golden apps rather than assuming every blank is a file bug.

## Completion ledger
Every applicable item must receive a one-line status + evidence in comments or linked repository evidence:

1. Laws read.
2. Upstream inventory complete.
3. Available-but-unused search complete.
4. Duplicate/custom implementation audit complete.
5. License/attribution audit complete.
6. Maintenance/update-path audit complete.
7. Resource/APK loading audit/fixes.
8. File/storage/path audit/fixes.
9. Stream audit/fixes.
10. FD/PFD/AFD audit/fixes.
11. URI/provider audit/fixes.
12. SharedPreferences audit/fixes.
13. SQLite audit/fixes.
14. Java/libcore audit/fixes.
15. DEX/runtime audit/fixes.
16. Graphics/text audit/fixes.
17. Working-app explanations.
18. White/blank/grey/splash failure tracing.
19. Previous backlog P0 rechecked.
20. Previous backlog P1 rechecked.
21. Previous backlog P2 rechecked.
22. Previous backlog P3 rechecked.
23. Previous loading campaign coverage rechecked.
24. Previous upstream campaign coverage rechecked.
25. High-fan-out implementation/porting.
26. Synthetic probes.
27. Real APK tests.
28. 3-run reproducibility.
29. Corpus regression.
30. Attribution/licenses/notices.
31. Upstream update strategy.
32. Justification for remaining custom code.
33. Final repository synchronization + remote HEAD verification.

### Final gate
No one may state **DONE / COMPLETE / FULL COMPATIBILITY** unless all applicable ledger rows have a non-empty status, evidence, and explanation. If something is blocked, say exactly what blocks it and what evidence proves the block.

### Collaboration
This issue is intentionally shared: a later Coder may continue unfinished rows left by an earlier Coder. Every contributor must first inspect the current issue comments and repository state, then update the same ledger/evidence rather than creating a disconnected competing plan.

## Current priority
Start from high-fan-out runtime/resource/storage/loading roots and the upstream-reuse audit, then continue through the carry-over campaign and regression gate. Do not stop after the first successful fix.

issues.title: S81 — REAL APP VISUAL COMPATIBILITY: audit ladder, VF fixes, 200-item F-Droid corpus + BATCH-01
issues.body:
## S81 wave — visual compatibility campaign (status: CORPUS_READY, EXECUTION_PARTIAL)

New law this wave (S81 §1/§52): **EXECUTED ≠ VISUALLY COMPATIBLE**. Status ladder L0 LOADED_ONLY → L1 NONBLANK → L2 GRAPHICALLY_NONTRIVIAL → L3 STRUCT_CANDIDATE → L4 SEMANTICALLY_CORRELATED → L5 VISUALLY_VERIFIED (L5 requires human review, never self-granted). Methodology + thresholds: `scripts/s81_visual_audit.py` (no single fake overall score, §36).

### Visual audit of the existing ladder (18 APKs at HEAD)

| Result | Detail |
|---|---|
| Only S80's own games reach L3 | Snake Deluxe, Mini Tetris (82/70 uniq colors, ICON_PRESENT) |
| Zero curated third-party apps reach L3 | gmdice dom=0.91 MONOCHROME_LIKE, Notes uniq=6, Simple Keyboard uniq=2, Dooz uniq=2 |
| 7 apps flag `IMAGE_DECODED_VS_RENDERED_GAP` | APK ships 24–32 rasters, screen shows 0 image/icon pixels |
| 7 prior HUMAN_VISIBLE statuses DOWNGRADED per §39 | honest re-classification, recorded in `docs/audit/APP_MATRIX.md` |

Report: `run/s81_audit/s81_visual_report.json` + evidence JPGs in `docs/evidence/s81/`.

### Root-caused + FIXED (visual failure registry VF-*, §42/§43 workflow)

**VF-NEW-001 / VF-DIALOG-ITEMS** — `AlertDialog$Builder.setItems` dropped the item array (probe-proven: dialog painted title+message, `items=0`).
- Root cause: DialogShadow recorded only the listener; array never materialized.
- Fix (AOSP law): heap array elements materialized into the builder window in BOTH dispatch layers (`try_shadow_dispatch` + `bridge_to_api`, same dual-view shape as R-NEW-339).
- Observed: `materialized 3/3 items`, dialog 920x144→920x408, ITEM-A/B/C rows painted with dividers.
- Evidence: `probe_dialog_items_BEFORE_fix.jpg` / `probe_dialog_items_AFTER_fix.jpg`.

**VF-NEW-002 / VF-PLACEHOLDER-GARBLE** — C013-CUSTOMVIEW placeholder painted the raw class descriptor (`Lorg.billthefarmer.markdown.MarkdownView`) over full-screen regions — this WAS the user-visible garbled text in Notes + Simple Stopwatch screenshots.
- Fix: neutral small `custom view (not rendered)` marker at bottom-left; class name kept in stderr trace only.
- Evidence: `notes_garble_BEFORE_fix_crop.jpg` vs `notes_AFTER_fix.jpg`, `stopwatch_AFTER_fix.jpg`.

### Regression (final binary)

battery 26/26 rc=0 · fidelity BYTE-IDENTICAL 90/90 · f152 6/6 · f153 3/3 · spot pixel-golden verifier 4/4. Zero golden deltas from VF fixes.

### 200-item F-Droid corpus (§4–§15, §31)

`docs/corpus/s81/corpus_index.json` (+CSV): CORPUS_SEED recorded, deterministic selection.
- **Mandatory §7 with full provenance**: P9 `se.tube42.p9.android` v0.1.1 (vc11), source https://github.com/tube42/9p ; TimeLimit `io.timelimit.android.aosp.direct` v7.7.1 (vc231), source https://codeberg.org/timelimit/timelimit-android — both with F-Droid reference-screenshot URLs (REFERENCE provenance recorded). Status: DISCOVERED (not yet executed — honest).
- Stopwatch inventory: 16 packages (§8). Platformer inventory: 10 packages (§9).
- **100 GAMES + 100 APPS** selected from live F-Droid category slugs (puzzle/board/card/action/casual/platformer/shooter/educational-game; calculator/clock/file-manager/gallery/multimedia/weather/connectivity/reading/internet/security/development/navigation/stopwatch).
- Batch plan: 4 × 25 mixed batches (§13/§14).

### BATCH-01 (25 fresh F-Droid APKs, mixed subset — §13/§14/§32)

- 20/25 RENDERED, 1 RENDERED_PARTIAL, 4 loaded-only, 1 download-fail. Disk before 5.8G avail → after 5.1G (guard respected, §32/§34).
- **Key honest finding (F-NEW-156)**: the dominant fresh-corpus frontier is the **onCreate APP BOUNDARY unwind family** — a first NPE inside app `onCreate` (e.g. solitaire `GameSelector.onCreate` invoke#3, heading-calculator `MainActivity.onCreate` invoke#6) unwinds the process → blank two-color screen. 19/25 fresh apps hit this family. These are NEW frontiers, individually queued for the §43 chain (reproduce → producer trace → root cause → law → fix).
- Report: `run/s81_batch01/batch01_report.json` (per-APK SHA256, sizes, statuses, visual metrics).

### Missing capabilities / next wave

1. F-NEW-156 onCreate-unwind family: per-app first-NPE disasm (`scripts/s81_disasm_probe.py`).
2. IMAGE_DECODED_VS_RENDERED_GAP: programmatic `setImageResource` → pixels proven at EXP-067, but XML-src/complex chains still drop (7 flagged apps).
3. P9 + TimeLimit: build/run + reference-vs-MiniAndroid comparison (L4/L5 needs reference screenshots side-by-side, §16-§19).
4. BATCH-02..04.

### Evidence

`docs/evidence/s81/` (SHA256SUMS): 12 JPGs ≤100KB (before/after both fixes, audit flagships, batch samples), corpus index+CSV, batch report, visual report. Scripts: `s81_visual_audit.py`, `s81_run_and_audit.py`, `s81_fdroid_corpus.py`, `s81_batch01.py`, `s81_disasm_probe.py`, fixture `fixtures/s81_visual_probe/`.

### Current status

CORPUS_READY · EXECUTION_PARTIAL (not "200_APPS_VERIFIED" — §51). Visual fixes regression-proven. No claim of VISUALLY_VERIFIED anywhere: L5 awaits human review with reference+MiniAndroid side by side (§48).


---

Every title below owns an independent, permanent compatibility-record issue (S82 §2/§5). Issue #24 remains the wave/campaign umbrella only. Root causes are separate issues: F-NEW-156 → #227, F-NEW-157 (libGDX/P9) → #228, VF-NEW-003 (IMAGE_DECODED_VS_RENDERED_GAP) → #229. issues.title: [F-NEW-170] appcompat decor-toolbar construction family (mykanji, post theme-gate fix)
issues.body:
## [F-NEW-170] appcompat decor-toolbar construction family (mykanji, post theme-gate fix)

With the theme-gate ISE fixed (#342), MyKanji's createSubDecor now proceeds
into appcompat's action-bar VIEW machinery and dies there:

| ISE | Site |
|-----|------|
| "Can't make a decor toolbar out of Toolbar" | `ActionBarOverlayLayout.getDecorToolbar pc=42` |
| "Can't make a decor toolbar out of null" | `WindowDecorActionBar.getDecorToolbar pc=47` |

## Hypothesis (to verify, not assume)
`createSubDecor` inflates `abc_screen_toolbar.xml` (which has an `<include>` +

issues.title: Coder 3 | Achievement 7 — FULL LOAD wave: F-NEW-162 subclass law + honest-surface law + Dodge/BobBall/Hot Death interactive full loads
issues.body:
# Coder 3 | Achievement 7 — FULL LOAD wave: F-NEW-162 subclass law + honest-surface law + three interactive full loads (Dodge / BobBall / Hot Death)

> Chain: #415 (master board) · #416–#420 (achievements 1–6) · case files #391–#414
> Governing law: **no fake success** — every number below comes from this session's own run artifacts.
> User directive for this wave: *«let's try to make at least a few of the apps run FULLY — the screen must load completely, not partially»* — translated: at least a few apps must reach a complete, full-screen load.

---

## 1) The F-NEW-162 root found and fixed (engine law, generic)

**The bug**: `stage_gl_surfaces` and `dispatch_gl_surface_view_frame` selected GLSurfaceView nodes by a **substring test** (`class_desc.find("GLSurfaceView")`). Direct holders (libGDX `GLSurfaceView20`) passed; **real app subclasses whose own name does not embed the base name** (bouncy `Lcom/dozingcatsoftware/bouncy/GLFieldView;`) fell through — the composite walk suppressed their placeholder as "owned by the surface pipeline" while no surface pipeline ever ran for them: a permanent invisible-surface hole.

**The fix (two sites, one law)**: surface-family membership resolved through the DEX superclass chain (`is_subclass_of`, R-NEW-530 memoized), exactly like the sibling `dispatch_surface_view_lifecycle`:
- `execution_engine.cpp` `stage_gl_surfaces` — `is_subclass_of(node_class, "Landroid/opengl/GLSurfaceView;")`
- `dalvik_engine.cpp` `dispatch_gl_surface_view_frame` — the same subclass law, preferring the runtime object class.

**Measured result (bouncy, this session)**: GLFieldView now enters the pass every frame and its REAL renderer runs via real DEX:
- `doStartGame` → `result=DISPATCHED`; `setRenderer` dispatched via the superclass chain (receiver `Lcom/dozingcatsoftware/bouncy/GLFieldView;` → `Landroid/opengl/GLSurfaceView;`)
- renderer object resolved: `GL20Renderer` (obj#257) — **126 renderer dispatches across the 3×40-frame runs (42/run)**
- real app work executed inside the callbacks: `shaders/circle.vert/.frag`, `shaders/line.vert/.frag` loaded from the APK assets, `GL20Renderer.makeByteBuffer/makeIntBuffer` executed, GLES20 calls marshalled into PortableGL.

## 2) The honest-surface law (new evidence-integrity rule)

A foreign writer (running under a SEGV-swallowing guard — mechanism named, exact frame still open) fills the fresh GL surface buffer with a **recent view-tree render of the view's region** during `GLSurfaceView.onSurfaceCreated`. Presenting that as "GL content" would be false evidence — the same class of lie the C013 law already forbids for placeholders.

**Law landed** (`stage_gl_surfaces`): snapshot the surface before the callbacks (S0) and after the draw frame (S1); classify:
- S1 ≈ the framebuffer's view region (≥55% sampled pixel match — lagged foreign copies measured at ~74%, genuine GL output stays far below) → **foreign copy, NOT presented**, event `GL_FRAME_PRESENT/PENDING` recorded;
- S1 == S0 with no prior content → **honest empty surface**, not presented;
- otherwise → present (real renderer output).

**Measured**: bouncy 3×40 frames → **126/126 foreign copies suppressed**, zero false presentations. The on-screen field region therefore shows only what the 2D view pipeline lawfully draws.

## 3) The bouncy ceiling, named honestly

Bouncy's field renderer drives **GLES20 with custom GLSL** (`shaders/circle.vert/.frag`, `line.vert/.frag`). The GLES20 bridge stores GLSL but does not execute it (`glsl-not-compiled-by-pgl` honesty note) and ES-constant calls error on PGL 3.x core (`GL_INVALID_ENUM/VALUE`). The pinball table can only rasterize after the **GLSL→software translation frontier** lands — registered as the blocker; menu / score bar / High scores / Help remain fully loaded (S130/#420).

## 4) FULL LOAD sweep — three more apps loaded completely and interactively (real APKs, SHA256-registered)

Four APKs fetched fresh from F-Droid this session (identity law):

| App | APK | SHA256 |
