issues.title: REPO-HYGIENE — Evidence-Driven Repository Cleanup, Artifact Governance, and Canonical Structure
issues.body:
## Mission

Perform a repository-wide, evidence-driven **Repository Hygiene, Artifact Governance, and Canonical Structure Standardization** for `Sh-TB/MiniAndroid-Compatibility-Runtime`.

The repository must remain a professional, reproducible **source-code + essential tools + tests/fixtures + canonical technical knowledge + carefully selected proof evidence** project. It must not become a storage dump for temporary build trees, extracted/decompiled APK contents, raw API exports, caches, duplicate dependency distributions, arbitrary screenshots, or generated JSON.

This is a controlled engineering migration, **not** a blind deletion/renaming exercise. The result must be easier to understand, clone, bootstrap, build, test, audit, and contribute to, without breaking runtime behavior, evidence traceability, scripts, tests, CI, or historical claims.

## Non-negotiable rules

1. **Inspect before modifying.** Read the repository constitution/contribution rules, README, `docs/ARTIFACT_LIFECYCLE.md`, `.gitignore`, `tools/check_repo_hygiene.py`, bootstrap/build/test scripts, CI workflows, canonical registries, and references to candidate paths.
2. **No mass deletion by extension or directory name.** A `.json`, `.png`, `.jar`, `.zip`, `.dex`, `.xml`, `.kt`, or `.txt` file is not disposable merely because of its extension. Classify its role and prove whether it is required.
3. **Do not break runtime compatibility.** Keep runtime source, essential Android framework/resource data, small intentional fixtures, reproducible build/bootstrap logic, and canonical source-law/knowledge data needed by the project.
4. **No APK/AAB, extracted app DEX/classes/resources, decompiled app trees, transient disassembly, local databases/WAL/SHM, caches, generated binaries, or temporary build trees in Git** unless an explicit, documented test/fixture exception is approved and minimized.
5. **Do not externalize/delete toolchain or upstream dependencies until reproducibility is proven.** For every retained external dependency, document source URL, exact version, license, SHA-256, retrieval method, and expected location. Test bootstrap from a clean environment before removing tracked copies.
6. **Do not rewrite Git history, force-push, or purge historical blobs in this issue.** History cleanup is a separate, explicitly approved migration with a backup, collaborator coordination, and before/after measurements.
7. **Do not invent measurements or claim success from a script exit code alone.** Record commands, environment, exit status, relevant output, commit SHA, and evidence paths. Distinguish measured facts from estimates.
8. **No project-specific compatibility regressions or app-specific hacks.** Hygiene changes must not change runtime semantics. If a cleanup requires a source/build change, isolate it and prove equivalence.
9. Preserve existing paths initially where moving them would create broad breakage. Relocate in small batches with references updated atomically and tests run after each batch.
10. The issue is complete only after the line-by-line checklist at the bottom has an explicit status and evidence for every item. “Done”, “cleaned”, or “tests pass” without proof is not closure.

## Known baseline to verify, not assume

A prior tree audit reported approximately 14,896 tracked blobs and these notable areas: `tmp/` (~1,392 files / 96.44 MiB), `upstream/` (~2,937 / 253.68 MiB), `tools/` (~66 / 107.52 MiB), `docs/` (~3,346 / 87.56 MiB), `miniandroid/` (~2,010 / 80.36 MiB), `evidence/` (~2,888 / 26.39 MiB), `docs/evidence/` (~2,263 / 43.07 MiB), `apk_build/` (~466 / 6.95 MiB), and `run/` (~17 / 1.72 MiB). The tree reportedly contained 3,045 JSON files (~76.78 MiB), 2,009 PNGs (~40.95 MiB), 70 DEX files (~69.19 MiB), 148 JARs (~224.43 MiB), and 36 ZIPs (~84.10 MiB).

Previously observed candidates included `miniandroid/a.out`, `tools/toolchain/`, duplicate Android 34 JAR paths, `tmp/cont12_b1/`, `tmp/cont12_oracle_build/`, `tmp/cont32/`, `tmp/s117_dataroot/`, raw `forensic_data/*` GitHub exports, extracted content in `corpus_cache/`, root-level WAL/SHM and probe outputs, and duplicated/large census JSON. These figures and examples are **leads only**: recalculate against the actual current HEAD and verify every path before acting. They are not authorization to delete any specific file.

A previous audit did **not** measure a fresh clone's actual `.git` size. Measure it; do not present working-tree byte totals as Git history savings.

## LIVE AUDIT ADDENDUM — 2026-10-15 (measured from current GitHub main)

This section supersedes neither the original baseline nor the safety rules. It records a fresh, read-only inventory of the current tree and turns observed inconsistencies into explicit work. Measurements below came from the recursive Git tree for HEAD `3d7227ddd98d910779cae3592b89a8fd35794879`; they are not a local clean-clone measurement.

### A. Current measured baseline

- Current HEAD/tree: `3d7227ddd98d910779cae3592b89a8fd35794879`.
- Recursive tree entries: **17,161**; tracked blob paths: **13,247**.
- Sum of per-path uncompressed blob sizes: **572,954,099 bytes / 546.41 MiB**. This counts each path, including repeated content.
- GitHub repository metadata reports `size=533098 KB` (about **520.6 MiB**). This is GitHub's repository-size field, **not** a verified local `.git` directory size.
- A fresh clone's checkout size and `.git` size remain **NOT MEASURED**. Do not infer them from the two figures above.
- Compared with the older audit's reported 14,896 tracked blobs, the current tree has 1,649 fewer paths (about 11.1% fewer), subject to confirming both audits used the same counting method. This does **not** mean repository hygiene is complete.

### B. Current high-priority findings (path-level evidence)

| Area | Current measurement | Audit implication / required disposition |
|---|---:|---|
| `upstream/cont12_maven/` | 632 paths / 232.90 MiB | Largest subtree. Separate required pinned runtime/build dependencies from compiler distributions, duplicate raw AAR/JAR payloads and extracted dependency trees. No bulk deletion. |
| `tools/toolchain/` | 4 paths / 81.89 MiB | Toolchain binaries are still tracked despite the repository's own `.gitignore` rule for `tools/toolchain/`. Determine exact bootstrap consumers and prove clean bootstrap before externalizing. |
| `tools/android-34/android-34.jar` and `tools/toolchain/android-34.jar` | Same blob SHA; 25.14 MiB per path | Confirm one canonical location and update all references. Removing a duplicate path may reduce checkout footprint, but does not by itself reclaim a second copy of the same Git blob from object storage. |
| `docs/evidence/` | 2,263 paths / 43.07 MiB | This matches the earlier count. Audit repeated screenshots/traces by provenance and canonical report references; same SHA alone is not permission to delete distinct run evidence. |
| `evidence/` | 2,988 paths / 30.57 MiB | Compared with the older reported 2,888 / 26.39 MiB, this is +100 paths and +4.18 MiB. Explain the increase by campaign, prove every retained artifact is referenced, and distinguish necessary run identity from redundant copies. |
| `docs/foundation/` | 61 paths / 23.93 MiB | Large JSON/census/knowledge data needs ownership, generation recipe, consumers and canonical-source declaration. Keep runtime-required data. |
| `miniandroid/framework_res/` | 1,123 paths / 20.02 MiB | Likely runtime-critical framework resource data; preserve unless a byte-identical, tested canonical replacement is proven. |
| `forensic_data/` | 233 paths / 8.29 MiB | Includes raw exports such as `issues_all.json` (2.77 MiB), `all_issue_comments.json` (2.41 MiB), and `commits.json` (1.35 MiB). Replace raw snapshots with stable IDs/links plus compact curated findings or reproducible fetch scripts where safe. |
| Repository root | `1` (491,299 bytes), `MessageSchema.java` (188,187 bytes) | Root-level files lack an obvious canonical role from their paths. Identify provenance, licensing, references and owner; classify as KEEP/MOVE/REGENERATE/EXTERNALIZE/REMOVE only after verification. |
| `tmp/` | 14 paths / 0.04 MiB | Much smaller than the old reported 1,392 paths / 96.44 MiB, but it still contains tracked generated build outputs under `tmp/capaudit_build/` and `tmp/f352_build/` (classes, DEX, generated R.java, res.zip). Confirm no required test consumes these outputs; preserve fixture source and deterministic regeneration recipe. |
| Python bytecode / compiled classes / DEX | 14 `.pyc`, 16 `.class`, 32 `.dex` paths | Classify each individually. Some DEX files may be intentional interpreter fixtures; tracked `__pycache__`, generated `build/classes`, and extracted duplicates are presumptive hygiene violations until proven necessary. |
| Archives | 3 tracked `.zip` paths, 82.91 MiB total | `fixtures/fnew253_probe/build/res.zip`, `tmp/capaudit_build/res.zip`, and `upstream/cont12_maven/kotlinc-2.1.20.zip`. The current hygiene checker has an empty archive allowlist and says all tracked ZIPs fail, so the current tracked tree should fail that rule. Classify each and test the gate. |
| Extension totals | 147 JAR / 224.26 MiB; 54 AAR / 23.88 MiB; 2,813 JSON / 75.06 MiB; 1,873 PNG / 37.97 MiB; 1 ARSC / 18.91 MiB | Treat these as audit queues, not deletion targets. The ARSC and required framework data may be runtime-critical; JSON and screenshots require semantic/provenance review. |

### C. Duplicate-content facts — do not misrepresent savings

The current tree contains **1,085 groups of paths sharing identical Git blob SHA**, involving **3,403 extra path occurrences**. Summing the bytes at those extra paths gives about **70.87 MiB of repeated checkout-path content**. This is a path/checkout metric only, **not** an estimate of `.git` savings: Git stores identical blob content once, and history retention is separate. Many identical screenshots are deliberately repeated under run-specific evidence directories; preserve run identity unless the canonical evidence model proves the copies are redundant.

### D. Hygiene-checker enforcement gap

The current `tools/check_repo_hygiene.py`:
- bans tracked ZIPs and has an empty `ARCHIVE_WHITELIST`, yet the current tree contains three ZIPs;
- rejects tracked files over 5 MiB unless explicitly allowlisted, yet the current tree contains large files such as `upstream/cont12_maven/kotlinc-2.1.20.zip`, `tools/toolchain/r8.jar`, and both Android 34 JAR paths that are not covered by the exact current allowlist entries;
- does not explicitly reject tracked `.pyc`, generated `.class`, extracted/generated `.dex`, or `__pycache__` paths as their own classes;
- cannot rely on `.gitignore` to remove already tracked files.

Therefore, do not report the current repository as hygiene-clean until the checker is run at this exact HEAD, its real output is recorded, its rules are reconciled with the tree, and positive/negative tests prove that intentional fixtures are retained while generated residue is caught. A checker PASS must not be fabricated from reading the code.

### E. Required next actions from this live audit

1. Re-run the current hygiene checker and capture exact command, exit code, and complete actionable findings.
2. Produce a path-by-path decision register for every tracked file under `tools/toolchain/`, `upstream/cont12_maven/`, `tmp/`, `forensic_data/`, all tracked `__pycache__/` paths, all generated `build/` paths, all ZIPs, and root-level unexplained files.
3. Prove which duplicate JAR/AAR/compiler artifacts are consumed by build/test scripts; add pinned version, URL, license, SHA-256, download/cache policy and clean-room bootstrap proof before removing any dependency copy.
4. Build an evidence-retention map: each retained screenshot/trace must point to one named test/run/report and preserve run identity; identify unreferenced, superseded and truly redundant files separately.
5. Measure baseline and final working tree, clean checkout and `.git` directory separately with reproducible commands; record Git version and clone mode. Do not claim history savings without a separately approved history migration.
6. Reconcile the registry/worklist copies and root-level mutable status files. Each data family must name exactly one canonical source of truth plus any generated read models and regeneration command.
7. Make cleanup reversible and incremental. Do not perform mass deletion, move large directories, rewrite Git history, or force-push as part of this issue.

## Required phases

### Phase 0 — Rules, current HEAD, and safe baseline

- [ ] Record repository URL, branch, current HEAD SHA, working-tree status, and whether any user changes are present. Do not overwrite uncommitted work.
- [ ] Read the project constitution, README, artifact lifecycle policy, contributor/agent instructions, hygiene checker, build/bootstrap scripts, tests, CI workflows, and canonical state/worklist files.
- [ ] Create a machine-readable inventory of every tracked path: path, blob SHA, bytes, extension, top-level owner, file type, likely role, generated/source status, and classification confidence.
- [ ] Record largest files, largest directories, extension totals, duplicate-content groups by SHA, and path-level references from scripts/tests/docs/CI.
- [ ] Measure a clean checkout's working-tree size and `.git` size separately. Record method, Git version, compression/clone mode, and whether LFS/submodules are involved.
- [ ] Save baseline test/build/hygiene results and hashes for critical binaries/artifacts. Use a disposable clean worktree or separate clone where feasible.
- [ ] Write a concise baseline report before deleting, moving, or rewriting anything.

### Phase 1 — File-by-file classification and decision register

Classify every tracked path into exactly one primary category:

- **A — Runtime/source of truth:** runtime source, configuration, required framework resources.
- **B — Essential build/tooling source:** scripts, small tool source, pinned manifests, bootstrap logic.
- **C — Tests and intentional fixtures:** minimal deterministic fixtures required by tests.
- **D — Canonical knowledge/registry:** curated Android source laws, architecture/ADR documents, root registries, worklists, API matrices, selected census data.
- **E — Canonical evidence:** minimal reports/traces/screenshots that prove a named test/campaign and are linked from a canonical report.
- **F — Reproducibly downloadable dependency:** binary/archive that may be replaced by a pinned, checksummed download.
- **G — Generated/build output:** compiler output, intermediate artifacts, generated binaries, APK build products.
- **H — App-derived/extracted/decompiled material:** extracted DEX/classes/resources, transient disassembly, APK-derived directories.
- **I — Temporary/runtime data/cache:** `tmp/`, cache directories, `__pycache__`, `.pyc`, local DB files, `-wal`, `-shm`, probe outputs, fetch scratch files.
- **J — Raw export / redundant evidence / superseded copy:** raw issue/comment/commit API dumps, duplicate generated JSON, uncurated screenshots or repeated content.
- **K — Unknown / needs owner decision:** anything whose role or dependencies are unclear.

For each G–K item and every large/duplicate item, record: exact path, size, SHA-256 or Git blob SHA, reason, inbound references, whether reproducible, proposed action, risk, required replacement, and verification. Do not silently omit unknowns. Unknowns remain untouched and are listed as blockers.

### Phase 2 — Define and enforce the canonical repository layout

Propose and document one clear target structure, adapted to real dependencies rather than imposed mechanically. Expected conceptual layout:

- Root: concise `README.md`, `LICENSE`, project constitution, contribution/agent instructions, `.gitignore`, and only essential configuration.
- `.github/`: workflows, issue/PR templates and repository automation.
- `miniandroid/`: runtime source and only required framework/resource data; no generated executable or local build outputs.
- `tools/` and `scripts/`: maintained tool source and reproducible scripts; no caches or large untracked tool distributions without an explicit dependency policy.
- `tests/` and `fixtures/`: deterministic tests and minimal, licensed, intentionally curated fixtures.
- `docs/`: architecture, source-derived Android laws, ADRs, contributor docs, standards, demos, and a single canonical evidence hierarchy.
- One clearly defined canonical registry/worklist location; avoid parallel competing copies in `registry/`, `canonical/`, root JSON files, or duplicate generated status documents unless their distinct roles are documented.
- `upstream/`: only curated source/reference material that must be versioned; large binaries and vendor archives should normally be retrieved by a manifest with version, URL, license and hash.
- Evidence: one canonical hierarchy with a report/manifest, run metadata, and only screenshots/traces necessary to support claims.

Before moving any path, map all references and update scripts/tests/docs/CI in the same change. Do not reorganize hundreds of paths in one unreviewable commit.

### Phase 3 — Controlled cleanup in small reviewable batches

Execute in this order; split into separate commits or PRs where practical:

1. Clearly disposable caches, local DB/WAL/SHM, `__pycache__`, `.pyc`, transient logs/probe outputs, and scratch fetch files, after verifying no test depends on them.
2. Temporary/build output trees and compiled executable artifacts, only after proving they are reproducible and not intentional fixtures.
3. Extracted/decompiled app artifacts and app-derived data. Preserve only minimal fixtures needed to reproduce a named failure, with provenance, license/redistribution review, and a documented reason.
4. Raw GitHub API dumps and large raw generated JSON. Replace them with concise, stable summaries/IDs/links or scripts that can re-fetch the data; do not lose important forensic findings or issue evidence.
5. Screenshot/evidence consolidation. Keep only evidence linked from a named report and needed to establish a claim. Identical SHA may be deduplicated only after checking whether separate run identity/provenance matters. Keep run metadata and hashes. Do not replace meaningful visual proof with an unsupported statement.
6. Duplicate dependency/toolchain copies. First add a pinned dependency manifest and verified bootstrap/download/cache behavior, then prove a clean bootstrap/build/test before removing copies.
7. Large upstream archives/JAR/AAR/Kotlin compiler distributions: review licensing and provenance; retain source references/patches and exact checksums. Do not vendor a second copy of the same artifact. Avoid deleting upstream source files merely because they are under `upstream/`.
8. Root and folder naming consistency: fix stray/ambiguous names only when the destination is canonical and references can be updated safely.
9. Rewrite the README as a concise landing page with mission, verified capabilities, quick start, limitations, architecture/status/worklist/evidence links, and contribution instructions. Move detailed living status into one canonical status file; avoid duplicated mutable status claims.

For every batch: show before/after inventory, exact paths changed, rationale, risk assessment, commands/tests, and commit SHA. Prefer reversible changes and small diffs.

### Phase 4 — Hygiene policy, CI guardrails, and regression prevention

- [ ] Update `.gitignore` for actual generated/temp patterns, while remembering that ignore rules do not untrack existing files.
- [ ] Audit and improve `tools/check_repo_hygiene.py`: explain every allowlist exception; avoid a broad whitelist; make failures actionable with path, size, classification, and remediation.
- [ ] Add a tracked-artifact policy (e.g., `docs/REPOSITORY_HYGIENE.md`) defining allowed categories, size thresholds, binary/dependency rules, evidence retention, fixture approval, and exception process.
- [ ] Add CI or a lightweight pre-merge check that rejects accidental APK/AABs, app-extracted DEX/class trees, cache/temp/database files, generated binaries, unapproved large files, unreferenced evidence, and duplicate canonical registries, with narrow explicit exceptions.
- [ ] Ensure legitimate required assets and fixtures are not falsely rejected. Include positive and negative tests for the hygiene checker.
- [ ] Ensure CI itself does not download enormous dependencies unnecessarily or depend on files removed from the repository.

### Phase 5 — Clean-room proof and quantitative closeout

Use a fresh clone or isolated clean worktree at the final commit. Do not use a dirty developer tree as proof of reproducibility.

- [ ] Bootstrap dependencies using documented commands and pinned hashes.
- [ ] Build the runtime from source.
- [ ] Run all existing required unit/integration/regression/hygiene tests and the project's established baseline gates, or document each unavailable gate with the exact reason.
- [ ] Run the minimal critical compatibility smoke tests that are feasible without paid services, and compare baseline/final outputs or hashes where deterministic.
- [ ] Confirm no runtime behavior change was introduced by repository-only cleanup.
- [ ] Confirm no tracked generated output, temp/cache/database scratch, APK/AAB, or unapproved extracted/decompiled artifacts remain.
- [ ] Confirm every retained large file and every exception has an owner, purpose, provenance/license, reproducibility status, and reference.
- [ ] Compare before/after tracked file count, unique blobs, tracked working-tree bytes, clean checkout bytes, `.git` bytes, largest files/directories, binary/archive count, JSON count/size, image/evidence count/size, and hygiene-check results.
- [ ] Clearly distinguish actual measured savings in a fresh clone from possible savings that would require a separate Git history rewrite.
- [ ] Publish a final report with command transcript excerpts, environment, HEAD SHA, commit list, test results, failures/blockers, retained exceptions, and links to the inventory/decision register.

## Required deliverables

1. `docs/REPOSITORY_HYGIENE.md` — rules, layout, retention policy, exception process.
2. A reproducible inventory/decision register (prefer compact TSV/CSV/Markdown; do not commit another huge raw JSON dump).
3. A canonical dependency manifest with versions, source URLs, license, SHA-256 and bootstrap instructions for dependencies that are externalized.
4. A single canonical evidence index and explicit policy for screenshots/traces.
5. A concise, link-oriented README that does not duplicate mutable status across several files.
6. An improved hygiene checker and automated tests/CI guardrails.
7. A final audit report with baseline-vs-final measurements and per-item disposition.
8. A line-by-line checklist comment on this issue, including status and evidence for every checkbox. Use only: **IMPLEMENTED, TESTED, OBSERVED, PARTIAL, BLOCKED, PENDING, SUPERSEDED**. “Implemented” is not “tested”; distinguish them.

## Completion checklist — update every line with status + evidence

For every item below, add a short evidence reference (path, command/output, test name, or commit SHA). Do not mark an item complete based only on intention.

- [ ] **C01 BASELINE:** HEAD, dirty-state check, repository rules and existing policies recorded.
- [ ] **C02 INVENTORY:** every tracked path inventoried and classified; unknowns explicitly listed.
- [ ] **C03 MEASUREMENTS:** working-tree, clean-clone, and `.git` sizes measured separately before/after.
- [ ] **C04 REFERENCES:** path references/dependencies in source, tests, scripts, CI and docs mapped before moves/deletions.
- [ ] **C05 RETENTION:** required runtime source, framework data, source laws, registries and fixtures preserved.
- [ ] **C06 TEMP:** disposable caches, scratch files, local DB/WAL/SHM and temp outputs handled safely.
- [ ] **C07 GENERATED:** generated executables/build outputs removed or explicitly justified and reproducible.
- [ ] **C08 EXTRACTED:** APK-derived/decompiled/extracted app material removed or reduced to documented minimal fixtures.
- [ ] **C09 JSON:** all JSON families classified; canonical data retained; raw/generated/redundant dumps handled with no knowledge loss.
- [ ] **C10 IMAGES:** screenshots/traces reviewed by provenance and claim; redundant evidence removed only when safe; canonical evidence index added.
- [ ] **C11 DEPENDENCIES:** large JAR/ZIP/AAR/toolchain/upstream files reviewed; versions/licenses/hashes/download methods documented; no unverified dependency removal.
- [ ] **C12 STRUCTURE:** canonical folder layout and registry/evidence locations documented; path changes tested.
- [ ] **C13 README:** concise landing page links to authoritative status, architecture, worklist and evidence; duplicate status minimized.
- [ ] **C14 IGNORE:** `.gitignore` covers generated files and existing tracked files are handled correctly.
- [ ] **C15 CHECKER:** hygiene checker improved with narrow allowlists and actionable diagnostics; positive/negative tests pass.
- [ ] **C16 CI:** preventive guardrails added and validated against legitimate files and intentional fixtures.
- [ ] **C17 CLEAN BUILD:** clean-room bootstrap/build succeeds, or each blocked step is documented with evidence.
- [ ] **C18 REGRESSION:** relevant tests/baseline gates pass; any failure is classified, not hidden.
- [ ] **C19 FINAL AUDIT:** before/after metrics, retained exceptions, changed paths, commit SHAs and test outputs published.
- [ ] **C20 ISSUE CLOSEOUT:** every checkbox has a status and evidence; unresolved items remain visibly PENDING/BLOCKED/PARTIAL and are not falsely closed.



### Additional live-audit checklist (2026-10-15)

- [ ] **C21 LIVE TREE:** Current HEAD `3d7227ddd98d910779cae3592b89a8fd35794879`, recursive tree entries, tracked path count, and per-path byte sum recorded; cite the exact inventory artifact/command.
- [ ] **C22 HYGIENE REAL RUN:** Run `python3 tools/check_repo_hygiene.py` at the final HEAD; attach complete output and exit code. Resolve or document every ZIP, oversize, generated-output and allowlist finding.
- [ ] **C23 TOOLCHAIN:** Every tracked path under `tools/toolchain/` has a consumer map and an explicit retain/externalize decision; clean-room bootstrap/build proves the decision.
- [ ] **C24 UPSTREAM:** `upstream/cont12_maven/` has a file-level dependency/license/provenance/duplicate decision register; compiler distribution and extracted copies are not removed before reproducibility proof.
- [ ] **C25 GENERATED RESIDUE:** All tracked `.pyc`, `__pycache__`, generated `.class`, generated build trees and temporary ZIPs are classified; intentional DEX fixtures are distinguished from extracted app artifacts.
- [ ] **C26 EVIDENCE DUPLICATION:** Duplicate-SHA groups are reviewed with run provenance and report references; path duplication is not reported as Git history savings.
- [ ] **C27 RAW EXPORTS / ROOT FILES:** Every `forensic_data/` export and unexplained root-level file has a recorded owner, purpose, provenance, references, and disposition.
- [ ] **C28 CHECKER TESTS:** Positive and negative tests demonstrate that the checker catches forbidden artifacts and permits narrowly approved fixtures; the checker and its tests agree with the actual tree.
- [ ] **C29 REPO SIZE:** Baseline/final working tree, fresh clone checkout, and `.git` sizes are separately measured. GitHub's repository-size metadata and summed tree blob sizes are not substituted for these measurements.
- [ ] **C30 CURRENT STATE RECONCILIATION:** Explain why `evidence/` increased from the older audit's reported 2,888 paths / 26.39 MiB to 2,988 / 30.57 MiB, while `tmp/` and other areas changed; cite the commits and exact path-level inventory.

## Final response format from the coder

Post a comment with:
1. **HEAD before / HEAD after** and all commit SHAs.
2. **What changed**, grouped by phase and exact path.
3. **What was intentionally retained** and why.
4. **What was not changed** and why (especially unclear/licensing-sensitive/required dependencies).
5. **Before/after metrics** with measurement commands and distinguish working tree from `.git`.
6. **Tests** with exact commands, exit codes and meaningful output.
7. **Regressions/failures/blockers** and follow-up issue links.
8. **C01–C20 checklist**: each item status plus evidence.
9. Explicit statement that no history rewrite/force push occurred.

Do not close this issue until clean-room verification and the C01–C20 evidence checklist are complete. If the task is too large for one safe patch, complete it as ordered, reviewable batches and keep the issue open with an honest status; do not stop after producing a plan or cleaning only the easiest directory.

# Coder 5 — full campaign report, open-source game execution on MiniAndroid

> This report was created **at the user's request** so the lead coder can read every achievement in one place, without scattered lookups.
> Per the directive: **no comments posted, no pushes made — only this one Issue.**
> Report date: **2026-11-02** · Sources: `evidence/canonical/registry.json`, `docs/verified_executed_games.json`, the S95-FOLLOWUP census audit, the f105–f124 campaign report, and issues #334–#354.
> Governing principle of this whole report: **no fake success** — every claim is tied to an exit code, frames, SHA or evidence path.

---

## 1) Campaign headlines (numbers verified by the census audit)

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Canonical corpus | **148 titles** (87 games) |
| Games with real-execution evidence (canonical artifact + session + SHA) | **23** |
| — VERIFIED games | **20** |
| — PARTIAL games (executed, visually disputed) | 2 |
| — Downgraded to OBSERVED in the audit | 1 |
| VERIFIED games with proven state change (real interaction) | **11** |
| Games with a meaningful screenshot/GIF (VERIFIED+PARTIAL) | **22** |
| Games with repeatable execution (≥2 recorded runs) | **16** |
| Games at E5 (deterministic repeatable runs) | **4** |
| Games executed with trace-only evidence (E3, no visual claims) | 64 |

Evidence ladder: **E0 hypothesis → E1 source → E2 unit test → E3 execution trace → E4 real APK run (screenshots/session) → E5 deterministic repeatable run → E6 corpus-level law.**

## 2) The 20 VERIFIED games — complete evidence table

| # | Game | Package | Evidence level | State change |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 2048 | `com.miniandroid.g2048` | E4 | ✅ score up to 200 (65 frames) |
| 2 | Anuto TD | `ch.logixisland.anuto` | E4 · L5 | — |
| 3 | Balance the Ball | `com.jeffliu.balancetheball` | E4 | — (sensor game) |
| 4 | Fish Rings | `eu.veldsoft.fish.rings` | **E5** | ✅ tap → 4,312 px pixel change |
| 5 | FreeKlondike | `eu.veldsoft.free.klondike` | E4 · L10 | — |
| 6 | Mines (premy) | `cos.premy.mines` | E4 | — |
| 7 | Mini Tetris | `com.miniandroid.tetris` | **E5** | ✅ piece fall + NEXT change across 3 identical runs |
| 8 | MiniCraft (House Builder) | `com.miniandroid.minicraft` | **E5** | ✅ house built: blocks 0→2 |
| 9 | OPMT (One More Time…) | `one.scarecrow.games.OPMT` | E4 | — |
| 10 | OpenSudoku | `cz.romario.opensudoku` | E4 · L5 | — |
| 11 | Snake Deluxe | `com.miniandroid.snakedeluxe` | **E5** | ✅ 2 lives, game over @frame94/192, restart |
| 12 | TicTacToe Deluxe | `com.miniandroid.tictactoedeluxe` | E4 | ✅ O/X placement + turn switch |
| 13 | Vector Pinball (bouncy) | `com.dozingcatsoftware.bouncy` | E4 | ✅ ball launch + score |

| 19 | BobBall | `org.bobstuff.bobball` | E4 | ✅ 6/6 click state changes |
| 20 | All In Gold | `x653.all_in_gold` | E4 | — |

**PARTIAL (execution + interaction proven, visually disputed):** TicTacToe Classic (`com.emmanuelmess.tictactoe` — O/X placement recorded), TriPeaks (`eu.veldsoft.tri.peaks`).
**Honest downgrade in the audit:** Memory (`eu.quelltext.memory`) — blank frame, carries no visual claim per the S54 law.

All 23 titles: canonical GIF/screenshot with SHA256 under `evidence/canonical/` + execution protocol + recorded run counts in `docs/verified_executed_games.json`.

## 3) The four games at the evidence summit (E5 — deterministic repeatable runs)

- **Snake Deluxe** — real-dalvik run with 23 automated taps + death/restart tap; full gameplay loop; 4 recorded runs (S79/S80/S83/S91).
- **Mini Tetris** — 6 unique frames per run, identical across 3 deterministic runs (`wave_c_determinism.json`); the ANIMATION_FROZEN classification was rejected (it was a harness bug, GAME-0004 CLOSED).
- **MiniCraft** — real house building: 5 block placements + material cycle + 2 digs; 3 identical deterministic runs; GAME-0005 CLOSED.
- **Fish Rings** — complete provenance chain SOURCE→TIMER→RESOLVE→DECODE→TAP→SETIMAGE(36)→PIXELS; 6 runs (S65/S79/S91/S93).

## 4) Playability campaign (f105–f124) — engine laws and the regression gate

- **4 general engine laws landed:** GPG-105 (exact overload resolution with full descriptor), GPG-106 (`AbstractList$ListItr` bridge), GPG-107 (live Map views in `CollectionShadow`), GPG-107b (typed `view_elements` reads). All generic — zero app-specific hooks.
- **Dooz (io.github.yamin8000.dooz):** a chain of 6 consecutive blockers fixed → **the campaign's first crash-free end-to-end Compose run: rc=0, zero uncaught, RESUMED** — honest classification: EXECUTED (not yet RENDERED; draw ops=0).
- **Regression gate:** TicTacToe golden **8/8 PASS** — 9/9 clicks, «X WINS», byte-identical replay (`613cfccc…`). Corpus battery f124: **10/14 with rc=0 and real frames** (gmdice, chessclock, bouncy, tictactoeclassic, …).
- Tooling: an exact Dalvik disassembler (`gpg_f105c_exact.py`) + a forensic probe kit.

## 5) Native game family — execution and auto-play issues

- **#334 GAMES-1** — full-load 5–10 games end-to-end (launch + render + interaction) ✅ closed
- **#335 GAMES-2** — Snake Deluxe auto-play (self-play without memory cheating) ✅ closed
- **#336 GAMES-3** — Minicraft house building automated ✅ closed
- **#337 GAMES-4** — new snake variant: build + load + play ✅ closed
- **#338 GAMES-5** — 2048 auto-play ✅ closed
- **#339 GAMES-6** — Mini Tetris auto-play
- **#340 GAMES-7** — TicTacToe Deluxe auto-play ✅ closed
- **#341 GAMES-8** — wave evidence package + gameplay GIFs on gh-pages ✅ closed
- **#354 [GAMES] Native game family** — gameplay GIFs, 5 engine-bug laws, 3-run-verified titles + honest 124-reopen audit
- **#353 [HTML5-APPS]** — WebView: from white screen to **real JS execution** — Breakout 71 runs its own game loop (#94)

## 6) Data assets and tooling produced

- **`evidence/canonical/registry.json`** — canonical registry: 91 games → **23 VERIFIED / 1 PARTIAL / 66 OBSERVED / 1 BLOCKED**
- **Compatibility matrix v1** (`compatibility_matrix.json`) — 15 apps (**9 VERIFIED / 3 TESTED / 1 PARTIAL / 2 BLOCKED**) + 91 games, L0–L7 checkpoints per subsystem
- **`candidates.json`** — 84 F-Droid candidates with license/version/repo + `github_verify.json` (repo/star verification) + the full F-Droid index
- **`MiniAndroid_20_Games_Roadmap.xlsx`** — a 20-game roadmap in 6 sheets: «20 selected games» (genre/package/size/license/repo/render path/risk/priority — e.g. Yet Another Pixel Dungeon 5.4MB GPL-3.0 priority 1, Remixed Dungeon 15.7MB priority 2), «Test protocol», «Execution checklist», «Phase 2», «Sources», «Review»
- **Audit and pipeline scripts:** `scan_fdroid.py`, `verify_github_games.py`, `build_games_xlsx.py`, `s96_games_audit.py`, `s96_validate_audit.py`, `tools/verify_canonical_evidence.py`, `tools/validate_control_system.py`

## 7) Honest identification — open gaps (per the no-fake-success law)

1. **64 games at E3 (trace) only** — execution recorded but no meaningful frame; no visual claims made.
2. **APK SHA256 not recorded for 4 titles** — FreeKlondike, TriPeaks, OpenSudoku, Anuto TD (identity gap).
3. **Interaction→state not recorded for ~10 statically VERIFIED titles** — Anuto TD, OpenSudoku, OPMT, adnihilation, Mines, Balance the Ball, all_in_gold, ballbreak, FreeKlondike, TriPeaks.
4. **Single-session status for 7 titles** — TicTacToe Deluxe, FreeKlondike, TriPeaks, adnihilation, Mines, all_in_gold, Memory.
5. **The S92 §29 promotion gate not executed** — 7 GIF titles still sit as `candidate_*` in the registry (AUD-IC-6 inconsistency).
6. **Compose front-end: draw ops=0** — composition runs but `drawRect/drawText` never reach the software canvas (dooz; the exact next path is localized).
7. **The libGDX/native-load family** — `SharedLibraryLoadRuntimeException` in HEAD-SMOKE (#388); GL games blocked (e.g. tictactoe with `GdxRuntimeException`).
8. **GFX-002** — the LinearLayout weight bug (dodge 3 flags, bouncy 1 flag); the largest measured visual fan-out.
9. **No per-game issue exists** — all 23 titles are recorded in the audit with `MISSING_ISSUE`; this very gap motivated the aggregate report.

## 8) Next queue (Coder 5's proposal — from the census audit)

| # | Action | Converts | Why first |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Run the S92 §29 review gate for the 7 `candidate_*` titles with S95 measured verdicts | registry drift → consistency | zero runtime work |
| 2 | Record APK SHA256 for the 4 SHA-less titles | identity gap → audit-proof identity | cheap |
| 3 | The S95 tap-capture protocol on static VERIFIED titles (OpenSudoku, FreeKlondike, Anuto TD, OPMT) | VERIFIED(static) → VERIFIED(interactive) | protocol ready |
| 4 | x3 repeats for the Snake-class titles lacking repeats (2048, TicTacToe Deluxe, dodge, bouncy, nounours, hotdeath, bobball) | E4 → E5 | the wave_c harness supports it |
| 5 | GFX-002 then re-capture dodge + bouncy | visual PARTIAL → SEMANTIC_PASS | largest measured fan-out |
| 6 | Single-cycle assault on the Compose draw-op pipeline (the Owner/CanvasHolder chain) | dooz EXECUTED → RENDERED | the most precisely localized front |

---

**Signed: Coder 5** — reporting steward of the games campaign. Awaiting the lead coder's review and direction.
This report deliberately contains no number or claim outside the evidence recorded in the repo; every row is tied to an evidence path or a session number.

# Coder 3 | Achievement 5 — Full self-play of Snake Deluxe on the fresh build: SCORE 2 / BEST 2 with the canonical S80 driver (vision-based, no memory cheating)

> Chain: #416 (fresh build) · #417 (Wave 2) · #418 (Wave 3) · board: #415 · per-app case file: #401
> Governing law: **no fake success** — evidence from this session's rendered frames.

---

## 1) What was executed

The official driver `scripts/autoplay/s80_sd_autoplay.py` (vision-based self-play with laws C1/C3/C4/C7) ran — with **zero changes to its logic** — on Coder 3's fresh build (`SD_CAPTURES=3`). The only environment prep: an ENG path symlink and copying the rebuilt APK to the driver's expected path.

Driver laws (from the script source itself):
- **C1**: only actuator = scheduled taps through the canonical TouchDispatcher
- **C3**: vision from rendered frames only (board cell centers) — zero access to game memory
- **C4**: the app's own logic stays authoritative (reverse guard, walls, growth)
- **C7**: every cycle re-runs the real APK from launch; the committed prefix is re-verified by per-frame pixel SHAs up to the first frame a newly added tap can influence

## 2) Results

- Cycles: `cycle 1: head=(8,7) d=R path=1 captures=1` → `cycle 2: head=(8,2) d=U path=4 captures=2` → death before obs frame 20
- **Final continuous run: 77 frames · 13-frame prefix verified · captures=2 · rc=0**
- **Two distinct food placements: (8,6) and (6,0) — the snake really ate twice**
- HUD: **"SCORE 0" → "SCORE 2 / BEST 2"** (HUD crops from frames 0/20/40/76)
- End: the **GAME OVER dialog** rendered with a "SCORE / SCORE(2)" summary + RESTART button

## 1) What was done (and why it matters)

All previous campaign sessions (S62+…S141) ran on earlier environments. In this session Coder 3 built **a brand-new environment from scratch** and re-ran the whole chain:

1. **Full runtime build from source** (`miniandroid/miniandroid`, C++17, make, g++ 14.2) — no dependency on previous binaries.
2. **APK toolchain rebuilt** — `tools/aapt2`, `tools/ecj`, `tools/d8` are empty placeholders in the repo (policy §20: zero committed APKs); the chain was rebuilt from official references: **aapt2 8.5.0-11315950** (Google Maven) + **ECJ 3.37.0** (official Eclipse mirror) + **R8/D8 8.3.37** (Google Maven) + the repo's vendored `android-34.jar`.

> Honest note: this APK SHA256 is a rebuild from the in-repo source with the rebuilt toolchain; byte-identity with any recorded S80 build is not expected (different aapt2/ECJ versions) — identity is established by source + canonical recipe, not by SHA equality.

## 3) Full Snake Deluxe run — evidence

Canonical command (same shape as the `scripts/autoplay/s80_sd_autoplay.py` driver):

```
build/miniandroid run --execution-mode real-dalvik --frames 20 --frame-delay 250 \
```

  - Framebuffer: 1,826,289 / 2,073,600 non-white pixels (~88%)

Meaning: **the render pipeline in the fresh environment is deterministic and reproducible** — the same E5 standard the registry records for Snake Deluxe, now re-proven on Coder 3's new build (`GAME-001` E5 → independent re-confirmation).

issues.title: EXTERNAL ROOT CENSUS — Deep multilingual root discovery and MiniAndroid cross-match
issues.body:
# EXTERNAL ROOT CENSUS — Deep multilingual root discovery for MiniAndroid

## Mission

Create one authoritative, continuously updated census of generic Android compatibility/runtime root causes that can explain APK failure, white/black/partial screens, wrong UI, missing state, native failures, silent stalls, or false-positive execution.

This is NOT an APK-by-APK test list. Find root families already discovered by AOSP engineers, emulator projects, Waydroid/Anbox/Redroid/WSA, ART/Dalvik, graphics/runtime projects, AndroidX/Compose/WebView, app/framework issue trackers, academic work, Chinese/Russian/English/Japanese/Korean communities, GitHub issues/comments/PRs, source code, and technical forums — then map them to MiniAndroid.

CRITICAL: Do NOT make thousands of APKs rediscover the same root.

For every external finding:
SOURCE → mechanism → Android/AOSP semantic law → root family → MiniAndroid registry cross-match → NEW / DUPLICATE / ALREADY-FIXED / ENVIRONMENT-ONLY → representative probe/APK → A/B proof.

## FOUR DEEP ROUNDS

ROUND 1 — AOSP/framework + major compatibility projects.
ROUND 2 — GitHub issue/PR/comment archaeology: Waydroid, Anbox, Redroid, WSA, emulator, ART, graphics, runtime, WebView, Compose, Flutter, Unity/Godot/libGDX.
ROUND 3 — multilingual: Chinese, Russian, Japanese, Korean, English; forums/blogs/source-reading communities and issue comments.
ROUND 4 — adversarial gap hunt: search specifically for root families missing from this census and challenge every P0/P1 assumption.

After EVERY round, update this same issue with:
1. sources searched;
2. new candidates;
3. deduplication against MiniAndroid registry;
4. priority/fan-out ranking;
5. evidence quality;
6. exact coder probes required.

## ALREADY KNOWN / CROSS-MATCH FIRST

Do not blindly recreate these:
- TypedArray semantics
- StaticLayout.Builder
- Space AT_MOST / weight semantics
- field identity / instance-field aliasing
- C013 placeholder/overpaint
- resource provenance
- Method-record reflection family
- Method.getModifiers/getParameterTypes/getAnnotation
- DEX annotation index decoding
- getDeclaredMethods constructor filtering
- ArrayList(Collection) / CollectionShadow
- annotation-proxy access
- LayerDrawable materialization/findDrawableByLayerId/getId/setId
- XmlPullParser / Resources.getLayout
- ShortcutInfo.Builder
- Compose/deferred UI
- Fragment materialization
- ViewPager/mCurItem artifact frontier
- F-NEW-084 progress-aware interpreter execution
- Canvas(Bitmap) / Bitmap pixel semantics
- AssetManager/resources
- SharedPreferences
- SQLite/WAL
- package data root/filesystem containment
- providers/Intent/BitmapFactory
- TouchDispatcher
- EGL facade/GL20
- WebView JS-DATA-PASS
- basic ABI/native execution gate
- install/persistence provenance
- lifecycle/window/root/deferred-UI family

These may still contain missing sub-roots; prove family completeness rather than assuming it.

# P0 ROOT FAMILIES

## P0-01 Window → ViewRoot → Surface → BufferQueue → presentation
Potential sub-roots:
Window creation/registration; WindowManager registration; ViewRoot creation; AttachInfo/root linkage; relayout; Surface allocation; BufferQueue producer/consumer; first buffer; acquire/release; EGLSurface; swap/present; compositor visibility/z-order; final presentation.

A ViewTree, successful draw, or process survival is NOT equivalent to presented pixels.

## P0-02 CPU / ABI / ELF / native execution
APK ABI selection; ELF machine/class; dynamic linker; DT_NEEDED; relocations; JNI_OnLoad; dlsym/symbol resolution; translation availability/correctness; ANativeWindow/native graphics; native filesystem assumptions.

EXTRACTED is not EXECUTED.

## P0-03 EGL/GLES/Vulkan capability and surface semantics
GLES version; EGL extensions; context; window surface; shader/compiler; texture/FBO limits; precision/GLSL; Vulkan feature mismatch; swap/present; AHardwareBuffer usage; software renderer; SurfaceFlinger/RenderEngine.

## P0-04 ClassLoader / ClassLinker / identity / initialization
Parent loader chain; DEX search order; duplicate class identity; class/method/field/interface resolution; clinit execution; initialization state; reflection visibility; hidden API policy; class-loader-specific behavior.

## P0-05 Binder / ServiceManager / system-service contract
Service registration/absence/restart; Binder identity; transaction code/version mismatch; Parcel schema; Parcelable version; permissions; oneway; death notification; lifecycle; system_server restart; boot-time service availability.

SERVICE EXISTS != SERVICE CONTRACT COMPATIBLE.

## P0-06 Looper / MessageQueue / Choreographer / traversal
Thread affinity; Handler; queue ordering; barriers; delayed callbacks; Choreographer; vsync; frame callbacks; invalidate; requestLayout; traversal scheduling; measure/layout/draw never reached.

Especially important for Compose/deferred UI.

## P0-07 WebView / renderer / storage dependency
Provider/backend; WebView package/version; renderer process/IPC; data directory; storage mount; cookies/local storage; asset loading; JS; DOM/CSS; network; TLS; GPU/WebGL; media-service dependencies.

## P0-08 Storage / package data / SAF / MediaStore / providers
/data/user/0 vs user_de; UID ownership/isolation; external storage; Android/data/media/obb; scoped storage; SAF; MediaStore; ContentProvider; URI grants; MIME/path permissions; restart persistence; clear/reinstall/uninstall cleanup.

PATH STRING EXISTS != ANDROID STORAGE SEMANTICS.

## P0-09 Permission / AppOps / UID / User identity
Manifest permission; runtime grant; AppOps; special access; UID; user/profile; signature permissions; service-side enforcement.

Do not globally grant permissions.

# P1 ROOT FAMILIES

1. Target-SDK semantic switches
2. API-level compatibility changes
3. hidden/non-SDK API enforcement
4. Fragment lifecycle/materialization
5. Compose ViewTreeLifecycleOwner and other ViewTree owners
6. SurfaceView
7. TextureView / SurfaceTexture
8. MediaCodec / mediaserver
9. AudioTrack / AudioRecord
10. Camera2
11. SensorManager
12. Location/provider state
13. ContentProvider authority/URI/MIME
14. Intent resolution/exported rules
15. Broadcast delivery
16. service binding/start/foreground-service semantics
17. Activity recreation/configuration change
18. density/locale/font configuration
19. RTL/Bidi/font fallback/text shaping
20. RenderThread synchronization
21. animation/time/frame semantics
22. Canvas(Bitmap) pixel writeback
23. bitmap decode/configuration/color-space semantics
24. SQLite locking/WAL/journaling
25. split APK / split resource resolution
26. dynamic feature/resource loading
27. APEX/bootclasspath/framework classpath
28. Bionic/linker differences
29. NDK API-level differences
30. Build.VERSION/system-property semantics
31. TLS/crypto provider/Keystore
32. notification/permission changes
33. clipboard/share/chooser
34. IME/text input
35. accessibility
36. autofill
37. widgets/shortcuts
38. backup/restore
39. alarms/jobs/work scheduling
40. background execution limits
41. network/DNS/VPN
42. proxy/SSL certificate behavior
43. media codec/container support
44. DRM
45. OpenGL shader compiler behavior
46. AHardwareBuffer
47. display/insets/cutout/multi-window
48. status/navigation/system bars
49. z-order/window flags
50. input focus/touch dispatch/window focus

# ROUND-1 HIGH-VALUE EXTERNAL SIGNALS

1. AndroidGoLab/binder demonstrates about 1,500 Android Binder interfaces and version-aware transaction-code resolution; even firmware/API revisions can shift transaction mappings.
2. Waydroid issue #1148 demonstrates intermittent black screen when launching an app directly while full UI works: session/window/compositor setup can be causal.
3. Current Waydroid issues include graphics composer crashes, ARM/libndk translation, libhoudini/Vulkan deadlocks, zygote bootclasspath, ANativeWindow/AV1, camera and graphical corruption — high-value archaeology targets.
4. Redroid issue #934 demonstrates SurfaceFlinger/SwiftShader/AHardwareBuffer failure during shader-cache warmup before ordinary app rendering.
5. dotnet/android issue #12077 demonstrates API/system-image ↔ emulator-version contract failure: old emulator lacked required SurfaceFlinger AIDL and boot stalled/black-screened.
6. dotnet/android issue #12119 demonstrates system_server restart causing package Binder service disappearance during install.
7. Google Maps Compose issue #875 demonstrates missing ViewTreeLifecycleOwner can directly break ComposeView creation/measurement.
8. Android API semantic-drift research reports thousands of Android API incompatibilities across releases; semantic differences must be treated as a major root source.

## SOURCE CLASSES — SEARCH ALL

AOSP; Android Developers; source.android.com; CTS/VTS; CDD; ART/Dalvik; Android emulator; Waydroid issues/comments; Anbox; Redroid; WSA; AndroidRecomp; DroidVM; droidsaw; Skydnir; libarsc; bundletool; Robolectric; Paparazzi; Roborazzi; emulator harnesses; Chromium/WebView; Mesa/SwiftShader; Skia; ANGLE; EGL/GLES/Vulkan; Flutter Android; React Native Android; Compose/AndroidX; libGDX/Unity/Godot; SQLite; Bionic/linker; Binder/AIDL; Chinese; Russian; Japanese; Korean; Stack Overflow; Reddit; academic papers.

Search source code, closed issues, PR discussions, and COMMENTS — not only issue titles.

## ROOT RECORD FORMAT

ROOT-ID | FAMILY | PRIORITY | LANGUAGE | SOURCE | SOURCE-TYPE | MECHANISM | ANDROID LAW | MINIANDROID CROSS-MATCH | EXISTING ROOT | FANOUT | WHITE/BLACK LINK | ENVIRONMENT/RUNTIME | CONFIDENCE | PROBE | REAL APK | STATUS | EVIDENCE | CODER ACTION

## NO FALSE ROOTS

Do not promote package-specific, OEM-only, GMS-only, host-desktop-only, corrupted-APK, stale, already-fixed, or symptom-only findings without causal proof. Mark them APP-SPECIFIC / ENVIRONMENT-ONLY / STALE / UNPROVEN as appropriate.

## PRIORITY

P0 = broad fan-out, lifecycle/framework initialization, native execution, presentation, storage, services, or can cause white/black/partial output.
P1 = substantial but narrower fan-out.
P2 = specialized.

## FINAL ROUND-4 DELIVERABLE

Report:
- sources inspected;
- languages;
- projects/issue trackers;
- candidate count;
- NEW/DUPLICATE/ALREADY-FIXED/ENVIRONMENT-ONLY counts;
- highest-fan-out 20;
- highest-confidence P0;
- white/black roots;
- CPU/ABI/native roots;
- file/resource/media roots;
- Compose/deferred roots;
- immediate probes;
- static-fingerprint candidates;
- exact implementation/test order.

Do not close until all four rounds are complete and every high-confidence P0 candidate is cross-matched against the MiniAndroid registry.

## Current source references

- https://github.com/waydroid/waydroid/issues
- https://github.com/waydroid/waydroid/issues/1148

This issue is a RESEARCH/CROSS-MATCH ledger. Do not implement speculative fixes merely because an external candidate exists. Confirm the Android law, compare MiniAndroid source/registry, then create a minimal synthetic probe and representative real-APK A/B test.

Update THIS issue after every research round; do not create another census issue.

# COMPLETE FOLLOW-THROUGH REQUEST — DO NOT LEAVE PRIOR OR NEW GAPS UNRESOLVED

This is the follow-through request after the latest #371/#372/#373/#374 campaign results. Treat ALL previous requirements, newly discovered roots, partials, blockers, and next steps as one reconciled worklist.

Do NOT stop at the latest reported success.

Re-read and reconcile:

- #374

- worklog/campaign state

- existing historical evidence

Then derive one complete matrix:
DONE / VERIFIED / PARTIAL / BLOCKED / PENDING / UNKNOWN / DUPLICATE / SUPERSEDED.

Every incomplete item must either be implemented and verified, or be proven to require an external prerequisite and recorded as BLOCKED with evidence.

Do not create duplicate roots.

## 1. FIRST REPRODUCE CURRENT BASELINE

Before changing code:
- verify current remote HEAD
- verify current binary SHA

- run the recorded baseline gates
- verify anchors/goldens
- verify Gate A

No regression may be hidden.

## 2. COMPLETE #374 — ANDROID BASE FOUNDATION

Execute the entire #374 98-section foundation contract, not merely its documentation.

For every domain prove:
SOURCE -> ANDROID LAW -> IMPLEMENTATION -> SYNTHETIC POSITIVE -> SYNTHETIC NEGATIVE -> REAL APK -> FIRST DIVERGENCE -> 3 RUNS -> REGRESSION.

Audit all previous #374 layers including:
- platform/device contract
- API/target-SDK behavior
- CPU/ABI/native/linker
- APK/package/install/update/splits/signing
- permissions/AppOps/special access
- UID/user/profile/sandbox/security

- Surface/BufferQueue/RenderThread/Skia/compositor/presentation/capture

- clipboard/share/chooser
- settings/system configuration
- widgets/shortcuts/launcher
- exceptions/ANR/watchdog
- observability
- corpus-derived discovery
- reference differential probes.

Do not count placeholders as VERIFIED.

## 3. CLOSE CURRENTLY KNOWN PARTIALS

### R-NEW-464
Finish the Method-record reflection/getDeclaredMethods route deterministically.
- Do not use broad reflection hacks.
- Preserve declaring-class identity and method metadata.
- Verify getDeclaredMethods/getModifiers/getAnnotation and related Method semantics.
- Add focused synthetic probes and a real APK.
- 3 clean runs.
- Cross-match registry before adding any new root.

### ViewPager / mCurItem
Resolve the primitive/field identity frontier if the APK is available and SHA-pinned.
- First establish exact APK identity.
- If current F-Droid artifact differs from recorded evidence, do NOT claim a runtime regression.
- Obtain/restore the exact evidence artifact through the existing reproducible corpus mechanism if available.
- Then reproduce and fix the generic law.
- No ViewPager-specific hack.

### Compose family / F-NEW-221
Use sudokusolver and another independent Compose APK.
- determine the actual missing platform/runtime contract
- distinguish Compose infrastructure from app-specific code
- fix generic contract only
- verify fan-out on another Compose app.

### Fragment materialization frontier
For ARM/native and mixed apps, separate:
ABI blocker
from
Fragment/component/lifecycle blocker.
Do not report a dual-cause without independent A/B evidence.

### F-NEW-084 interpreter halt
Investigate the infinite-loop cap 50001.
- determine whether the interpreter loop is semantically legitimate, incorrectly bounded, or missing a runtime operation
- never simply raise/remove the cap to make the game pass
- add a bounded semantic execution law and regression probe
- test fairymahjong plus another game.

## 4. ENVIRONMENT / PREREQUISITE LAYER

Complete #373 into an operational preflight gate.

For every APK inspect:
- min/target/max SDK
- target-SDK behavior changes
- permissions + AppOps/special access
- features
- graphics requirements
- Vulkan/GLES requirements

- DT_NEEDED dependency closure
- WebView

- providers/content authorities
- external dependencies
- splits
- required services.

Return:
AVAILABLE / PARTIAL / MISSING / INCOMPATIBLE / NOT_TESTED
and
REQUIRED / OPTIONAL / CONDITIONAL / IMPLIED / UNKNOWN.

The gate must run BEFORE ordinary runtime debugging.

## 5. CAPABILITY HONESTY

Audit every advertised capability against actual execution.

In particular:
- SUPPORTED_ABIS must not advertise non-executable ARM unless translation exists.
- Vulkan must not be advertised if only GLES2 exists.
- camera/GPS/telephony/BT/NFC must remain honestly absent unless implemented.
- permissions must not all become granted.
- services must not return fake success.
- Build.* and feature flags must match behavior.
- storage paths must correspond to real storage.
- native libraries must be executable, not merely extractable.

Produce a FALSE_ADVERTISED matrix and drive every false claim to zero or explicit documented limitation.

## 6. UNKNOWN APK GATE

Make the Agent Skill consume the same preflight contract.

For an unknown APK the skill must be able to answer:
- what is this package?
- what does it require?
- what can MiniAndroid provide?
- what is missing/incompatible?
- what permissions are requested/granted/denied?
- what ABI can execute?
- what system services are needed?
- what storage is accessible?
- what graphics/media/input prerequisites exist?
- what is the first blocker/divergence?
- should this enter runtime root work?

Mandatory verdict:
PREFLIGHT_PASS / ENVIRONMENT_BLOCKED / INSTALL_BLOCKED / SECURITY_BLOCKED / IDENTITY_BLOCKED / SERVICE_BLOCKED / EXECUTION_BLOCKED / RESOURCE_BLOCKED / GRAPHICS_BLOCKED / MEDIA_BLOCKED / NETWORK_BLOCKED / INPUT_BLOCKED / CAPTURE_ONLY / RUNTIME_ROOT / UNKNOWN.

## 7. CORPUS-DERIVED DISCOVERY

Do not rely only on the predefined foundation list.

Mine the current corpus and representative new APKs for:
- framework APIs
- Java APIs
- reflection
- system services
- permissions
- intents
- providers
- URI schemes
- MIME types
- native libraries
- ELF dependencies
- graphics APIs
- media codecs
- SQLite
- storage
- crypto
- scheduling
- WebView
- sensors/hardware.

Cluster failures by generic contract. One generic fix should fan out.

## 8. NEW APP + NEW GAME ACCEPTANCE

After foundation changes test at least:
- 1 genuinely new independent-family app
- 1 genuinely new independent-family game
- preferably a second app/game if the first exposes a major new frontier.

Do not select only known-good APKs.

For each:
APK SHA
preflight
install
launch
first divergence
execution level
visual evidence/provenance
state change
3-run result.

## 9. WHITE / BLACK / PARTIAL AUDIT

Revisit historical white/black/partial cases.

For every case prove one of:
ENVIRONMENT_MISMATCH
ABI_NATIVE
API_PLATFORM_CONTRACT
PACKAGE_INSTALL
PERMISSION_SECURITY
IDENTITY_SANDBOX
SYSTEM_SERVICE_IPC
RESOURCE_CONFIGURATION
COMPONENT_LIFECYCLE
VIEW_WINDOW
GRAPHICS_SURFACE
BUFFER_COMPOSITION
PRESENTATION
MEDIA
NETWORK
INPUT
CAPTURE_ONLY
ORDINARY_RUNTIME_ROOT
UNKNOWN.

Do not let environment failures become fake runtime roots.
Do not let runtime roots be hidden behind environment labels.

## 10. ROOT REGISTRY DISCIPLINE

For every candidate:
A already covered
B same root/new evidence
C existing root/missing sub-law
D genuinely new platform/runtime root
E environment prerequisite
F future/out-of-scope.

Only C/D become root work.

Before every new registry ID, search the entire registry and evidence history.

## 11. SECURITY / NEGATIVE TESTS

Prove denial semantics for:
- permissions
- signature permissions
- AppOps
- private storage
- cross-package storage
- wrong UID/user
- unexported components
- provider/path permissions
- URI grants
- PendingIntent identity
- unsupported ABI
- missing native library
- unavailable service
- unavailable hardware
- unsupported API
- incomplete split.

No universal root, universal permission, universal service or universal capability.

## 12. PERSISTENCE / INSTALLATION PROOF

For at least 3 independent installed apps including a complex app:
- install
- verify package-owned directories
- create real file
- write real bytes
- read bytes
- stat/length
- SharedPreferences
- SQLite where used
- media/assets where used
- restart
- verify persistence
- clear data
- verify expected removal
- reinstall
- verify expected reset/preserve semantics
- uninstall
- verify cleanup/isolation.

Path strings alone are not evidence.

## 13. VISUAL PROVENANCE

For white/black/partial results:
APK -> component -> ViewTree -> draw op -> surface -> buffer -> compositor/presentation -> capture.

Record the first stage that diverges.

A non-empty PNG is not success.
A ViewTree is not success.
EGL initialization is not success.

## 14. BASELINE / REGRESSION AFTER EACH GENERIC FIX

After every generic foundation fix:
- focused synthetic probe
- focused real APK
- relevant random app/game
- baseline battery
- anchors/goldens
- negatives
- reinstall/uninstall
- NATX if native path affected
- 3 clean runs.

No batch of speculative changes without intermediate evidence.

## 15. SOURCE-FIRST RESEARCH REQUIREMENT

Before implementing a missing semantic law:
1. locate Android/AOSP reference behavior
2. identify actual source/algorithm
3. write the semantic law
4. identify current MiniAndroid divergence
5. implement the smallest generic correction
6. test positive + negative
7. test real APK
8. cross-match registry
9. record evidence.

Do not infer platform semantics from one application's crash.

## 16. FINAL COMPLETION LEDGER

Update one consolidated ledger containing:

DOMAIN
LAW
SOURCE
IMPLEMENTATION
SYNTHETIC
NEGATIVE
REAL APK
STATUS
FIRST DIVERGENCE
EVIDENCE
3-RUN
REGRESSION
COMMIT

Include numerical totals:
REQUIRED
IMPLEMENTED
TESTED
VERIFIED
PARTIAL
BLOCKED
PENDING
UNKNOWN
FALSE_ADVERTISED
REAL_APK_COVERAGE
NEGATIVE_COVERAGE.

Do NOT collapse these into one percentage.

## 17. DEFINITION OF DONE

This campaign is complete only if:

- #371 baseline remains green
- #372 has zero duplicate roots
- #373 preflight is operational
- #374 foundation domains are executed, not merely documented
- current partial roots are resolved or externally blocked with evidence
- environment blockers are separated from runtime roots
- capability advertisements are honest
- unknown APK gate works
- at least one new app + one new game pass through the complete pipeline
- persistence/security negative tests pass
- visual first-divergence tracing works
- 3 clean runs are green for the final binary
- all evidence is committed and pushed
- worklog/registry/issues are reconciled
- remaining unknown surface is explicitly numbered.

Do not declare "complete" while any known PARTIAL/PENDING item above is merely deferred without a proven blocker.

## 18. IMPORTANT — DO NOT CHEAT THE BASE

Forbidden:
- app-specific hacks
- package-name conditionals
- APK-specific constants
- universal permissions
- universal services
- fake ABI advertisement
- fake Vulkan/feature advertisement
- swallowing exceptions
- removing execution limits without semantic justification
- bypassing security
- treating extraction as execution
- treating launch/process survival as success
- treating screenshot existence as success
- treating parser success as execution
- treating one successful APK as foundation verification.

## 19. FINAL REPORT

At the end report:
- final HEAD
- final binary SHA
- all commits
- all issue ledgers
- every resolved item
- every externally blocked item and proof
- every remaining unknown
- exact L0-L6 counts
- new app/game evidence
- environment blocker counts
- runtime-root counts
- regression result
- 3-run result.

No high-level "done" statement without the evidence matrix.

issues.title: ARCH-001: Execution Family Matrix for Generic App/Game Compatibility
issues.body:
## Objective

Establish a generic Execution Family / Target Architecture Matrix so MiniAndroid can execute families of real Android software without creating app-specific executors.

This issue is complementary to #383 and must remain BASE-FIRST.

## Core rule

Do NOT implement Telegram, WhatsApp, Signal, Instagram, Dooz-specific, or game-specific executors.

Instead identify the shared execution path and fix the first missing generic primitive.

Required reasoning chain:

READ LOCAL SOURCE
→ READ UPSTREAM SOURCE
→ IDENTIFY SEMANTIC LAW
→ MAP TO EXISTING MINIANDROID ABSTRACTION
→ MINIMAL GENERIC FIX
→ RUNTIME GRAPHICAL VERIFICATION
→ CROSS-FAMILY REGRESSION

SOURCE-FIRST ≠ PORT-FIRST.

## Target families

Build and document a matrix covering at least:

1. Base/View applications
2. 2D Canvas/View games
3. SurfaceView/game-loop applications
4. Messaging: Telegram / Signal / WhatsApp-like architecture
5. Social/media: Instagram-like architecture
6. Compose applications: Dooz + an independent Compose target
7. WebView/HTML5 applications or games

For each family record:
- Representative APK/target
- Expected execution path
- Android/framework primitives required
- Current MiniAndroid coverage
- First known divergence
- Exact runtime evidence
- Number of other targets sharing the primitive
- Genericity status
- Verification level
- Regression target
- Next minimal root
- Authoritative source reference

## Expected execution patterns

### Base/View
Activity → Context → View hierarchy → measure → layout → draw → input → state

### 2D Canvas
Activity → View/Canvas → Bitmap/Paint/Text → frame → input → state

### Surface/game loop
Activity → SurfaceView/Surface → timing → loop → Canvas/render → input → frame

### Messaging
Activity → lifecycle → View/Recycler/Layout → Text/Image → measure/layout/draw → storage/network/background → input/state

Telegram, Signal and WhatsApp-like targets are evidence for shared primitives, not separate implementations.

### Social/media
Activity → feed/layout → scrolling → image/media loading → async/background → storage/cache → measure/layout/draw → input/state

### Compose
Activity → app-bundled Compose runtime → Composer/SlotTable/Applier/ComposeNode → LayoutNode → measure/layout/draw

Do not build a large local Compose runtime unless evidence proves a genuinely missing generic primitive cannot be solved in Base.

### WebView/HTML5
Activity → WebView → HTML/CSS/JS → rendering/input/state

## Current known constraint

CONT-19/#383 established that Dooz reaches the Compose composition path and then currently encounters a generic Base/heap/field divergence (F-NEW-271).

Therefore F-NEW-271 / generic Base investigation remains higher priority than wholesale Compose work.

Do not reopen the rejected large local Compose runtime approach.

## Required phases

### Phase A — Inventory
Create the family matrix and select representative targets.

### Phase B — Execution-path proof
For each target prove the actual path with runtime trace, not assumptions.

### Phase C — Shared-primitive clustering
Cluster failures by the first shared missing primitive.

Example: if Telegram + Signal + another app all fail at the same RecyclerView/View/field/layout primitive, classify it as Base/framework work.

### Phase D — Source-first semantic validation
For each high-value root:
- inspect MiniAndroid local implementation;
- inspect authoritative upstream source;
- state the semantic law;
- explain the mapping to MiniAndroid;
- identify the smallest reusable correction.

Use AOSP for Android framework semantics and AndroidX/Compose source for Compose semantics. For engines, use the relevant engine source when needed.

### Phase E — Minimal generic fix
Only implement a fix after genericity is demonstrated.

No:
- package-name checks
- APK-specific branches
- screenshot hacks
- exception suppression
- arbitrary PC advancement
- fake objects
- large subsystem rewrites

### Phase F — Runtime proof
Every accepted fix must include:
- APK SHA
- runtime commit
- Activity/lifecycle evidence
- first-divergence trace
- object/field identity where relevant
- ViewTree/provenance
- state change where applicable
- draw operations
- dimensions
- unique colors / meaningful pixel metrics
- screenshot SHA
- repeated runs
- independent-family regression

### Phase G — Coverage decision
Report which primitives benefit how many targets/families.

A fix that helps only one APK is not sufficient evidence of a generic root.

## Required output

Create/update a persistent evidence artifact at evidence/<wave>/EXECUTION_FAMILY_MATRIX.md.

The report must contain a row for every representative target and a summary of shared primitives.

Use statuses:
IMPLEMENTED / TESTED / OBSERVED / PARTIAL / BLOCKED / PENDING / SUPERSEDED

Use verification levels:
UNEXECUTED / LOADED / LIFECYCLE_VERIFIED / RENDER_STARTED / FRAME_CAPTURED / VISUALLY_PARTIAL / VISUALLY_VERIFIED / INTERACTION_VERIFIED / FULLY_VERIFIED

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Family matrix exists and is committed.
- [ ] At least the 7 families above are represented.
- [ ] At least 2 independent targets are used for shared-primitive claims where practical.
- [ ] Telegram/Signal/WhatsApp/Instagram are treated as family coverage targets, not app-specific implementations.
- [ ] 2D games have an explicit Canvas/Bitmap/Input/Timing execution model.
- [ ] Compose has an explicit execution model but no blind large local Compose port.
- [ ] WebView/HTML5 has an explicit execution model.
- [ ] First-divergence evidence exists for each tested target.
- [ ] Shared failures are clustered before any fix is selected.
- [ ] Upstream source is consulted for every selected semantic root.
- [ ] Any fix is generic and independently regression-tested.
- [ ] Graphical proof is produced for representative targets.
- [ ] Cross-family regressions are recorded.
- [ ] Final report states which roots are Base, which are family-specific, and which are truly app-specific.
- [ ] No unsupported done claim: every checkbox has evidence/status.

## Priority

P0 architecture/coverage mapping.
P1 generic Base roots discovered by the matrix.
P2 family-specific primitives only after Base coverage is sufficient.

The immediate objective is not to make one named app work. It is to make the runtime increasingly capable of executing whole families of Android software.
