issues.title: [CONT-24 EXPERIMENT — measurement only] Skeleton-Light: one 490-line generic skeleton painter vs ~10.6K lines of graphics machinery — measured impact
issues.body:
## What this is (and is not)

Per the wave directive, this is a **measurement-only experiment**: "instead of emulating the graphics stack piece by piece, fully simulate ONE generic skeleton-light — by adding one skeleton-light, thousands of lines for graphics and roots and others were deleted. Test it ONLY as a test; if it has impact, explain the measured impact here. Do not change our main line."

- **No main-line change.** Everything lives on the branch `cont24/skeleton-light-experiment` (commit 12bd2a39), behind `MINIANDROID_SKELETON_LIGHT=1` (default OFF, proven byte-inert).
- The user's "thousands of lines deleted" claim was **confirmed quantitatively for the frame-production role** — and the costs were measured too. Full evidence: `evidence/cont24/SKEL_LIGHT_EXPERIMENT.md`, runs `run/cont24/`.

## 1. What was built

| item | size |
|---|---|
| `miniandroid/src/renderer/skeleton_light.{h,cpp}` — ONE self-contained painter: compact measure (MATCH_PARENT/WRAP_CONTENT/margins/orientation) + paint (real `bg_color` fills, 5×7 ASCII texts, depth-cycled outlines, image placeholders, clickable ticks, GONE/INVISIBLE) | **490 lines** |
| env-gated hook in `stage_render_frame_impl` (+ census mapping) | +50 lines |
| Makefile | 2 lines |

**Zero-dependency proof (link level, checkable):** `nm -u build/renderer/skeleton_light.o` → 14 undefined symbols = C++ runtime + `getenv` + `roundf` + `std::string::find` + `ViewShadow::find_node`. **No reference at all** to canvas_shadow, text_shaper, bitmap_font_data, vector_decode, gif_decoder, bitmap_shadow, state_list.

**Inertness sanity:** gate OFF on the experiment binary → anchors byte-identical (dooz `d602648e8e401895`, opencalc `a976d2f9fb675cb3`).

## 2. The "thousands of lines" arithmetic (the user's claim, measured)

For the **classic-canvas frame family**, machinery the skeleton path does not execute:

| file | lines |
|---|---|
| engine draw walk (`execution_engine.cpp` 2903–5162) | ~2,140 of 2,260 |
| `canvas_shadow.cpp` (Canvas-op emulation) | 2,261 |
| `text_shaper.cpp` (HarfBuzz/FreeType/FriBidi) | 1,166 |
| `bitmap_font_data.h` | 2,028 (skeleton: 672-byte 5×7 font) |
| `software_renderer.cpp` | ~1,284 of 1,434 |
| `vector_decode.cpp` | 949 |
| `bitmap_shadow.cpp` (paint decode) | 604 |
| `state_list.cpp` | 176 |
| **total** | **~10.6K lines** |

→ **490 lines replace the role of ~10.6K lines for producing an informative frame of a View-family app.** Scope honesty: this is the *frame-production role* — the same files still serve DEX-side Canvas calls, measure, and app-logic APIs, so they are not wholesale-deletable from the repo.

Registry cross-check: **255 of 586 roots (43.5%) are graphics-labeled**; 105 of them ROOT-CAUSED-FIXED — a large share of past root work exists because of the per-op graphics emulation whose frame role the skeleton covers.

## 3. A/B battery — 11 targets (canonical sweep, 5 frames / 15 s)

| target | family | base → skel colors | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| dooz | Compose | 1 (blank) → 2 | structure hint; **rc flip 1→0 = verdict inflation (§4)** |
| telegram | complex | 1 (blank) → 2 | **first non-blank pixels at this protocol** (structure only) |
| ballbreak | Canvas game | 1 (blank) → 2 | structure hint |
| opencalc | View | 217 → 4 | structure visible; fidelity LOSS |
| unote | View | 128 → 6 | fidelity loss, structure ok |
| microtimer | View | 120 → 7 | fidelity loss, structure ok |
| gmdice | View game | 187 → 7 | fidelity loss, structure ok |
| tictactoe | View game | 364 → 5 | full-coverage structure (2.09M px) |
| notes | AppCompat | 65 → 2 | wash (baseline flat) |
| **flappycow** | Surface/GL game | **507 (SUCCESS) → 1 (blank, rc 1)** | **REGRESSION — skeleton replaced the surface composite** |
| stopwatch | View | 1 (blank) → 1 (unchanged) | tree absent at frame time → skeleton cannot help |

Determinism ×3: dooz `4163ee86125d52c0`, tictactoe `4bce76f0a58269a7`, telegram `e88f290b3550711a` — byte-identical. Telegram/notes/ballbreak skel frames are byte-identical to each other: the "generic minimum frame" is target-independent.

## 4. The hazards (measured, not hypothetical)

1. **Verdict inflation — proven.** dooz flipped rc 1→0 (`Status: SUCCESS`) because painting the ComposeView *wrapper outline* set `app_draw_ops>0` → REAL_APP_CONTENT proof. That is the FRAMEWORK_CHROME_ONLY ≠ REAL_APP_CONTENT violation. A production skeleton needs its own verdict class (`SKELETON_STRUCTURE_ONLY`), strictly weaker.
2. **Surface-family destruction — proven.** flappycow 507-color SUCCESS → blank + rc 1. Family routing is mandatory; a global paint hook must never replace the GL/surface composite.
3. **Fidelity loss — proven.** Every rich render collapses to structure; non-ASCII text (opencalc ×6) becomes placeholder bars.
4. **No help where the tree is absent** (stopwatch). The skeleton cannot invent a tree.
5. **Log masking.** opencalc "uncaught" grep hits 9→3: the same 2 exception roots simply stop repeating per frame when the draw walk is skipped. Fewer log lines ≠ fewer defects.

## 5. Verdict — where the idea helps, where it cannot

**Wins:** (a) the machinery arithmetic (490 vs ~10.6K, link-proven); (b) first pixels on baseline-blank View-family faces + structure on the Compose blank; (c) a deterministic generic minimum frame = a cheap corpus-wide smoke-test instrument; (d) a fallback frame class for future wave evidence when the real pipeline is blocked.

**Cannot win:** Compose *content* (dooz's real blocker is F-NEW-277 recomposition starvation — composition, not paint), surfaces/games (must keep compositing), glyph fidelity, absent trees.

**Bottom line:** a legitimate **diagnostic + fallback layer with its own verdict class**, not a main-line replacement. The main line stays source-first.

## 6. Bonus finding + unapplied-achievements inventory

- **Stale asset:** `view_renderer.cpp` (684 LOC, UNIFIED_007 era) **no longer compiles** against the current ViewShadow API — discovered when reusing it was attempted; it is itself a scattered achievement (recommend: delete or repair as the shared measure pass).
- Inventory pushed as `evidence/cont24/UNAPPLIED_ACHIEVEMENTS.md`: **16 RESEARCHED-NOT-IMPLEMENTED** rows (12 of them one generic jni_bridge classification law — highest single-law ROI), **110 PARTIAL**, **72 UNPROVEN**, the reverted CONT-23 lifecycle patch (probe locked 5/5), the CONT-12 real-Compose oracle (test-only, proved F-NEW-266), and the 10,258-LOC deleted experiment chain (f9f3013d).

## 7. Reproduce

```bash
git checkout cont24/skeleton-light-experiment
cd miniandroid && timeout 570 make -j1 BUILD_DIR=build     # 614677b60931b94f
bash scripts/cont24_battery.sh run/cont24/bin/miniandroid_baseline_fa88902f run/cont24/base base
bash scripts/cont24_battery.sh miniandroid/build/miniandroid run/cont24/skel skel
```

*Labels: experiment, measurement-only, no-main-line-change.*

issues.title: BASE-FIRST: Establish a Generic Graphical Runtime Baseline
issues.body:
# BASE-FIRST: Establish a Generic Graphical Runtime Baseline

## Goal

From this point forward, MiniAndroid's primary target is the generic Android runtime and the broad application/game corpus, not one specific app such as Dooz.

Dooz/Compose remains a useful boundary test, but it must NOT become the definition of Base completion.

The immediate goal is to prove that the Base runtime can install/load/run several technically different, simple real applications and games and produce real graphical output that can be measured and reproduced.

## Important context

We already have HTML5/WebView execution working for some targets. We also have simple apps/games that were originally useful for building the runtime foundation.

Do not throw away that progress. Use those targets as a controlled baseline and expand from them.

The previous Dooz/Compose work must not be treated as the next mandatory implementation wave. Full Compose runtime work should be deferred until there is evidence that it has significant cross-app value.

## What this Issue is NOT

- Not a request to implement every Android API.
- Not a request to complete Jetpack Compose.
- Not a request to make Dooz render at any cost.
- Not a request for app-specific hacks.
- Not a request to maximize an implemented-API counter.
- Not a request to run hundreds of apps blindly.
- Not a request to restart source reading from line 1.

The runtime must remain generic.

## Phase 0 — Lock the current Base

Before changing code:
- Record current HEAD/commit, build command, runtime launch command, screenshot/capture method.
- Record current HTML5/WebView working examples.
- Record current successful native/simple-app examples.
- Reuse existing evidence instead of reproducing already-proven behavior.
- Do not modify the architecture during this phase.

## Phase 1 — Select a Small Representative Baseline

Select at least:

### Native/simple games
At least 2 simple games, preferably using different rendering paths where possible: one simple View/Canvas-based game and one other simple graphical game using a different lightweight path.

### Simple applications
At least 2 simple native applications: one basic UI application and one exercising state/resources/files/preferences or another common Android facility.

### HTML5/WebView
At least 1 simple HTML5 game/application using the WebView/HTML5 path that is already working.

If existing corpus candidates already satisfy these categories, use them. Do not invent new infrastructure merely to create test apps.

Record APK/package identity, APK SHA-256, source/corpus origin if known, rendering technology, and reason for selection.

## Phase 2 — Establish the graphical proof standard

A target is NOT considered successful merely because APK parsed, classes loaded, process exited successfully, Activity was created, an API counter increased, a non-crashing run occurred, or a screenshot file exists.

For each baseline target collect the strongest available evidence:
1. APK identity/SHA
2. runtime commit
3. Activity/lifecycle evidence
4. ViewTree or equivalent UI ownership/provenance
5. draw/render operations
6. screenshot dimensions
7. unique-color count
8. non-background/meaningful pixel evidence
9. screenshot SHA-256
10. input/state-change evidence where applicable
11. repeated-run evidence

Use the existing verification vocabulary:
UNEXECUTED / LOADED / LIFECYCLE_VERIFIED / RENDER_STARTED / FRAME_CAPTURED / VISUALLY_PARTIAL / VISUALLY_VERIFIED / INTERACTION_VERIFIED / FULLY_VERIFIED

Do not promote a target without evidence.

## Phase 3 — Find the first generic divergence

For every baseline target that fails or renders incorrectly, do NOT immediately patch the final symptom.

Trace the earliest meaningful divergence through: APK/install semantics; DEX execution; Java object/heap identity; Context/Application/Activity; resources and AssetManager; filesystem/persistence; ViewTree; measure/layout; Canvas/draw; Bitmap/image loading; input; state changes; screenshot/framebuffer.

For every discovered root record: target, observable failure, earliest divergence, source file/function/line or stable anchor, Android/Java/runtime semantic law, existing implementation, evidence-backed root cause, generic impact, minimal fix, exact test, runtime proof, and status.

Use statuses: IMPLEMENTED / TESTED / OBSERVED / PARTIAL / BLOCKED / PENDING / SUPERSEDED.

## Phase 4 — Fix only high-value shared roots

Prioritize roots when evidence indicates they affect multiple applications/games. Examples: object/heap identity; Java collection/iterator semantics; array/null/bounds semantics; filesystem/install roots; resources/assets; Context/Application/Activity lifecycle; ViewTree creation; measure/layout; Canvas/drawing; Bitmap decoding; input/state; common framework APIs.

Do NOT implement a root solely because one app happens to call it.

Do NOT use exception suppression as a compatibility strategy, arbitrary PC advancement, random fallback method dispatch, fake objects, app-specific branches, or screenshot-only hacks.

If an exception suppression or fallback is necessary for investigation, mark it diagnostic-only and do not count it as a completed compatibility fix.

## Phase 5 — Graphical success gate

Minimum target: 2 simple native games + 2 simple native apps + 1 HTML5/WebView target.

At least 4 of the 5 should reach VISUALLY_VERIFIED or better. At least 2 targets must demonstrate an actual state/input change visible in the resulting frame.

The HTML5/WebView target is a separate rendering backend, not evidence that the native Android View runtime is complete.

If a target fails, record the exact reason. Do not hide the failure by suppressing exceptions.

## Phase 6 — Cross-target regression

After each generic fix, rerun the smallest relevant regression set, confirm the original failing target improved, confirm at least one unrelated target did not regress where relevant, and retain screenshot/trace evidence.

Do not run the entire corpus after every tiny change. Use focused regression first, then expand only when the root demonstrates cross-target impact.

## Phase 7 — Compose / Dooz decision gate

Dooz is explicitly not the current Base milestone. Keep the existing Dooz findings as research evidence.

Before starting a large Compose implementation, answer: how many current corpus targets require Compose; which missing primitives are shared; which are already provided by Base; what percentage of the target corpus would benefit; whether a minimal Compose subset unlocks several targets; and whether the work is generic and reusable.

Only if evidence demonstrates meaningful cross-app benefit should full Compose work become a major wave.

## Required final report

Update this Issue with a table containing: Target | Technology | Current status | First divergence | Root cause | Generic fix | Screenshot proof | Interaction proof.

Then provide: Native games visually verified X/2; native apps visually verified X/2; HTML5/WebView visually verified X/1; interactive targets X; shared roots fixed X; regressions X; remaining blockers X.

Choose exactly one final decision: BASE READY FOR NEXT CORPUS WAVE / BASE NOT READY — SHARED ROOTS REMAIN / BASE BLOCKED — SPECIFIC INFRASTRUCTURE GAP / COMPOSE NOW JUSTIFIED BY CROSS-APP EVIDENCE.

## Strict instructions to the primary coder

You are primarily the validator and runtime investigator, not a blind implementation agent.

Do not spend days rediscovering known problems if repository history, previous reports, tests, or attached evidence already establishes them.

For every claim: READ → TRACE → VERIFY → TEST ONLY IF NEEDED → RECORD.

Do not accept a historical claim merely because it sounds plausible. Do not reject it merely because you have not personally reproduced it yet.

Use ACCEPTED / REJECTED / PARTIAL / NEEDS REPRODUCTION and explain why.

The purpose of this Issue is to establish a real generic graphical Base that can support many Android applications and games.

Dooz is only one test case.

The success condition is not 'Dooz works.'

The success condition is: MiniAndroid can run multiple independent real apps/games through different common Android paths and produce reproducible, meaningful graphical output and state changes without app-specific hacks.

issues.body:
# A1–A104 Knowledge Transfer: Runtime Findings, Visual Proof, and Review Checklist

> **Purpose:** Transfer the complete knowledge package from the previous investigator to the primary coder. This is NOT a request to start the investigation from zero and NOT permission to rewrite or replace the previous work. The primary coder must first inspect the source, commits, existing evidence, screenshots, and reproduction instructions; then mark each claim ACCEPTED, REJECTED, PARTIAL, or UNVERIFIED with reasons. Re-run tests only where source/evidence review cannot establish the claim or where a claim explicitly requires runtime reproduction.

## Persistent knowledge file

The full current audit ledger and review instructions are also committed in the repository so the coder can read them without relying on issue rendering: [`docs/knowledge-transfer/A1_A104_PRIMARY_CODER_AUDIT.md`](https://github.com/Sh-TB/MiniAndroid-Compatibility-Runtime/blob/main/docs/knowledge-transfer/A1_A104_PRIMARY_CODER_AUDIT.md) (commit `862ec6297fcae624f4891b14e947d5e1ad84b936`). This file mirrors the current Issue audit body; it is **not** the original ZIP archive.

## 1. Mandatory instructions for the primary coder

- Read `CONSTITUTION_V2.md` first, then `docs/S92_GRAPHICS_VERIFICATION.md`.
- Review this knowledge transfer as prior work to audit, not as an untrusted list to discard and rebuild from scratch.
- For each numbered claim in this Issue, mark one: **[ ] ACCEPTED FROM SOURCE/EVIDENCE  [ ] REJECTED  [ ] PARTIAL  [ ] NEEDS REPRODUCTION**.
- Every decision must include: **reason, source file/function/line, existing evidence inspected, and next action**.
- Do not blindly accept the previous investigator's conclusions. Equally, do not blindly reject them or repeat all tests from zero. Check existing commits, traces, screenshots, hashes, ViewTree evidence and test artifacts first.
- If source and evidence already prove a claim, mark it accepted and cite them. If only a hypothesis, label it PARTIAL/NEEDS REPRODUCTION.
- Keep the original results and historical status. Do not silently rewrite history or promote an app based on an old binary.
- Do not make broad architecture changes or start a multi-week feature implementation as part of this review. This is primarily a **source/evidence review and claim-verification task**.
- Do not close an app's visual failure because its APK loads, lifecycle callbacks fire, a ViewTree exists, a test passes, or a PNG exists.
- If a claim is rejected, explain exactly why and what evidence contradicts it. If the source hint/line differs, record the actual location.
- Update this issue claim-by-claim. At the end, report counts of ACCEPTED, REJECTED, PARTIAL, and NEEDS REPRODUCTION, plus the remaining actual blockers.

## 2. Essential visual-verification law: S92 Verification Ladder

Use these verdicts exactly and do not promote an app without evidence:

- `UNEXECUTED` — no screenshot produced.
- `LOADED` — APK parsed, nothing more.
- `LIFECYCLE_VERIFIED` — onCreate/onStart/onResume dispatched.
- `RENDER_STARTED` — renderer initialized.
- `FRAME_CAPTURED` — screenshot exists but is flat/single-color.
- `VISUALLY_PARTIAL` — few colors, likely only background or incomplete content.
- `VISUALLY_VERIFIED` — multiple colors and real app content.
- `INTERACTION_VERIFIED` — tap dispatched and app state visibly changed.
- `FULLY_VERIFIED` — interaction proof plus three byte-identical runs.

Non-negotiable rules:
1. A screenshot existing does not mean graphics loaded. A flat one-color PNG is FRAME_CAPTURED, not VISUALLY_VERIFIED.
2. A callback firing does not prove interaction. Prove pixel/state change.
3. A ViewTree existing does not prove graphics correctness. Pixels are the truth.
4. Use 1080×1920 by default because the runtime uses density 2.0. At 540×960, glyphs may be drawn outside the framebuffer (reported y=1156 when framebuffer height is 960).
5. The source document reports a CLI resolution correction that changed gmdice from 1 to 113 unique colors and glxy from 1 to 20,421 unique colors.
6. FULLY_VERIFIED requires three runs with byte-identical screenshot SHA256 values.
7. Fresh evidence is required for a changed binary. Never carry old screenshot/test evidence forward to a new binary.
8. Never invent AOSP semantics. If the contract is unknown, preserve UNKNOWN until verified.

Reported classification heuristic in the transferred material:
```python
if unique_colors <= 1:
    verdict = "FRAME_CAPTURED"
elif unique_colors <= 3:
    verdict = "VISUALLY_PARTIAL"
elif unique_colors >= 8 and non_dominant_pixels >= 1000:
    verdict = "VISUALLY_VERIFIED"
```
Check this heuristic against the project's actual S92 law before changing it; do not silently replace the law.

## 3. A1–A104 patch history and findings to audit

### A1–A50: Compose setup (dooz focus)
- Created ComposeView, AndroidComposeView, WrappedComposition.
- Created internal Compose classes c1 and N/a.
- Called LF/A0.a() (Compose setContent).
- Reported outcome: composition did not materialize because SlotTable, Composer, Applier, and LayoutNode were not implemented.
- Treat this as historical implementation context, not proof that Compose now works.

### A51–A52: File null receiver guards
- Reported bug: File.getName() / File.getAbsolutePath() called on a null receiver.
- Reported fix: null-receiver guards in File shadow methods.
- Review the actual source and commit before accepting the fix claim.

### A61: dialog_shadow.cpp null dereference
- Reported bug: `find_node(row_id)->children.push_back(...)` when find_node returned null.
- Reported fix: call `get_or_create_node(row_id)` before accessing children.

### A62: shell injection through popen
- Reported bug: shell command assembled with APK path in `popen("unzip -p '" + apk_path + "'...")`.
- Reported fix: replaced shell execution with an in-process ZIP parser.
- Confirm the current code no longer sends untrusted APK paths through a shell.

### A64: hard-coded /tmp path
- Reported bug: default File path hard-coded to `/tmp/miniandroid/files`.
- Reported fix: use `Storage::package_data_dir()`.

### A68: stale ViewTree after finish()
- Reported bug: Activity.finish() did not clear content_view_id, so renderer kept drawing an old ViewTree.
- Reported fix: clear content_view_id after finish(), reported in `execution_engine.cpp` around line 7490.

### A91: onPostCreate dispatch (PARTIAL / wrong path)
- Reported issue: games such as minos create GameView in onPostCreate, not onCreate.
- Initial patch put onPostCreate dispatch in Path A (multi-DEX index lookup, around line 2083), not Path B (single-DEX around line 1814).
- This patch did not cover most single-DEX apps.

### A92: framebuffer resolution mismatch (verification-tooling fix; no source change)
- Reported issue: 540×960 framebuffer with density 2.0 clipped glyphs outside the framebuffer.
- Required default: `--width 1080 --height 1920`.
- Reported effect: gmdice 1→113 unique colors; glxy 1→20,421 unique colors.
- Review the screenshots and actual invocation evidence before accepting those promotions.

### A93: onPostCreate dispatch in Path B
- Reported fix: add dispatch in the single-DEX Path B too, between onActivityCreated and onActivityPostCreated.
- File: `miniandroid/src/dex/dalvik_engine.cpp`, reported around line 1864; log marker `[A93-POSTCREATE]`.
- Reported effect: minos reaches createGame(); IMPLEMENTED API count rose from 137 to 256.

### A94: Display.getWidth/getHeight
- Reported issue: minos DisplayUtils.getDisplaySize called missing Display.getWidth/getHeight; zero dimensions caused empty maze dimensions and Random.nextInt(0).
- Reported fix: stubs return 1080/1920, consistent with existing getMetrics/getSize device profile; also added Display.getDisplayInfo safety net.
- File: `miniandroid/src/dex/dalvik_engine.cpp`, reported around line 35665.

### A95: View.getWidth/getHeight before layout
- Reported issue: View.post() runnables queued during onCreate drain before the first traversal/layout. GameView constructor read container width=0, producing zero cell size and zero maze dimensions.
- Reported fallback order:
  1. measured_right - measured_left if positive;
  2. measured_width if positive;
  3. if width == -1 (MATCH_PARENT), parent's measured_width or screen width (1080);
  4. explicit positive width;
  5. otherwise zero.
- File: `miniandroid/src/framework/android_shadows.cpp`, reported around line 4330.
- Reported effect: minos container 1080×1920, cols=6, rows=10, cellSize=180; IMPLEMENTED APIs rose from 262 to 688.

### A101: HashMap.size() always returned zero
- Reported bug: HashMap.size() was a stub returning zero regardless of entries.
- Reported fix: count real `key_`-prefixed fields in the heap object, excluding `__` internal fields.
- File: `miniandroid/src/dex/dalvik_engine.cpp`, reported around line 44238.
- Primary coder must inspect how this interacts with the actual HashMap storage/dispatch path.

### A102: ArrayDeque/LinkedList omitted from collection class-name gate
- Reported bug: ArrayList handler recognized ArrayList/List-like names but missed ArrayDeque and LinkedList; minos uses ArrayDeque for maze cells.
- Reported fix: add ArrayDeque and LinkedList to the handler gate around line 44793 in `miniandroid/src/dex/dalvik_engine.cpp`.
- The source document includes this implementation sketch:
```cpp
if (class_name == "Ljava/util/ArrayList;" ||
    class_name.find("ArrayList") != std::string::npos ||
    class_name.find("List;") != std::string::npos ||
    class_name == "Ljava/util/ArrayDeque;" ||
    class_name.find("ArrayDeque") != std::string::npos ||
    class_name == "Ljava/util/LinkedList;" ||
    class_name.find("LinkedList") != std::string::npos) {
```
- Verify the actual committed implementation and ensure dispatch does not shadow or misclassify other collection classes.

### A102 investigation: Map.keySet returns a view with the wrong class (OBSERVED / NOT FIXED)
- Reported observation: `CollectionShadow::dispatch` F-064, around line 1036 of `android_shadows.cpp`, creates a HashSet view with view_elements copied from map entries.
- It allocates `Ljava/util/HashSet;`, but later the receiver's class_descriptor is reported as `Ljava/util/ArrayList;`.
- hasNext then checks `state->view_elements`, which is empty for the ArrayList-classed object.
- Reported downstream chain: minos MazeFactory.getUnvisitedNeighbours returns an empty collection; Random.nextInt(0) throws IllegalArgumentException; zero pixels.
- Status in source package: deep shadow-dispatch bug observed, not fixed. Do not promote minos based on A102's collection-gate fix.
- Candidate explanations in source package: heap object ID reuse or iterator handler around line 914 returning the wrong class. These are hypotheses, not established facts.

### A103: three-run repeatability verification
- Reported method: run each of seven INTERACTION_VERIFIED apps three times at 1080×1920, frames=5, max-seconds=15, and compare SHA256 of screenshot.png.
- Reported result: all seven produced byte-identical screenshots across all three runs; together with interaction proof, promoted to FULLY_VERIFIED.
- Apps reported: 2048, snake_deluxe, tetris, tictactoe_deluxe, minicraft, snakeneon, gmdice.
- Primary coder should inspect existing hash records and binary identity first; rerun only if evidence is missing, stale, or tied to a different binary.

### A104: dooz (TicTacToe) — Compose Navigation boundary
- APK: io.github.yamin8000.dooz v18.
- SHA256 reported: `d81292cd346dcb23b04488bca400ca95af0f6eaa4aefefd31f847fe535cbdc17`.
- Reported execution: 20,166 IMPLEMENTED APIs; 253 STUBBED; 0 MISSING; 0 ERROR.
- ViewTree: ComposeView → AndroidComposeView, 0 children, 0 draw ops.
- Screenshot: one unique color, RGB (250,250,250), white background.
- Reported cause: NavHost calls addNavigator("composable", ComposableNavigator()) during composition, but composition never materializes because Compose runtime internals are missing: SlotTable, Composer, Applier, LayoutNode.
- Reported error: could not find Navigator with name "composable".
- Honest verdict: FRAME_CAPTURED, not visually verified. The transferred material estimates full Compose runtime as WAVE 8 / multi-week work. The coder's task here is to verify this boundary and evidence, not to begin implementing Compose.

## 4. Final reported verification state at A104

These are transferred claims to audit, not automatically accepted facts:

| App | Reported verdict | Unique colors | Tap pixel change | Reported 3-run SHA prefix |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| 2048 | FULLY_VERIFIED | 81 | 14.32% at UP button | 59ca1526611c4622 ×3 |
| snake_deluxe | FULLY_VERIFIED | 132 | 0.81% at START button | 34a712689ce66e58 ×3 |
| tetris | FULLY_VERIFIED | 135 | 1.85% at START button | f360daa244cfca8d ×3 |
| tictactoe_deluxe | FULLY_VERIFIED | 227 | 1.76% at button 5 | af6094295ecb50e3 ×3 |
| minicraft | FULLY_VERIFIED | 128 | 0.20% at UP button | b0876952f41e4af2 ×3 |
| snakeneon | FULLY_VERIFIED | 61 | 0.91% at UP button | cc986d4b4d3ec3f3 ×3 |
| gmdice | FULLY_VERIFIED | 113 | 0.81% at 3D20 button | f3b483fe7b7cf51b ×3 |
| blockbuster | VISUALLY_VERIFIED | 83 | n/a (WebView) | — |
| glxy | VISUALLY_VERIFIED | 20,421 | n/a (GLSurfaceView) | — |
| dooz | FRAME_CAPTURED | 1 | n/a | — |
| minos | FRAME_CAPTURED | 1 | n/a | — |
| bullseye | FRAME_CAPTURED | 1 | n/a | — |
| battleship | FRAME_CAPTURED | 1 | n/a | — |

Reported total: 7 FULLY_VERIFIED + 2 VISUALLY_VERIFIED + 4 FRAME_CAPTURED = 13 apps. **The source document elsewhere says “5 FRAME_CAPTURED” and “14 apps”; this arithmetic/list discrepancy must be explicitly reconciled by inspecting the actual artifacts. Do not silently fix the report or choose one number without evidence.**

## 5. Known boundaries / next technical work (not authorization to start coding immediately)

### Boundary 1: Compose runtime internals — WAVE 8
Affected: dooz, battleship, other Jetpack Compose apps.
Missing internals listed: SlotTable, Composer, Applier, LayoutNode. AndroidComposeView.dispatchDraw reportedly has zero draw operations and composition never materializes.
Proposed future approach: port/implement the needed behavior from AOSP androidx.compose.runtime and androidx.compose.ui sources. This is a substantial project; first verify the current boundary and evidence.

### Boundary 2: AppCompat setContentView(int) inflation
Affected: bullseye.
Reported cause: AppCompatDelegateImpl.setContentView(resId) inflates XML (52 views reported), but the inflated root is not attached as a child of ContentFrameLayout.
Reported ViewTree: FitWindowsLinearLayout → ViewStubCompat + ContentFrameLayout (0 children).
Proposed investigation: trace AppCompatDelegateImpl.setContentView → LayoutInflater.inflate and verify the inflated root is attached to contentParent.

### Boundary 3: Map.keySet view class / iterator bug
Affected: minos.
Reported chain: HashSet view allocated; later receiver class descriptor becomes ArrayList; hasNext checks an empty view_elements state; empty neighbours cause Random.nextInt(0) and zero pixels.
Investigate why class_descriptor changes and trace object identity through keySet, iterator, hasNext and next. The suggestion that heap object ID reuse or the iterator handler is responsible is a hypothesis.

### Boundary 4: WebView HTML5/JS pipeline — WAVE 10+
Affected: blockbuster (partial).
Reported state: WebView chrome renders but HTML5 game canvas does not. QuickJS exists, but DOM/JS/Canvas pipeline remains partial.
Future work: complete WebView HTML5/Canvas rendering pipeline after verifying the current state.

## 6. Architecture map and source-reading order

1. `CONSTITUTION_V2.md` — engineering laws; read first.
2. `docs/S92_GRAPHICS_VERIFICATION.md` — graphics verification ladder.
3. `miniandroid/src/dex/dalvik_engine.cpp` — main interpreter; start at `execute_apk_with_activity` around line 1556.
4. `miniandroid/src/framework/android_shadows.cpp` — shadow layer; start at `CollectionShadow::dispatch` around line 263.
5. `miniandroid/src/runtime/execution_engine.cpp` — render traversal; start at `stage_render_frame`.
6. `root_registry.json` — source document reports 540 catalogued root causes.
7. `miniandroid/APK_REGISTRY.json` — source document reports 22 test APKs.

Architecture concepts from the transferred material:
- `try_recursive_invoke(class, method, args, ...)`: tries DEX bytecode then falls back to bridge_to_api.
- `bridge_to_api(class_name, method, args, ...)`: framework API bridge/stub layer.
- `try_shadow_dispatch(class_name, method, ...)`: dispatches to shadow classes such as CollectionShadow, ViewShadow, ActivityShadow.
- `throw_deferred(exc_class, message, ...)`: sets pending_exception_ and redirects to catch handler or unwinds frame.
- Shadows: ActivityShadow (lifecycle/content), ViewShadow (tree/measure/layout/draw/getWidth/getHeight), CanvasShadow (draw-op recording), CollectionShadow (List/Map/Set), HandlerShadow (Handler/Looper), TouchDispatcher.
- Render traversal: attach wave → measure → layout → draw-op recording → pixel copy to framebuffer.
- Heap objects have object_id, class_descriptor, and fields; DalvikValue may be INT32, FLOAT, OBJECT_REF, STRING_REF, CLASS_REF, BOOLEAN, etc.
- APK registry catalogs test APKs and stores metadata; APKs must not be committed to the repository (zero-APK policy); APKs live in external cache.

## 7. Reproduction commands from the transferred document

Build:
```bash
cd miniandroid
make -j 1
```

Run a target APK at the correct default resolution:
```bash
./miniandroid/build/miniandroid run <apk_path> \
  --width 1080 --height 1920 \
  --frames 5 --max-seconds 15 \
  -o /tmp/verify_<app>
sha256sum /tmp/verify_<app>/screenshot.png
```

Three-run repeatability:
```bash
for run in 1 2 3; do
  ./miniandroid/build/miniandroid run <apk_path> \
    --width 1080 --height 1920 \
    --frames 5 --max-seconds 15 \
    -o /tmp/repeat_${run}
  sha256sum /tmp/repeat_${run}/screenshot.png
done
```
For FULLY_VERIFIED, all three SHA256 hashes must be identical and interaction evidence must also exist.

Interaction test:
```bash
./miniandroid/build/miniandroid run <apk_path> \
  --width 1080 --height 1920 \
  --frames 15 --max-seconds 30 \
  --tap <x>,<y>@<frame> \
  -o /tmp/tap_test
```
Inspect the actual tap-dispatch marker and compare pre-tap/post-tap pixels. Do not accept callback logs alone.

The original document lists APK paths from a prior investigator's environment under `/home/z/my-project/upload/`, `/home/z/my-project/games_test/apks/`, and `apk_cache/`. These paths may not exist in the primary coder's environment; do not assume they do. Check the registry/cache and preserve the zero-APK repository policy.

## 8. Common pitfalls learned from the campaign

1. Always use 1080×1920 by default with density 2.0; wrong framebuffer size can create misleading flat screenshots.
2. HashMap.size must count actual entries, not return a fixed zero.
3. Collection dispatch gates must include actual collection implementations, but avoid broad gates that accidentally misclassify classes.
4. Shadow view objects must preserve the class they were allocated with; the keySet view class mismatch remains a reported bug.
5. onPostCreate dispatch must exist in both multi-DEX Path A and single-DEX Path B.
6. View.getWidth during pre-layout Runnables can be zero; inspect the measured-size/MATCH_PARENT fallback against the intended law.
7. Reproducible pixel-level proof is stronger than a successful exit code.
8. Three byte-identical runs are mandatory for FULLY_VERIFIED.
9. New binary means new evidence; stale screenshots are not proof for a new build.
10. Never invent API semantics; unknown remains unknown.

## 9. Screenshots and visual artifacts supplied with this transfer

The source ZIP contains:
- `screenshots_v4/FINAL_MOSAIC.png`
- `screenshots_v4/2048.png`
- `screenshots_v4/snake_deluxe.png`
- `screenshots_v4/tetris.png`
- `screenshots_v4/tictactoe_deluxe.png`
- `screenshots_v4/minicraft.png`
- `screenshots_v4/snakeneon.png`
- `screenshots_v4/dooz.png`

The source document additionally refers to prior-environment artifacts:
- `/home/z/my-project/download/screenshots_v4/FINAL_MOSAIC_FULLY_VERIFIED.png`
- `/home/z/my-project/download/screenshots_final/INTERACTION_PROOF.png`
- `/home/z/my-project/download/screenshots_v4/REPEATABILITY_PROOF.md`
- `/home/z/my-project/download/screenshots_final/` before/after tap pairs
- `/home/z/my-project/download/repeatability/` SHA stamps

The ZIP's screenshots are not automatically attached to this GitHub Issue by this action. The primary coder must inspect the supplied source package/screenshots available to them, compare them with current binary provenance, and attach or link the actual image files in GitHub if the repository workflow supports it. Do not claim that images are attached to this Issue unless the GitHub UI confirms that they are.

## 10. Reported next-step sequence (A105 onward)

These are candidate work items, but first verify their source/evidence and report acceptance/rejection:
- **A105:** investigate/fix Map.keySet view class bug; trace class_descriptor/object ID from keySet through iterator/hasNext/next.
- **A106:** investigate/fix AppCompat setContentView(int) inflation; prove root is attached to ContentFrameLayout.
- **A107+:** Compose runtime internals (SlotTable, Composer, Applier, LayoutNode); major WAVE 8 effort.
- **A108+:** complete WebView HTML5/JS/Canvas pipeline for blockbuster.

## 11. Claim-by-claim review checklist

For every claim above and every specific result in the knowledge transfer, add/update a record in the comments using this format:

```text
Claim/section:
Decision: ACCEPTED FROM SOURCE/EVIDENCE / REJECTED / PARTIAL / NEEDS REPRODUCTION
Source: file :: function/class :: line(s)
Existing evidence inspected: commit / trace / screenshot / hash / ViewTree / test
Reason:
Does this require a new runtime test? YES/NO
If YES, why is existing source/evidence insufficient?
Next action:
Reviewer:
```

Prioritize **source inspection and existing evidence review first**. Do not rerun every app from scratch unless evidence is absent, stale, contradictory, or does not identify the binary. Any new run must record commit/build identity, APK SHA, command, runtime trace, screenshot SHA, unique-color/non-dominant-pixel metrics, ViewTree/provenance, and interaction pixel diff where applicable.

## 12. Required final audit report

- Claims accepted from source/evidence:
- Claims rejected (with reasons):
- Claims partially supported:
- Claims requiring targeted reproduction:
- Any source/evidence contradictions:
- Verified screenshot/image artifacts and their exact locations:
- Binary/commit provenance for each visual verdict:
- Corrected app-count arithmetic:
- Confirmed A105/A106 root cause(s), if already provable from source:
- Remaining blockers:
- Next smallest, highest-value verification step:

**Do not say “all verified” or “fixed” unless the exact claims, source locations, and existing or new evidence justify it. The task is to transfer and audit the previous investigator's knowledge—not to discard it and restart.**

# ADDENDUM: PRIMARY CODER MUST AUDIT, NOT REPEAT THE INVESTIGATION

## A. What this task is (and is not)

This is a knowledge-transfer audit. The previous investigator already supplied a technical path, candidate fixes, exact source locations for several changes, runtime results, screenshots, and verification commands. The primary coder must reuse that work first.

**Do not start 104 experiments from scratch. Do not implement A105+ features in this audit. Do not rerun all apps by default.** Start with the cheapest high-confidence checks:
1. Read the transferred knowledge and project laws.
2. Inspect current git log and commit diffs for the listed A-items.
3. Confirm whether the cited code is present at the cited locations (line numbers may have moved).
4. Check whether existing screenshots, SHA records, test results, and binary identity are already available.
5. Mark claims ACCEPTED / REJECTED / PARTIAL / NEEDS REPRODUCTION / SOURCE GAP.
6. Run only the small number of tests needed to settle material uncertainty or stale/missing evidence.

For each decision, record the exact changed file/function/line or commit diff, evidence inspected, and a short reason. If source confirms a patch and existing regression/evidence proves it, do not rerun it just to repeat the work. If source confirms a patch but behavior is unproven, mark PARTIAL and name the smallest confirming test.

## B. Source-backed patch locations already supplied

| A-item | Reported change | Reported source location | Minimum audit action |
|---|---|---|---|
| A51–A52 | File.getName / File.getAbsolutePath null receiver guards | File shadow methods; exact line not supplied | Inspect current methods and relevant diff; no broad test suite |
| A61 | dialog shadow null dereference fixed with get_or_create_node | dialog_shadow.cpp; exact line not supplied | Inspect diff and guard |
| A62 | Shell injection removed; in-process ZIP parser replaces popen/unzip | APK ZIP reading code; exact line not supplied | Inspect diff and confirm no shell interpolation remains |
| A64 | package-specific storage path replaces hard-coded /tmp path | Storage::package_data_dir() | Inspect diff/call site |
| A68 | Clear content_view_id after Activity.finish() | execution_engine.cpp ~7490 | Inspect finish path and existing test/log |
| A91 | onPostCreate added to Path A only; PARTIAL | dalvik_engine.cpp ~2083 | Confirm why Path B was missed; preserve historical partial status |
| A92 | 1080×1920 verification invocation; no source change | CLI/test commands | Inspect old command + pixel metrics; do not call this a code patch |
| A93 | onPostCreate added to Path B | dalvik_engine.cpp ~1864; [A93-POSTCREATE] | Inspect dispatch ordering and existing minos evidence |
| A94 | Display.getWidth/getHeight and Display.getDisplayInfo | dalvik_engine.cpp ~35665 | Inspect return values against device-profile law |
| A95 | pre-layout View.getWidth/getHeight fallback | android_shadows.cpp ~4330 | Inspect fallback ordering and existing minos dimensions |
| A101 | HashMap.size counts actual key_ fields, excluding __ internals | dalvik_engine.cpp ~44238 | Inspect storage representation and implementation |
| A102 | ArrayDeque/LinkedList added to collection class gate | dalvik_engine.cpp ~44793 | Inspect gate/diff; do not confuse with separate keySet bug |

The available GitHub connector exposes UTF-8 text-file creation but no binary issue-attachment upload action; do not fabricate image URLs. The primary coder should inspect the original archive if it is available to them, otherwise explicitly record that the PNG payloads are unavailable in the GitHub issue.

## G. Required audit result

- A1–A104 ledger with every number present and a status;
- exact current source line / diff / commit for each claimed code fix;
- accepted claims backed by existing evidence;
- rejected claims with contradicting evidence;
- partial claims and the smallest test needed to settle them;

The objective is to transfer knowledge and make the primary coder a reviewer and minimal tester, not to make them repeat the previous investigator's hours of discovery.

issues.title: Unverified Claims — Complete Runtime Evidence Audit
issues.body:
# Unverified Claims — Complete Runtime Evidence Audit

## Purpose

This issue is the complete evidence audit for every claim made during the blank/white/black-screen investigation.

Every numbered claim must be independently verified, rejected, or explicitly left pending. A passing unit test is not proof that the real App path is fixed. A hypothesis must not be treated as a fact.

## Required record for EVERY claim

Status: VERIFIED / REJECTED / PARTIAL / BLOCKED / PENDING / SUPERSEDED
Source: exact file + function/class + exact or approximate line
Test: exact test file/name or runtime reproduction
Before: observed pre-fix result
After: observed post-fix result
Evidence: runtime trace, object ID, screenshot SHA, ViewTree, metrics, or commit
Reason: why the evidence proves or disproves the claim
Commit: SHA or N/A
Next action: one concrete action

Never invent a source line. If a source hint below is wrong, record the actual location and explain the discrepancy.

---

# A. Rendering / blank-screen claims

1. Renderer performs normal Activity content traversal only when a content root exists (root_id != 0).
2. root_id == 0 means there is no ViewTree for normal traversal.
3. Without a content root the visible frame can consist mainly of the window background.
4. The reported default window background is #303030.
5. Activity/theme windowBackground can replace that default.
6. Missing setContentView can leave the Activity without its intended content tree.
7. A crash in onCreate before setContentView can leave the content root absent.
8. A crash during setContentView can leave content construction incomplete.
9. An NPE during onCreate can produce blank output.
10. The documented F-NEW-156 observation of 19/25 fresh F-Droid APKs producing blank two-color frames is accurate.
11. The 19/25 figure is supported by project evidence.
12. In the cited cases the first-run exception occurred before or during setContentView.
13. An App can call an Android API that has no bridge in dalvik_engine.cpp.
14. An unbridged API can reach a STUBBED path.
15. The relevant stub path can return null.
16. App code can dereference or unwrap that null.
17. That dereference can generate an NPE.
18. The NPE can propagate to the App boundary.
19. EXC-UNCAUGHT-TOP is the relevant uncaught-exception boundary.
20. With strict mode disabled the runtime can continue after an exception by returning null.
21. Continuing with null can hide the original failure and create a later null dereference.
22. In the cited blank-screen chain setContentView does not complete after the exception.
23. That chain can produce a blank/two-color frame.
24. This chain is not sufficient to claim that every blank screen has the same root cause.
25. An unsupported DEX opcode can stop execution.
26. handle_unimplemented can produce HALTED_OPCODE.
27. An unsupported class can stop execution.
28. Interpreter termination can occur before UI creation completes.
29. A Compose App can produce a blank first frame if the Recomposer is not pumped.
30. Recomposer pumping is required for the affected Compose first-frame path.
31. A Custom View can receive a placeholder instead of real rendering.
32. SurfaceView can use a rendering path that is currently incomplete.
33. OpenGL/GL Apps can fail because Surface/GL support is incomplete.
34. libGDX Apps can fail at createGLSurfaceView.
35. A screenshot can capture a surface different from the actual final Activity surface.
36. Multi-Activity Apps can produce a screenshot of the splash window while another window rendered correctly.
37. A screenshot alone is insufficient proof of final-window rendering.
38. WhatsApp can fail through AppContext.set because of a null return.
39. Sliding-panel layouts can produce near-blank frames.
40. OpenCalculator is a concrete example of the SlidingUpPanelLayout issue.
41. The SlidingUpPanelLayout gravity idiom can produce a near-blank layout.

# B. String.split / Pattern claims

42. Pattern.compile is implemented.
43. Pattern.matcher is implemented.
44. Pattern.split was missing from the relevant bridge before e127a71.
45. The missing Pattern.split bridge falls into the generic stub path.
46. That stub path can return a zero-length array.
47. The zero-length result can cause a downstream AGET failure.
48. Two separate String.split handlers existed.
49. The two String.split handlers can behave differently.
50. Duplicate handlers create a dispatch and maintenance risk.
51. Fixing one String.split handler does not necessarily fix the other.
52. The old String.split implementation did not implement full regex semantics.
53. The old implementation mishandled split using the regex whitespace pattern.
54. The old implementation mishandled split using an escaped pipe pattern.
55. The old implementation mishandled split using a character class such as comma/semicolon.
56. The old implementation only partially supported quoted regex syntax.
57. The old implementation retained trailing empty elements.
58. The final substr push could create trailing empty elements.
59. The old split with an empty delimiter could enter an infinite loop.
60. The infinite-loop mechanism is that find with an empty delimiter returns the current position.
61. An empty delimiter has length zero.
62. Therefore the old loop does not advance start.
63. Unbounded parts growth can cause memory exhaustion/OOM.
64. The old empty-delimiter split path was actually observed to hang or timeout.
65. The reported timeout was approximately five seconds.
66. Pattern.compile slash followed by split lacked a working bridge before the fix.
67. The a|b|c escaped-pipe split returned one element before the fix.
68. The a,b,, split retained trailing empty elements before the fix.
69. After the fix Pattern.split returns a real array.
70. After the fix empty-delimiter split terminates.
71. java_split implements the required Java split semantics for the tested cases.
72. java_split uses std::regex.
73. java_split supports quoted-regex syntax.
74. java_split removes trailing empty elements correctly.
75. java_split handles zero-length matches at the start correctly.
76. java_split handles an empty delimiter without nontermination.
77. The active String.split handler uses java_split.

Visual/user goldens: 2048, Snake Deluxe, MiniCraft, HelloWorld.
Determinism/installed-state anchors: dooz, microtimer, unote, opencalc.
Other VERIFIED external real APKs: Fish Rings, FlappyCow, GameMasterDice, TriPeaks, Sudoku and other current VERIFIED/REAL_APP_CONTENT titles.
For each: package, exact APK SHA, source, native libs, ABI tree, ELF machine, PURE_DEX/x86/x86_64/mixed, LAW-001 verdict, L-level, frame verdict, 3-run status and evidence path.
If pure-DEX, explicitly say PURE_DEX. If ARM-only, classify ABI_OUT_OF_SCOPE rather than runtime failure.

## 6. NEW REAL APK CORPUS — MANDATORY
Acquire/build and execute at least 12 new independent APK artifacts; preferably 16–20.
Minimum mix: 6 games + 6 general apps; 2 Compose; 2 non-Compose; 1 native x86/x86_64; 1 resource/image-heavy; 1 storage/SQLite-heavy; 1 WebView-heavy where available; 1 difficult white/partial case; 2 known-good controls.
Use legitimate open-source sources: F-Droid, official upstream GitHub releases, reproducible open-source builds.
Do not commit APK binaries. Cache outside git, SHA-pin and record provenance.
Every candidate: acquire → SHA → intake → LAW-001 → prerequisites → install → hide source APK → installed-identity run → observe → first divergence → L0-L6 → screenshot/provenance → 3 runs where applicable.
Do not select only known-good APKs.

## 7. COMPOSE / R8 / CLASS-NAME HYPOTHESIS
Investigate the hypothesis that R8-renamed/merged Compose class names break runtime dispatch.
Do not assume true or false.
Important: com.example.blockblast and com.sidhant.blockblast are different APK artifacts. Never merge their results.
Build a comparison with at least one successful Compose APK, one failing Compose APK and another independent Compose APK. Prefer R8-renamed and non-renamed examples.
Record APK SHA, Compose-related descriptors, superclass/interface graph, R8 evidence, exact dispatcher lookup key, actual runtime class, receiver identity, method descriptor, first divergence, ViewTree materialization and draw result.
Test exact-string matching, descriptor identity, superclass traversal, interface closure, ClassLoader identity, reflection vs direct dispatch, R8 horizontal class merging and exact method resolution.
Required causal A/B: BASE same failing APK → first divergence; PATCH same APK → divergence removed; ViewTree changes; app-owned draw ops increase; REAL_APP_CONTENT independently proven; unrelated negative control unchanged; second independent Compose APK tested.
Only a generic semantic fix is allowed. No package-name conditionals, no descriptor whitelists, no fake Compose View insertion.
If the hypothesis is false or only partially true, record that honestly.

## 8. F-NEW-084 / LONG INIT
Do not merely increase max-instructions.
Distinguish legitimate long execution, semantic infinite loop, missing operation, pathological initialization and genuine budget exhaustion using progress, repeated PC/method patterns, state changes, bounded probes and negative controls.
Test fairymahjong plus another difficult independent APK.

## 9. WHITE/BLACK/PARTIAL FIRST-DIVERGENCE
For every target: APK → ABI gate → prerequisites → install identity → Activity → ViewTree → measure → layout → draw → surface → buffer → composition → capture.
Use REAL_APP_CONTENT / DEFAULT_BACKGROUND_ONLY / NO_ROOT / PARTIAL_MARGINAL / WHITE_BLANK honestly.
exit 0, RESUMED, PNG existence, EGL initialization, non-white pixels or process survival are not success.

## 10. CONT-6 EXTERNAL KB
Use current snapshot SHA d717e9c745609fdf3ca11eb5d60649910089c9e2ca1d2ad942c22f4712ad7931.
Counts: 5,976 total; 5,434 VERIFIED-NEW; 274 VERIFIED-EXISTING; 266 PARTIAL-EXISTING; 2 REJECTED.
Do not treat VERIFIED-NEW as runtime proof. Do not import thousands of rows into root_registry.
Use: external KB → semantic cluster → current-head overlap → runtime reachability → first divergence → generic law → real APK fan-out → 3-run regression → registry only after proof.

## 11. SOURCE-FIRST / REUSE-FIRST
For every root: SOURCE → ALGORITHM → ANDROID LAW → MINIANDROID DIVERGENCE → smallest generic fix → synthetic positive/negative → real APK → independent second APK/family → 3 runs → regression.
Consult AOSP/AndroidX/Compose/libcore/ART and relevant open-source runtime/emulator projects before implementing.

## 12. NO DUPLICATE ROOTS
Before every new root: search root_registry, canonical registry, master worklist and evidence history.
Classify A existing / B same root-new evidence / C missing sub-law / D genuinely new generic root / E environment / F future-out-of-scope / X duplicate-invalid.
Only C/D become runtime root work.

## 13. REQUIRED MATRIX
Create one compact matrix:
APK | TYPE | ABI | SCOPE | PREFLIGHT | INSTALL | LAUNCH | FIRST DIVERGENCE | FRAME VERDICT | L-LEVEL | 3-RUN | STATUS.
Include existing goldens, known failures, all new APKs, at least two Compose apps, two games, two general apps, one native x86/x86_64 app and one pure-DEX control.

## 14. REQUIRED DELIVERABLES
Update only compact canonical artifacts: current-head reconciliation; golden ABI census; new APK acquisition/provenance matrix; execution matrix; Compose/R8 investigation; first-divergence ledger; root cross-match; Skill compliance record; worklog; Issue completion ledger.
Do not flood the repository with raw logs. Use bounded evidence directories plus compact manifests.

## 15. REGRESSION
After every generic fix: focused synthetic → affected APK → independent APK → random app → random game → user goldens → determinism anchors → negatives → reinstall/uninstall → battery → Skill self-test.

## FINAL COMPLETION LEDGER
HEAD / FINAL BINARY SHA / SKILL VERSION / SKILL SELFTEST / LAW-001 GATE / BASELINE.
ABI census: PURE_DEX / X86 / X86_64 / MIXED / ABI_OUT_OF_SCOPE / UNKNOWN.
For every golden: APP / APK SHA / ABI / LAW-001 / RESULT / EVIDENCE.
For every new APK: APP / VERSION / SHA / SOURCE / ABI / SCOPE / RESULT / FIRST DIVERGENCE / FRAME VERDICT / L-LEVEL / 3-RUN.
Compose/R8: successful control / failing control / R8 evidence / exact lookup failure / first divergence / generic law / synthetic proof / A-B / second APK / regression.
Root accounting: existing reused / C / D / environment / duplicates / research-only / blocked / partial / unproven.
Fan-out: games improved / apps improved / Compose apps improved / native x86/x86_64 exercised / pure-DEX exercised / regressions.
Agent Skill: manifest / self-test / LAW-001 integration / safe-stop-resume / machine-readable evidence / CLI drift.
List every unresolved limitation. Never say complete while anything is PARTIAL/BLOCKED/UNPROVEN.

## DEFINITION OF DONE
LAW-001 first gate is regression-proven; current GitHub state reconciled; golden ABI classifications proven from actual APKs; multiple independent x86/x86_64/pure-DEX apps and games executed; at least two independent Compose APKs compared; R8/class-identity hypothesis causally tested; current white/black/partial roots receive first-divergence analysis; external KB used as searchlight; Agent Skill actually used; no app-specific workaround; real APK evidence has provenance and 3-run proof where applicable; regressions clean; every limitation explicitly classified.
Never confuse source evidence with runtime evidence, package/title identity, or different APK artifacts.

issues.body:
# CONT-6 — External Root Knowledge Base Forensic Audit + Runtime Fan-out Validation

## Canonical external knowledge snapshot

The latest supplied archive has now been independently inspected.

**Archive:** `MiniAndroid_Root_Audit_Archive (1).zip`  
**Archive SHA-256:** `d717e9c745609fdf3ca11eb5d60649910089c9e2ca1d2ad942c22f4712ad7931`  
**Archive size:** 2,171,810 bytes  
**Audit date:** 2026-10-05  
**Audited MiniAndroid HEAD inside archive:** `f8d4088b9384b603ce5a903eefe037412eb104d3`  
**Current project HEAD at CONT-6 creation:** `1c2ccdfd24957cef8affc4989dd439ccb30d7276`

### The latest archive DOES contain the claimed 5,434/5,976 dataset

Independent count of `download/MiniAndroid_Root_Knowledge_Base.jsonl`:

- **5,976 total records**
- **5,434 VERIFIED-NEW**
- **274 VERIFIED-EXISTING**
- **266 PARTIAL-EXISTING**
- **2 REJECTED**
- **40 domain JSONL files**
- **5,976 unique IDs**
- 250 VERIFIED-NEW entries have empty `test_apks`
- all rows are source/audit knowledge records; the `VERIFIED-NEW` label must NOT be interpreted as real-APK runtime proof
- `head` is empty in the JSONL rows; use the archive INDEX/report's audited HEAD `f8d4088b...` as snapshot provenance
- the archive's own human report states that existing registry roots were catalogued rather than independently re-verified in this audit.

The archive is therefore a legitimate and useful **external discovery database**, but it is NOT a ready-made 5,434-item runtime worklist.

## CRITICAL ARTIFACT ACCESS CONTRACT

Do NOT paste the 6.5 MB JSONL into this Issue.

The full archive must remain available to the coder as a separate artifact. Use this priority order:

1. **Preferred permanent location:** a dedicated repository research-data path, NOT `root_registry.json`, e.g.
   `research/external-root-kb/current/MiniAndroid_Root_Audit_Archive.zip`
   plus a small `MANIFEST.md` containing archive SHA-256, audit HEAD, record counts, and update date.
2. **If repository binary/data publication is not yet available:** attach the exact ZIP to this Issue as a GitHub issue attachment and record its SHA-256 here.
3. Never copy the full JSONL into the Issue body.
4. Never merge these 5,434 findings into the runtime root registry merely because they exist in the KB.
5. Future snapshots replace/update only the external KB artifact and manifest; the Issue remains the stable audit contract.
6. Keep old snapshot hashes in a tiny history table so a later KB can always be compared against the previous one.

### Future snapshot protocol

For every new archive:

`new archive -> SHA256 -> record counts -> compare IDs -> compare semantic clusters -> compare current HEAD -> runtime validation -> only then promote selected roots`

The coder MUST print the exact snapshot SHA it consumed at the beginning of every CONT-6 run.

## REQUIRED WORKFLOW

### Phase 0 — snapshot and current HEAD

1. Read the external KB artifact directly.
2. Verify archive SHA-256.
3. Verify current main HEAD.
4. Verify the archive's audited HEAD.
5. Record stale-vs-current findings.
6. Do not modify `root_registry.json` in the ingestion phase.

### Phase 1 — forensic reconciliation

Classify every external candidate:

- **A** = already covered by current registry
- **B** = same root, additional evidence
- **C** = existing semantic root but missing sub-law
- **D** = genuinely new generic runtime/platform root
- **E** = environment/prerequisite
- **F** = source-only/reference/future/out-of-scope
- **X** = duplicate/invalid/over-split/malformed

Mandatory:
- exact ID uniqueness
- semantic duplicates
- original/source collisions
- current registry overlap
- already-fixed-at-current-HEAD findings
- stale source references
- source-only vs runtime-proven distinction
- environment findings incorrectly counted as runtime roots.

Do NOT create 5,434 registry entries.

### Phase 2 — semantic clustering

Collapse API/method-level observations into semantic laws.

Explicitly cluster:
- Intent/Activity/Service/lifecycle families
- Collections/ArrayList/Map/Iterator families
- JNI slot families
- View/ViewGroup families
- Compose/Material3 families
- WebView families
- reflection families
- NIO/security/crypto families
- Kotlin/coroutines families
- media/camera families
- libGDX/game-engine families.

For each cluster:
- raw findings
- distinct semantic laws
- current coverage
- fan-out estimate
- best real APK consumers
- highest-confidence candidate root.

Raw row count MUST NOT be reported as independent root-cause count.

## Phase 3 — highest-ROI runtime validation

Select approximately 20 high-confidence semantic clusters, not thousands of rows.

Selection priority:
1. current white/black/partial frontiers
2. games
3. general apps
4. high fan-out
5. strongest source evidence
6. independent consumer diversity.

Use approximately 10–20 real APK consumers total, including at least:
- 3 games
- 3 non-game apps
- one previously white/partial title
- one known-good regression control.

## Phase 4 — six-game claim validation

The external audit claims these six built-in games reached REAL_APP_CONTENT:

- 2048
- mini-tetris
- minicraft
- snake-deluxe
- snake-neon
- tictactoe-deluxe

Validate independently at current HEAD where possible.

For every title record:
- exact APK SHA
- build provenance
- install identity
- ViewTree
- draw operations
- app-owned content provenance
- pixel metrics
- screenshot SHA
- state/input evidence where applicable
- 3 clean runs
- first divergence if not successful.

Non-white pixels alone are NOT sufficient. A fixture/background/harness surface is not REAL_APP_CONTENT.

The archive's six-game result is a valuable hypothesis and acceptance candidate, not a current-HEAD fact until re-run.

## Phase 5 — generic law and fan-out

For each confirmed law:

`source -> law -> current divergence -> first runtime divergence -> generic fix/non-fix -> real APK -> 3 runs -> independent consumer -> fan-out`

Measure:
- titles improved
- games improved
- apps improved
- visual/state/lifecycle/storage/media/native effect
- regressions.

Do not claim “5,434 roots fixed”.

## Phase 6 — registry promotion

Only **C/D** candidates can enter the normal registry.

Before adding anything:
- full registry search
- evidence-history search
- current HEAD check
- semantic duplicate check
- external provenance attached
- runtime proof attached separately.

The external KB remains a discovery/source artifact.

## Required final table

| Metric | Count |
|---|---:|
| External raw records | |
| VERIFIED-NEW source findings | |
| Existing | |
| REJECTED | |
| Semantic clusters | |
| A existing | |
| B evidence-only | |
| C missing sub-law | |
| D genuinely new | |
| E environment | |
| F source/future/out-of-scope | |
| X duplicate/over-split/invalid | |
| Runtime-proven new roots | |
| Real APK consumers | |
| Independently improved games | |
| Independently improved apps | |
| Regressions | |

Also report:
- top 20 semantic clusters
- strongest 5 runtime proofs
- six-game claim verdict
- current-HEAD overlap
- stale-finding count
- duplicate/over-splitting estimate
- recommendation: **IMPORT / PARTIAL-IMPORT / DISCOVERY-ONLY / REJECT**

## HARD RULES

- No app-specific hacks.
- No package-name conditionals.
- No bulk 5,434-root implementation.
- No registry pollution.
- No source-only -> runtime-proven promotion.
- No RESUMED/exit=0/PNG-only closure.
- Preserve source -> law -> divergence -> runtime -> 3-run evidence discipline.
- The external KB is a continuously growing **searchlight**, not the runtime registry.

## Snapshot history

| Snapshot | SHA-256 | Records | NEW | Audited HEAD |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| 2026-10-05 FINAL v3 | `d717e9c745609fdf3ca11eb5d60649910089c9e2ca1d2ad942c22f4712ad7931` | 5976 | 5434 | `f8d4088b` |

Add one row for every future snapshot. Never delete old hashes.

issues.title: BASE-ANDROID — Complete Android Platform Contract Foundation Audit
issues.body:
# BASE ANDROID FOUNDATION — COMPLETE PLATFORM CONTRACT AUDIT

## PURPOSE
This is a foundation task, broader than #373. Do NOT keep fixing individual white/black/partial APK failures before the Android base contract is complete enough to understand an unknown APK.
Required chain: APK -> package -> install -> identity -> permissions -> sandbox -> storage -> Context -> system services -> Binder/IPC -> components -> lifecycle -> Intent resolution -> resources/configuration -> main thread -> window/View -> graphics/surface -> input -> network -> media -> native/ABI -> persistence -> verification.

## NON-NEGOTIABLE
Do not make apps run by granting every permission, advertising every ABI, returning every feature as supported, returning fake system services, bypassing SecurityException, giving apps root, sharing private storage, bypassing exported/signature checks, swallowing missing-service failures, or pretending unsupported GLES/Vulkan/native execution works.
Capabilities must be honest and machine-readable.

## 1. PLATFORM / DEVICE CONTRACT
Build a machine-readable MiniAndroid environment profile covering API level, VERSION.SDK_INT, VERSION.RELEASE, VERSION_CODES behavior gates, Build.*, device/model/manufacturer/product/board/fingerprint, system properties, locale/language/country, timezone/clock, 12/24-hour settings, display width/height, density/dpi/scaledDensity/fontScale, orientation, smallestWidth/screenWidth/screenHeight, screen-size class, uiMode/night mode, touch/keyboard/navigation configuration, display ID/state, refresh rate and color mode.
Every capability must record ADVERTISED / IMPLEMENTED / TESTED / EXECUTABLE.

## 2. CPU / ABI / NATIVE FOUNDATION
Audit host CPU, executable CPU, 32/64-bit process model, supported and actually executable ABIs, native bridge/translator and version, ELF class/machine/ABI, PT_LOAD alignment/page size, DT_NEEDED dependency closure, JNI registration, native loader, linker namespaces, symbol resolution, nativeLibraryDir, argv/environment semantics and executable permissions.
Never report arm64 as executable unless arm64 code really executes. Unsupported native ABI must become a preflight blocker: ABI_MISMATCH_TRANSLATION_REQUIRED.

## 3. PACKAGE MANAGER / INSTALLATION
Implement/verify packageName, versionCode/versionName, ApplicationInfo, ActivityInfo, ServiceInfo, ReceiverInfo, ProviderInfo, PermissionInfo, signatures/signing identity, sharedUserId, process names, exported/enabled state, directBootAware, launch modes, metadata, intent filters, queries/package visibility, uses-sdk, uses-feature, uses-library, uses-native-library, supports-screens, uses-configuration, sourceDir/publicSourceDir, splitSourceDirs, nativeLibraryDir, dataDir, deviceProtectedDataDir, credentialProtectedDataDir, codeCacheDir, install/update/uninstall state.
Installation must create real package state. APK parsing is not installation. Installation is not execution.

## 4. APK STRUCTURAL PREFLIGHT
Inspect AndroidManifest.xml, classes*.dex, resources.arsc, res/, assets/, lib/, META-INF/, split metadata and native ELF files.
Extract SDK min/target/max API, all components and entry points, exported state and intent filters; native ABIs/libraries/DT_NEEDED/JNI/load paths; resource packages/splits/configurations/densities/languages/overlays/assets/fonts/XML/drawables; and implied requirements such as WebView, SQLite, media, camera, microphone, sensors, network, external storage, foreground services, alarms, notifications, accessibility, overlay, providers, FileProvider/content URIs, dynamic loading, reflection and native loading.
Classify every requirement as REQUIRED / OPTIONAL / CONDITIONAL / IMPLIED / UNKNOWN.

## 5. PERMISSION FOUNDATION
Implement a real permission state machine for normal, dangerous/runtime, signature, signature|privileged, development, installer/system, special-access and AppOps-controlled operations.
Track requested, declared, granted, denied, request-pending, user decision, revocation and API-version semantics.
Every protected operation must follow: caller UID -> package -> declaration -> grant -> AppOps/special access -> user/profile policy -> API policy -> allow/deny/error.
Do not use a universal permission=true.

## 6. PACKAGE / USER / UID / SECURITY IDENTITY
Model package, UID, GID, userId, profile, process, signing identity, shared UID and isolated process identity.
Two packages must not accidentally share private storage, UID, preferences, databases, providers, Context identity, process state or Binder identity.

## 7. FILESYSTEM / STORAGE
Create actual per-package storage, not path strings. At minimum model /data/user/<user>/<package>, /data/user_de/<user>/<package>, files, cache, code_cache, no_backup, databases, shared_prefs, app-specific external files/cache, shared external storage, APK/source paths and nativeLibraryDir.
Test create, exists, open, read, write, append, truncate, rename, delete, mkdir, recursive mkdir, stat, length, timestamps, file descriptors, locking, persistence, restart, reinstall, uninstall cleanup, package isolation, user isolation, path traversal and permission denial.
File.exists() and File.length() must reflect real filesystem state.

## 8. CONTEXT / CONTEXTIMPL
Audit application/package/Activity/Service/display/device Contexts, createPackageContext, createConfigurationContext, createDisplayContext, classloader, Resources, PackageManager, ContentResolver, data/database/shared-preference directories and getSystemService.
Wrong Context identity is a platform root.

## 9. SYSTEM SERVICES
Inventory at minimum ActivityManager, PackageManager, WindowManager, PowerManager, UserManager, PermissionManager, AppOpsManager, StorageManager, ConnectivityManager, AlarmManager, JobScheduler, NotificationManager, ClipboardManager, InputManager, SensorManager, LocationManager, CameraManager, AudioManager, MediaSession, Vibrator, Bluetooth, Wifi, Telephony, DownloadManager, Accessibility, DevicePolicy, Keyguard, Account services, ContentResolver/provider infrastructure and WebView-related services.
For each record SERVICE / API / IDENTITY / PERMISSION / STATE / ERROR MODEL / LIFECYCLE / IPC / IMPLEMENTED / TESTED / REAL APK / MISSING.
Never return fake non-null services just to suppress crashes.

## 10. BINDER / IPC
Audit service lookup, registration where needed, Binder identity, calling UID/PID, clearCallingIdentity/restoreCallingIdentity, Parcel, Parcelable, interface tokens, transactions, callbacks, death recipients, RemoteException, service unavailable and permission checks at the service boundary.

## 11. ACTIVITY / SERVICE / RECEIVER / PROVIDER / PROCESS
Activity: resolve, instantiate, attach, Context, Application, lifecycle, saved state, configuration changes, task/back, launch modes, result delivery.
Service: startService, foreground-service semantics where supported, bindService, ServiceConnection, lifecycle, process association.
Receiver: registration, resolution, delivery, lifecycle/timeout.
Provider: authority, attachInfo, URI resolution, permissions/path permissions, CRUD, openFile/openAssetFile, caller identity and lifecycle.
Process: package-to-process mapping, start, death, restart, multiple processes, importance, cold/warm startup.

## 12. INTENT / RESOLUTION
Implement explicit/implicit intents, action/category, URI/MIME, component/package, flags, extras, ClipData, selectors, filters, priority/default handlers, exported checks, permission checks, package visibility and activity/service/provider/receiver resolution. No app-specific intent routing.

## 13. RESOURCES / CONFIGURATION
Treat resources.arsc, AssetManager, asset paths, resource IDs/packages, split resource composition, overlays/RRO/idmap, locale, density, orientation, smallest width, screen size, night mode, API/version qualifiers, styles/themes, attributes, TypedArray, strings, arrays, dimensions, colors, ColorStateList, drawable/mipmap/raw, XML, fonts, NinePatch, vector, animated drawable and fallback/default resources as base platform infrastructure.
Resource selection must be deterministic and configuration-aware.

## 14. MAIN THREAD / SCHEDULING
Audit Looper, MessageQueue, Handler, HandlerThread, Runnable, delayed messages, main-thread identity, Executor, synchronization, Choreographer, frame callbacks, traversal scheduling, vsync abstraction, lifecycle ordering and reentrancy. No arbitrary sleep-based compatibility fixes.

## 15. WINDOW / VIEW / INPUT FOUNDATION
Core chain: Activity -> Window -> WindowManager -> WindowManagerGlobal -> ViewRootImpl -> DecorView -> ViewTree -> measure -> layout -> draw -> Surface.
Audit addView/removeView, ViewRoot attachment, DecorView ownership, requestLayout, invalidate, traversal, measure/layout/draw, dirty propagation, focus, touch/key dispatch, MotionEvent, pointer IDs, coordinate transforms, insets, system bars, window flags, visibility, alpha, clipping, matrix, elevation, z-order and hardware/software layers.
ViewTree existence is not visual success.

## 16. GRAPHICS / SURFACE / PRESENTATION
Audit View/Canvas/RenderNode -> Surface -> BufferQueue -> gralloc/backend -> SurfaceFlinger/compositor -> display -> capture.
Include Surface, SurfaceHolder, SurfaceView, GLSurfaceView, SurfaceTexture, TextureView, EGL, GLES, Vulkan, ANativeWindow, framebuffer, viewport, shader compile/link, texture upload/binding, swap, presentation, buffer format/size/usage flags, fences, back-pressure, surface generation/replacement, BLAST/transactions, HWC, composition, colorspace, alpha and secure/protected surfaces.
Track DRAWN -> BUFFER_QUEUED -> BUFFER_ACQUIRED -> COMPOSITED -> PRESENTED -> CAPTURED.
Do not equate EGL initialization with visible output.

## 17. INPUT / DEVICE FEATURES
Model touchscreen, mouse, keyboard, DPAD, gamepad, stylus, pointer capture, focus, key repeat, sensors, vibrator, device IDs and display IDs. Feature reporting must match actual capability.

## 18. NETWORK
Audit network, loopback, DNS, IPv4/IPv6, sockets, TLS, proxy, cleartext policy, connectivity callbacks, network capabilities, identity, permissions, offline behavior and timeout/error semantics. Do not fake network success.

## 19. MEDIA / AUDIO
Audit MediaPlayer, MediaCodec, MediaExtractor, MediaMetadataRetriever, AudioTrack, AudioRecord, AudioManager, MediaSession, audio focus, volume, codecs, MIME/container, sample formats, YUV/RGB, video Surface, synchronization and surface recreation.

## 20. HARDWARE / SENSOR CAPABILITIES
Inventory camera, microphone, location/GPS, accelerometer, gyroscope, magnetometer, proximity, light, pressure, temperature, step detector/counter, Bluetooth, Wi-Fi, NFC, USB, biometrics, telephony and vibration.
Each capability must be DECLARED / AVAILABLE / PERMITTED / FUNCTIONAL / OPTIONAL.

## 21. SYSTEM PROPERTIES / BUILD CONTRACT
Audit Build.*, VERSION.*, SUPPORTED_ABIS, CPU_ABI, device/model/manufacturer, graphics properties, GLES version/extensions, Vulkan properties, display properties, locale/timezone, API behavior flags and feature flags.
No false capability advertisement.

## 22. UNIFIED APK PRE-FLIGHT
Create one machine-readable prerequisite report covering PACKAGE, INSTALL, SDK/API, ABI, NATIVE, DEX, RESOURCES, FEATURES, PERMISSIONS, SYSTEM SERVICES, STORAGE, NETWORK, GRAPHICS, MEDIA, INPUT, CONFIGURATION, SECURITY and EXTERNAL DEPENDENCIES.
Each requirement is REQUIRED / OPTIONAL / CONDITIONAL / IMPLIED / UNKNOWN and compared against AVAILABLE / PARTIAL / MISSING / INCOMPATIBLE / NOT_TESTED.
Required JSON fields: package, sdk, components, permissions, special_access, features, abi, native, resources, splits, system_services, storage, network, graphics, media, input, configuration, security, environment, mismatches, blockers, verdict, first_divergence, execution_level.

## 23. PRE-FLIGHT MUST PRECEDE LAUNCH
For every unknown APK: inspect APK -> identify package -> inspect manifest -> inspect DEX -> inspect native -> inspect resources/assets -> inspect splits -> derive requirements -> inspect MiniAndroid environment -> compare -> classify blockers -> select execution mode -> install -> launch -> trace -> find first divergence -> classify environment/platform/runtime cause.
This is required for the Agent Skill too.

## 24. WHITE / BLACK / PARTIAL RECLASSIFICATION
Reclassify historical cases into ENVIRONMENT_MISMATCH, ABI_NATIVE, API_PLATFORM_CONTRACT, PACKAGE_INSTALL, PERMISSION_SECURITY, IDENTITY_SANDBOX, SYSTEM_SERVICE_IPC, RESOURCE_CONFIGURATION, COMPONENT_LIFECYCLE, VIEW_WINDOW, GRAPHICS_SURFACE, BUFFER_COMPOSITION, PRESENTATION, MEDIA, NETWORK, INPUT, CAPTURE_ONLY, ORDINARY_RUNTIME_ROOT or UNKNOWN.
Only genuine runtime roots remain in the ordinary root pipeline.

## 25. ROOT REGISTRY CROSS-MATCH
Before creating a root: A=already covered, B=same root/new evidence, C=existing root/missing sub-law, D=genuinely new platform root, E=environment prerequisite, F=future/out-of-scope.
Only C/D create new runtime-root work. E belongs to the foundation/environment matrix.

## 26. NEGATIVE SECURITY TESTS
Prove that MiniAndroid does NOT over-grant: denied permission, missing permission, signature mismatch, private storage access, cross-package file access, wrong UID, wrong user, unexported component, provider without permission, missing feature, unsupported ABI, missing native library, unavailable service, unavailable graphics feature, unavailable camera/microphone, unavailable network, unsupported API and incomplete split APK.
Failures must be deterministic and semantically honest.

## 27. REAL APK VALIDATION
Use independent families: pure DEX app; resource-heavy app; storage/database app; WebView app; ARM-native app; libGDX/game; media app; permission-heavy app; multi-component app; Telegram-class complex app; one random corpus app; one random corpus game.
Do not validate the foundation only against already-working apps.

## 28. EVIDENCE
Every foundation law requires STATUS, SOURCE, ANDROID LAW, IMPLEMENTATION, SYNTHETIC PROBE, REAL APK, FIRST DIVERGENCE, RUNTIME TRACE, ACTUAL STATE CHANGE, SCREENSHOT/PROVENANCE where visual, 3-RUN RESULT, REGRESSION RESULT and COMMIT.
Insufficient: exit code, APK parsed, PNG exists, process alive, EGL initialized, ViewTree exists or coder statement.

## 29. REQUIRED FINAL OUTPUT

## 30. DEFINITION OF DONE
An unknown APK must be processable as: UNDERSTAND -> PREFLIGHT -> INSTALL -> IDENTITY -> PERMISSION -> SANDBOX -> SERVICES -> COMPONENTS -> LIFECYCLE -> RESOURCES -> EXECUTION -> RENDERING -> INPUT -> STATE -> PERSISTENCE -> REPEATABLE VERIFICATION.

This is the Android foundation required before broad compatibility claims.
